statements.label: On the matrix-completion basis M = {e_i etilde_j^T} the Hessian H(pi;Theta_*) = diag(pi(i,j) mu-dot_{ij}) is diagonal, so Definition 3.1 of arXiv:2506.03074v5 collapses to GL(pi;c) = max( max_i sum_j c_{ij}/pi_{ij} , max_j sum_i c_{ij}/pi_{ij} ) with c_{ij} := mu-dot((Theta_*)_{ij})^{-1} > 0 -- the larger of the largest row sum and the largest column sum of the matrix c/pi. Every other row of this family is a statement about that collapsed objective

Weak duality for the collapsed GL-Design objective on the matrix-completion basis, for all d1, d2 >= 1 and all c > 0: for every design pi with all row and column sums of c/pi at most t, all alpha in R^{d1}, beta in R^{d2} with alpha, beta >= 0, and all s >= 0 with s_{ij}^2 = (alpha_i + beta_j) c_{ij}, one has (sum_{ij} s_{ij})^2 <= (sum_i alpha_i + sum_j beta_j) * t; equivalently GL_min(M;c) >= (sum_{ij} sqrt((alpha_i+beta_j) c_{ij}))^2 / (sum alpha + sum beta)

Strong duality at a certified dual point, for all d1, d2 >= 1: given alpha, beta >= 0 with alpha_i + beta_j > 0 everywhere and s > 0 with (alpha_i + beta_j) c_{ij} = s_{ij}^2, put S = sum_{ij} s_{ij} and A = sum alpha + sum beta. If sum_j s_{ij}/(alpha_i+beta_j) <= S/A for every i and sum_i s_{ij}/(alpha_i+beta_j) <= S/A for every j, then GL_min(M;c) = S^2/A exactly, attained at the design pi*_{ij} = s_{ij}/S

The bound of Proposition 3.2(iii) of arXiv:2506.03074v5 is EXACTLY the GL value of the design its own proof uses: for every c > 0 and all d1, d2 >= 1, the inverse-curvature-proportional (E-optimal) design pi_E(i,j) = c_{ij}/sum_{kl} c_{kl} of Appendix E.1 has every row sum of c/pi_E equal to d2 sum_{ij} c_{ij} and every column sum equal to d1 sum_{ij} c_{ij}, hence GL(pi_E; c) = (d1 v d2) sum_{ij} c_{ij} = Harm(Theta_*)^{-1} d1 d2 (d1 v d2)
Universal lower bound on the optimal GL-design of the matrix-completion basis: GL_min(M;c) >= sum_{ij} c_{ij} for every c > 0 and all d1, d2 >= 1

The bracket: sum_{ij} c_{ij} <= GL_min(M;c) <= (d1 v d2) sum_{ij} c_{ij} for every c > 0 and all d1, d2 >= 1. Equivalently, the bound of Proposition 3.2(iii) of arXiv:2506.03074v5 overshoots the true optimal GL-design value by a factor of at most d1 v d2, uniformly in the curvature -- and by GDC3 that factor is exactly the suboptimality of the E-optimal design its own proof uses

GL_min(M; [[1,1],[1,7]]) = 18 exactly, attained at the design pi* = (1/12, 1/6, 1/6, 7/12), against the bound 2 * (1+1+1+7) = 20 printed by Proposition 3.2(iii); the E-optimal design of Appendix E.1 achieves exactly 20, so it is strictly suboptimal here by the factor 10/9

The d1 v d2 ceiling of GDC5 is sharp at d1 = d2 = 2: for every real k >= 1, GL_min(M; [[1,1],[1,2k^2-1]]) = 2(k+1)^2 exactly, attained at pi* = (1, k, k, 2k^2-1)/(2k^2+2k), while Proposition 3.2(iii) prints 2 * (2k^2+2) = 4k^2+4; the ratio 2(k^2+1)/(k+1)^2 increases to 2 = d1 v d2

Proposition 3.2(iii) of arXiv:2506.03074v5 is ATTAINED at constant curvature: for c == 1 on d1 x d2 with d1 <= d2, GL_min(M;c) = d1 d2 d2 = (d1 v d2) sum_{ij} c_{ij}, the uniform design (which is the E-optimal design of Appendix E.1 here) being GL-optimal

GL_min(M; [[1,1],[1,100]]) = 103 + 2 sqrt 202 = (sqrt 101 + sqrt 2)^2 = 131.4253408... exactly, against the bound 2 * 103 = 206 printed by Proposition 3.2(iii): the printed bound is loose by the factor 1.56743... at this curvature matrix

Negative controls for the family: (a) nothing below 18 is achievable for c = [[1,1],[1,7]] (refutes a too-small value); (b) 19 is achievable but is not GL_min (refutes a too-large value); (c) the dual point alpha = (1,4), beta = (0,24), s = [[1,5],[2,14]] satisfies (alpha_i + beta_j) c_{ij} = s_{ij}^2 for that c (the four products are 1, 25, 4, 196) and so is a legitimate weak-duality point with value 484/29 = 16.69, yet its row-0 slackness inequality FAILS (6/5 > 22/29) and 484/29 is not GL_min -- the complementary-slackness hypotheses of GDC2 are not vacuous and weak duality alone does not give the value

Conjecture, NOT claimed proved: sup over c > 0 of (d1 v d2) sum_{ij} c_{ij} / GL_min(M;c) = d1 v d2 for every d1, d2. The <= half is GDC5 (proved); the >= half is proved only at d1 = d2 = 2 (GDC7) [superseded 2026-09-08: proved as GDC14 / GDC17; this row stays a MEASUREMENT of the numerical evidence]

GL_min(M;c) as an infimum: GLinf c := sInf {t | some design pi has GL(pi;c) <= t}, which exists for every c > 0 without any attainment hypothesis, agrees with GLmin wherever the least element exists (so 18, 103 + 2 sqrt 202, 2(k+1)^2, d1 d2 d2, 931 and 13312 are all values of it), and satisfies the bracket sum_{ij} c_{ij} <= GLinf c <= (d1 v d2) sum_{ij} c_{ij} for all d1, d2 >= 1

The constant d1 v d2 of the bracket GDC5 is SHARP in every pair of dimensions: sup over c > 0 of (d1 v d2) sum_{ij} c_{ij} / GL_min(M;c) = d1 v d2 for all d1, d2 >= 1 (as an IsLUB statement about the set of overshoot ratios, with GL_min read as the infimum GDC13). [The conclusion that no constant smaller than d1 v d2 can replace it INSIDE Proposition 3.2(iii) is true but is GDC8's (c = 1 attains the bound), not a consequence of this supremum: sup = d1 v d2 says GLinf / sum c -> 1, which is compatible with GLinf <= K sum c for some K < d1 v d2 -- wording corrected 2026-09-08 after referee pass 2] of arXiv:2506.03074v5. The extremal curvature is the spiked one c_11 = 1, c_ij = u^2 elsewhere with the balanced design pi_11 = 1-u, pi_ij = u/N (N = d1 d2 - 1, 0 < u <= 1/N, u < 1), whose GL value is exactly 1/(1-u) + (d1 v d2 - 1) N u against sum c = 1 + N u^2

An exact GL_min in every dimension on a two-parameter rational family: on d x d with d = k+1, alpha = beta = (X/2, 1/2, ..., 1/2), kap := k - (k-1) lam, c = [[X kap^2, ((X+1)/2) lam^2, ...], [((X+1)/2) lam^2, 1, ...], ...], one has GL_min(M;c) = (k + lam)^2 (X + k) EXACTLY and sum_{ij} c_{ij} = X kap^2 + k(X+1) lam^2 + k^2, for every X > 0 and lam > 0 with kap > 0 -- all 2d complementary-slackness inequalities holding with equality at k + lam, with no relation imposed between X and lam. The gap is the polynomial GL_min - sum c = k(k(k-1) + 2k lam (X+1) - (k-1) lam^2 X); on the reciprocal path X = x, lam = y with x y = 1 it collapses to k(k+1)(k+y) and the overshoot ratio is at least d - d^2 y, so for every b < d some rational instance with GL_min ATTAINED overshoots by more than b

Negative controls for the sharpness pull: 3/2 is not the supremum at d1 = d2 = 2 (it is not even an upper bound), 3 is an upper bound there but not the least one, the hypotheses of the spiked family are not vacuous (at d1 = d2 = 2, u = 1/3 -- the extreme allowed by u N <= 1 -- the design (2/3, 1/9, 1/9, 1/9) achieves 5/2), and the exact family pins a single number (GL_min = 18, not 17, at (k,X,lam) = (1,7,1/2))

The lower end of the bracket GDC5 is never attained once d1 d2 >= 2: sum_{ij} c_{ij} < GL_min(M;c) STRICTLY for every c > 0 -- proved through the stronger bound sum_i (sum_j sqrt c_{ij})^2 <= GL_min(M;c) (the intermediate step Core.sum_le_of_achievable discards) plus strict Cauchy-Schwarz for a row with two positive entries, with transposition of the objective covering d2 = 1 <= d1 - 1. Hence every overshoot ratio is strictly below d1 v d2 and the supremum of GDC14 is NOT attained

Controls for GDC17: the hypothesis d1 d2 >= 2 is necessary and not vacuous -- at d1 = d2 = 1 the supremum of the overshoot ratio IS attained (the ratio is 1 = d1 v d2 for every curvature) and sum_{ij} c_{ij} = GL_min(M;c) exactly, so both the strict inequality and the non-attainment fail there

The lower end of the bracket GDC5 IS approached: inf over c > 0 of GL_min(M;c) / sum_{ij} c_{ij} = 1 for every d1, d2 >= 1, as an IsGLB statement about the set of ratios with GL_min read as the infimum GLinf (GDC13). By GDC17 the infimum is not attained once d1 d2 >= 2, so the lower end is approached and never reached; the witnesses are the spiked curvatures of GDC14, whose curvature spread c_max/c_min diverges

A certified gap under a curvature box: if 0 < m <= c_{ij} <= M for all i, j then GL_min(M;c) / sum_{ij} c_{ij} >= 1 + 2 (d1 v d2 - 1) sqrt(mM)/(m+M) = 1 + 2 (d1 v d2 - 1) sqrt(rho)/(1+rho) with rho = M/m -- so the lower end sum c of GDC5 is approached only as the curvature spread diverges, at rate rho^{-1/2}. At m = M the bound is exactly d1 v d2, which GDC8 attains. At d1 = d2 = 2 the bound is EXACT: 1 + 2 sqrt(mM)/(m+M) is the greatest lower bound of the ratio over the box and it is attained (a minimum) at the anti-diagonal curvature c = [[M,m],[m,M]], whose optimum is GL_min(M;c) = 2 (sqrt M + sqrt m)^2 exactly, e.g. GL_min([[4,1],[1,4]]) = 18 against sum c = 10 and the printed bound 20 (ratio 9/5)

The 1-bit matrix completion of Section 5.1 of arXiv:2506.03074v5 always has a bounded curvature spread, hence a gap: the logistic curvature is c(z) = mu-dot(z)^{-1} = (1+e^z)^2/e^z = 4 cosh^2(z/2), so 4 <= c(z) <= c(B) whenever |z| <= B, and GL_min(M;c) / sum_{ij} c_{ij} >= 1 + 2 (d1 v d2 - 1) sqrt(4 c(B)) / (4 + c(B)). At B = ln 4 (entrywise success probabilities in [1/5, 4/5], curvatures in [4, 25/4]) and d1 = d2 = 2 this is 81/41 = 1.97561, so the bound of Proposition 3.2(iii) overshoots the optimal GL-design value by at most 82/81 = 1.0123

Negative controls for GDC20 / GDC21: (a) at m = M the gap bound equals d1 v d2 exactly, which GDC8 attains, so the coefficient 2(d1 v d2 - 1) in front of sqrt(mM)/(m+M) cannot be raised; (b) the anti-diagonal curvature [[4,1],[1,4]] has ratio 9/5, so 2 is not a lower bound of the box ratio set at d1 = d2 = 2, [m,M] = [1,4] (a too-large value refuted); (c) 3/2 IS a lower bound there but is not the greatest one (a too-small value refuted)

GL_min is homogeneous of degree 1 in the curvature: GL_min(M; a c) = a GL_min(M; c) for every a > 0 and all d1, d2 >= 1 (and likewise the achievable set scales). Hence both ends of the bracket GDC5 scale and the overshoot ratio of Proposition 3.2(iii) depends only on the shape of the curvature matrix

An exact integer GL_min at every square size: on d x d with d = t + 2, the curvature with corner (8t^2+8t+1)(2t^2+2t+1)^2 and EVERY other entry (2t+1)^2 has GL_min(M;c) = (2t^2+3t+2)^2 (8t^2+9t+2) exactly, with sum_{ij} c_{ij} = (8t^2+8t+1)(2t^2+2t+1)^2 + (t+1)(t+3)(2t+1)^2. At t = 3 this is the 5 x 5 instance: corner 60625, other entries 49, sum c = 61801, printed bound 5 * 61801 = 309005, GL_min = 84941 (ratio 3.637878); t = 1 and t = 2 are exactly the 3 x 3 and 4 x 4 instances of GDC11 (931 and 13312), and t = 0 is the all-ones 2 x 2 curvature where GL_min = 8 equals the printed bound

Negative controls for GDC24: 84940 and 84942 are both refuted as the value of GL_min of the 5 x 5 instance (a too-small and a too-large value), and scaling that curvature by 1/49 gives GL_min = 84941/49, not 84941 -- so the homogeneity of GDC23 is not vacuous

The exact minimum of GL_min(M;c)/sum_{ij} c_{ij} over a curvature box, in every square dimension, from two new pieces: (i) a second, complementary lower bound of Schweitzer type, GL_min(M;c)/sum c >= 4 (d1 v d2) sqrt(mM)/(sqrt m + sqrt M)^2 for m <= c_{ij} <= M (better than GDC20 at small spread, worse than the trivial bound 1 at large spread); (ii) the diagonal curvature -- M on the diagonal, m off it, on (d+1) x (d+1) -- whose optimum is GL_min = (d+1)(sqrt M + d sqrt m)^2 EXACTLY with sum c = (d+1)(M + d m), certified by the constant dual alpha = beta = (1/2,...,1/2) with all 2(d+1) slackness inequalities tight; (iii) their meeting point M = d^2 m, where min over the box { GL_min(M;c)/sum_{ij} c_{ij} : m <= c_{ij} <= d^2 m } = 4d/(d+1) exactly, attained at that diagonal curvature -- 2 at 2x2 (constant curvature), 8/3 at 3x3 with the box [m,4m], 3 at 4x4 with [m,9m], tending to 4

Controls for GDC26: at 3 x 3 with the box [1,4] the exact minimum is 8/3, so 27/10 is not a lower bound of that box ratio set (a too-large value refuted), and the chord bound is genuinely weaker than GDC20 at large spread -- at d1 = d2 = 2 with [1,100] it prints 80/121 < 1, below the trivial bound of GDC5

The exact optimum of every sqrt-regular curvature: if c > 0 on d x d and every row and every column of the matrix sqrt(c) sums to the same K, then GL_min(M;c) = d K^2 exactly, attained at the design pi* = sqrt(c)/(d K) -- so for such curvatures the optimal GL-design is proportional to sqrt(c), not to c (the E-optimal design of Appendix E.1 that Proposition 3.2(iii) of arXiv:2506.03074v5 uses). It subsumes the constant curvature (K = d sqrt a, GL_min = d^3 a, GDC8), the diagonal curvature of GDC26 (K = sqrt M + (d-1) sqrt m), and every curvature that is M on a p-regular 0/1 pattern and m off it (K = p sqrt M + (d-p) sqrt m)

The exact minimum of GL_min(M;c)/sum_{ij} c_{ij} over a curvature box, for every regularity p: on D x D with D = a+b+2, p = a+1 <= D/2 and the box [m, ((D-p)/p)^2 m], min { GL_min(M;c)/sum c : m <= c_{ij} <= ((D-p)/p)^2 m } = 4 p (D-p)/D exactly, attained at the p-regular cyclic curvature (M on the p cyclic diagonals j - i in {0,...,p-1}, m elsewhere), whose optimum is GL_min = D (p sqrt M + (D-p) sqrt m)^2. Equivalently the chord bound of GDC26 is tight at the discrete spreads rho = ((D-p)/p)^2, p = 1,...,floor(D/2): 8/3 at D = 3 with rho = 4, 3 at D = 4 with rho = 9, 24/5 at D = 5 with rho = 9/4, and the ceiling D at rho = 1 (p = D/2) [corrected 2026-09-09, hygiene 11d: was tight exactly at the discrete spreads -- only tightness AT those spreads is proved; that they are the ONLY such spreads is a hand remark, not formalised]

families.paper_title: The optimal GL-design on the matrix-completion basis:\\ the exact optimum, its duality, and the slack of a bound in GL-LowPopArt
families.paper_abstract: GL-LowPopArt (Lee, Jang, Jun, Vojnovi\'c and Yun, AISTATS 2026) introduces the GL-design objective $\GL(\pi;\Thst)$ for the second stage of its estimator for generalized low-rank trace regression, and its Proposition~3.2 bounds the optimal value on the matrix-completion basis $\Mcal=\{\ve_i\vet_j^{\top}\}$ by $\GLmin(\Mcal)\le\Harm(\Thst)^{-1}d_1d_2(d_1\vee d_2)$, where $\Harm(\Thst)$ is the harmonic mean of the entry-wise curvatures $\dmu((\Thst)_{ij})$; its Appendix~N asks whether such bounds are tight.  On $\Mcal$ the Hessian is diagonal and, with $c_{ij}=\dmu((\Thst)_{ij})^{-1}$, the objective is the larger of the largest row sum and the largest column sum of the matrix $c/\pi$, while the printed bound reads $(d_1\vee d_2)\sum_{ij}c_{ij}$.  We show: (i)~the printed bound is exactly the GL value of the design the paper's own proof uses, the inverse-curvature-proportional (E-optimal) design $\piE\propto c$, for every $c$; (ii)~$\sum c\le\GLmin(\Mcal;c)\le(d_1\vee d_2)\sum c$ for every $c>0$, so the bound overshoots the optimum by a factor of at most $d_1\vee d_2$, that factor being exactly the suboptimality of $\piE$; (iii)~both ends are reached: the upper one at constant curvature, where the uniform design is GL-optimal, and the lower one in the limit, so that $\sup_{c>0}(d_1\vee d_2)\sum c/\GLmin(\Mcal;c)=d_1\vee d_2$ for \emph{every} $d_1,d_2$ --- at $d_1=d_2=2$ along the exact family $\GLmin(\Mcal;\bigl[\begin{smallmatrix}1&1\\1&2k^2-1\end{smallmatrix}\bigr]) =2(k+1)^2$ against the bound $4k^2+4$ for every real $k\ge1$, and in general along a curvature with one dominant cell; (iv)~exact values: $18$ against $20$ for $c=\bigl[\begin{smallmatrix}1&1\\1&7\end{smallmatrix}\bigr]$, $103+2\sqrt{202}=(\sqrt{101}+\sqrt2)^2$ against $206$ for $\bigl[\begin{smallmatrix}1&1\\1&100\end{smallmatrix}\bigr]$, and $931$ against $1491$, $13312$ against $34624$ for a $3\times3$ and a $4\times4$ instance.  The tool is a duality: $\GLmin(\Mcal;c)\ge\bigl(\sum_{ij}\sqrt{(\alpha_i+\beta_j)c_{ij}}\bigr)^2/(\sum\alpha+\sum\beta)$ for all $\alpha,\beta\ge0$ (Cauchy--Schwarz), with equality certified by an explicit design whenever $d_1+d_2$ complementary-slackness inequalities hold; every exact value above is such a finite certificate.  No statement of the source is contradicted: its bound is correct and is an identity for its own design.  What is added is the exact optimum and the size of the gap, which answers the question of its Appendix~N for the arm set $\Mcal$: the bound is not tight, it is loose by at most $d_1\vee d_2$, it is an equality exactly when the inverse-curvature design is GL-optimal, and no constant smaller than $d_1\vee d_2$ will do, in any dimensions.  Exact rational instances at $d=3,4,5$ accompany the last statement. Every theorem about the row-and-column-sum objective displayed above is checked in Lean~4 with Mathlib except the sharpness statement in general dimensions, whose $d_1=d_2=2$ case is formalized and whose general case is an elementary hand proof; the collapse of the source's Definition~3.1 onto that objective is itself a hand derivation about diagonal matrices.  Both are labelled as such wherever they are used. \par\smallskip\noindent\emph{Added in version~2.}  The sharpness statement is now machine-checked in every pair of dimensions, and the two ``is it attained?'' questions about the bracket are settled.  With $\GLmin(\Mcal;c)$ read as the infimum $\GLinf(c)$ of the achievable values --- which agrees with the minimum wherever a minimizer is certified --- the set of overshoot ratios $\{(d_1\vee d_2)\sum c/\GLinf(c):c>0\}$ has least upper bound exactly $d_1\vee d_2$ for every $d_1,d_2\ge1$, the supremum being approached along the spiked curvatures $c_{11}=1$, $c_{ij}=u^2$ with $u=1/M$ for an $M$ the proof writes down; for $d_1d_2\ge2$ one has $\sum c<\GLmin(\Mcal;c)$ strictly for every $c>0$, so the lower end of the bracket is never attained and neither is that supremum, whereas at $d_1=d_2=1$ both are; and on the $d\times d$ basis, $d=k+1$, the two-parameter rational family with $c_{11}=X\kappa^2$, $c_{1j}=c_{i1}=\tfrac{X+1}2\lambda^2$ and $c_{ij}=1$ otherwise, $\kappa=k-(k-1)\lambda>0$, has $\GLmin(\Mcal;c)=(k+\lambda)^2(X+k)$ exactly, all $2d$ complementary-slackness inequalities holding with equality; it contains the $2\times2$ instances above, and the $3\times3$ and $4\times4$ ones after a scaling, and along $X\lambda=1$ it approaches the supremum with the optimum attained and rational.  Every numbered statement of the new section is checked in Lean~4 with Mathlib on the same three axioms, the scalings and one equality being hand steps flagged where they occur; everything stated in version~1 is kept unchanged. \par\smallskip\noindent{\sloppy\emph{Added in version~3.}  The lower end of the bracket is examined.  It is approached, $\inf_{c>0}\GLmin(\Mcal;c)/\sum c=1$ in every pair of dimensions (the reciprocal of the sharpness statement), but only along curvatures of diverging spread: under a box $0<m\le c_{ij}\le M$, $\GLmin(\Mcal;c)/\sum c\ge1+2(d_1\vee d_2-1)\sqrt{mM}/(m+M)$, which is exactly the minimum at $d_1=d_2=2$, attained at $\bigl[\begin{smallmatrix}M&m\\m&M\end{smallmatrix}\bigr]$ with optimum $2(\sqrt M+\sqrt m)^2$.  For the 1-bit matrix completion of the source's Section~5.1 the logistic curvature $(1+e^z)^2/e^z$ lies in $[4,c(B)]$ when $|(\Thst)_{ij}|\le B$, which that section assumes, so its bound is near-tight there for a small such $B$: at $B=\ln4$ and $d_1=d_2=2$ it overshoots the optimum by at most $82/81$ --- the slack of Proposition~3.2(iii) is a curvature-spread phenomenon.  A complementary bound of Schweitzer type, $4(d_1\vee d_2)\sqrt{mM}/(\sqrt m+\sqrt M)^2$, is attained by the $p$-regular cyclic curvatures, $1\le p\le D/2$, and gives the exact minimum $4p(D-p)/D$ of $\GLmin/\sum c$ over the box $[m,((D-p)/p)^2m]$ on $D\times D$; behind it, $\GLmin(\Mcal;c)=dK^2$ whenever $\sqrt c$ has constant row and column sums $K$, at $\pi^*\propto\sqrt c$ rather than $\propto c$.  Homogeneity puts the exact family of version~2 into integer form, with $\GLmin=84941$ against the bound $309005$ on $5\times5$.  The ingredients (Kantorovich--P\'olya--Szeg\H{o}, Schweitzer, Neyman) are classical and named as such; every numbered statement of the new section is checked in Lean~4 with Mathlib on the same three axioms, and versions~1 and~2 are kept unchanged.\par}

families.title: Reachable states and Gardens of Eden of Conway's Life on an n x n patch
families.description: **Source.** arXiv:2604.14966v1, Attila Egri-Nagy and Chrystopher L. Nehaniv, *Measuring the Computational Power of Finite Patches of Cellular Automata* (nlin.CG primary, cs.FL cross-list, v1 only, submitted 16 Apr 2026, 6 pages, MSC 20M20 / 20M35). The paper converts a small patch of Conway's Game of Life into a transformation semigroup and decomposes it. Everything quoted below was read off the **compiled e-print** (`tectonic gol-decomp.tex`, PDF p. 4), not off the raw LaTeX.
families.paper_title: Reachable states and Gardens of Eden of Conway's Life\\ on an $n\times n$ patch
families.paper_abstract: Fix $n\ge1$ and let $\Phi_n$ be the one-step map of Conway's Game of Life (rule B3/S23) on the $2^{n^2}$ global states of an $n\times n$ patch, under either of the two boundary conventions of Egri-Nagy and Nehaniv (arXiv:2604.14966): the \emph{finite} patch, whose exterior is permanently dead, and the \emph{toroidal} patch, whose indices are read modulo $n$.  A state is \emph{reachable} when it lies in the image of $\Phi_n$ and a \emph{Garden of Eden} otherwise. Those authors print the complete $4\times4$ census---$17879$ reachable toroidal states, $11659$ reachable finite states, and the index/period pairs $(9,8)$ and $(14,6)$ of $\Phi_4$ in the full transformation monoid---as the input to a semigroup decomposition, and stop there.  We certify every one of those numbers by exhaustive computation checked in the Lean~4 kernel, and add the two quantities the census leaves out at $4\times4$: the second iterate has image of size $7725$ (toroidal) and $4452$ (finite), so one further tick discards a further $57\ of the reachable set, and the patch has exactly $53$ (toroidal) and $158$ (finite) still lifes. The proofs rest on a linear-time image certificate (a witness array checked by three sweeps) whose soundness is proved by ordinary induction, so that the kernel replays the mathematics and evaluates only a Boolean.  We also report, as replayable data outside the formal development, the complete $5\times5$ census for both boundaries ($8\,520\,996$ and $3\,356\,562$ reachable states out of $2^{25}$; $3456$ and $725$ still lifes; index/period $(51,60)$ and $(38,24)$), and we pin the boundary conventions against the source's own $2\times2$ remark.  No reachable-state or Garden-of-Eden census of a Life patch appears in the OEIS or in the Garden-of-Eden literature, which works on the infinite plane where no Garden of Eden fits in a $5\times5$ box at all.  The one published quantity that overlaps---Vidunas and Vaicekauskas's $17$ ``stabilised patterns'' of the $4\times4$ torus---is recovered exactly by reducing our cycle data modulo the order-$128$ symmetry group.

families.title: Good involutions of linear quandles: the closing conjecture of arXiv:2508.16772 (|Good Lambda_{4n,2n-1}| = 10 for odd n), and a closed count for the coprime case
families.description: Source: **arXiv:2508.16772v1**, Luc Ta, *Good involutions of twisted conjugation subquandles and Alexander quandles* (22 Aug 2025; live categories math.GT, math.GR, math.QA; the arXiv API reports v1 as the only version; published as *Communications in Algebra*, DOI 10.1080/00927872.2026.2643415, online 2026-04-30 — that version is paywalled and was not read). Read from the live e-print (`curl -sSL https://arxiv.org/e-print/2508.16772v1 | tar xz`, toplevel `main.tex` per `00README.json`).

statements.label: Conjecture 5.13 of arXiv:2508.16772v1 proved for EVERY odd n (not only the n = 3, 5, 7 the author's GAP program reached): |Good L_{4n,2n-1}| = 10, with the instances n = 9 (L_{36,17}) and n = 41 (L_{164,81}) spelled out
The source's Remark 5.14 proved from the family's own reduction: for n EVEN, |Good L_{4n,2n-1}| = 4, so the odd hypothesis in Conjecture 5.13 is load-bearing and not decoration

Twenty-seven rows of the source's Table 1 recomputed in Lean: the 26 rows whose reduction parameter g = gcd(N,k-1) is at most 5 (including (8,5) = 36, (15,11) = 26, (24,5) = 36 and part of the dihedral column (label corrected 2026-08-28: N = 7,17,18,19,22,23,25,26,27 have no theorem in Linear.lean; N = 3,4,5 sit under GI-G; true coverage 30 of 47 Table-1 entries)), plus the row (21,8) = 232 reached by counting involutions inside S_7 instead (coverage updated 2026-08-29: 31 of 47 after GI-6 landed (24,17) = 764)

A closed identification the source does not state (its Proposition 5.9 is the g <= 2 sub-case; g >= 3 is new): whenever k^2 = 1 in Z/N, g = gcd(N,k-1) and gcd(N/g, g) = 1, the good involutions of L_{N,k} are in explicit bijection with the involutions of a g-element set, so |Good L_{N,k}| = A000085(g). This is where the conjecture's 10 = A000085(4) comes from, and it reaches the Table 1 rows (21,8) and (24,17) that a g^g decision cannot

The reduction: for N = g*m with k^2 = 1 in Z/N and the ideal (k-1) equal to the ideal (g), the good involutions of L_{N,k} are in explicit bijection with the maps D : Z/g -> Z/g satisfying D(u) + D(u + m*D(u)) = 0 -- a problem g symbols wide, independent of N

The encoding gate: |Good L_{N,k}| computed for N <= 5 by testing ALL N^N functions Z/N -> Z/N against the three axioms, with no structural assumption -- Table 1 rows (3,-1) = 1, (4,-1) = 4, (5,-1) = 1, and on the trivial quandles L_{4,1} = 10 and L_{5,1} = 26

The linear quandle really is a quandle: s_x(x) = x, the self-distributive law s_x s_y = s_{s_x(y)} s_x, bijectivity of every s_y when k is a unit, and the identity is a good involution whenever k^2 = 1

Negative controls: the claim |Good L_{N,k}| <= 10 is refuted (L_{8,5} has 36), the claim |Good L_{N,k}| >= 1 is refuted (L_{5,2} has none, by full 5^5 enumeration), and each hypothesis of the reduction is shown non-vacuous -- k^2 = 1 fails at (16,5) where the reduced count would be 16, the ideal condition (k-1)*a = g fails at (8,5) with g = 2 where the wrong count would be 4 against the true 36, and gcd(N/g,g) = 1 fails at (16,9) where A000085(8) = 764 against the true 5776 (2026-08-29 dichotomy pull: 8 new control declarations, journal/2026-08-29-good-inv-dichotomy.md sec 6) (2026-08-30 hyper pull: 5 new control declarations, journal/2026-08-30-good-inv-hyper.md sec 6 -- hyper_control_branch_needed, the branch hypothesis is load-bearing: at (24,17), where g = 8 and m = 3 are coprime, the hard-branch right-hand side would read A000898(4)^2 = 5776 against the true 764; hyper_control_two_branches, the dichotomy does not collapse to one formula: at (16,9) the answer is 5776 while A000085(8) = 764; hyper_control_not_le, refuting the too-small claim |Good L_{N,k}| <= 5776, since (28,15) gives 42406144; hyper_control_not_ge, refuting the too-large claim that the hard branch always gives at least 36, since (4,3) gives A000898(1)^2 = 4; and hyper_control_nonvacuous, every hypothesis of the hard branch simultaneously satisfiable at (16,9))

The complete two-case classification of ` | Good Λ_{N,k} | ` for every `N ≥ 1` and every `k : ZMod N`: it is `0` unless `k² = 1`; and with `g = gcd(N,k−1)`, `d = gcd(N/g, g)`, one has `d ∈ {1,2}` and the count is `A000085(g)` when `d = 1` and `A000898(g/2)²` when `d = 2`. Proved in prose in `journal/2026-08-29-good-inv-strategy.md` §2; the `d = 1` half plus the dichotomy are formalized (rows GI-5, GI-6, GI-8), the `d = 2` half is not

Total in `k`, and the hypotheses discharged: `Good Λ_{N,k} ≠ ∅ ⇒ k² = 1` (so the count is 0 for every other `k`, with no hypothesis on `N`); the dichotomy `gcd(N/g, g) ∣ 2` for `g = gcd(N,(k−1).val)` whenever `k² = 1`; and the ideal hypothesis `(k−1) = (g)` of `Reduce.lean`, which every instance in this family previously discharged by `decide`, proved once and for all at `g = gcd` by divisibility and Bézout

`#{F : α → α | F ∘ F = id} = A000085(card α)` for every finite `α`, proved by a localized deletion induction over `Finset`s (the transposition-composition map `F ↦ F ∘ (u₀ v)` is its own inverse, so one `funext` discharges both halves of `Finset.card_nbij'`) — Mathlib has no involution-counting lemma. With it: the family's parked cell ` | Good Λ_{24,17} | = 764`, the row `(21,8) = 232` for free, ` | Good Λ_{4n,2n−1} | = 10` re-derived as `A000085(4)` rather than by a 256-case decision, and ` | Good Λ_{N,1} | = A000085(N)` uniformly in `N`

The last also shows that `4 ∣ N` does not by itself put a cell in the hard branch

The mechanism is that the dichotomy's second branch needs `g` and `N/g` both even, hence `4 ∣ N`; the odd-modulus form is stated separately without the `if`

The neighbouring `(21,8) = 232`, where the search does finish, costs 1 min 47 s at 8.81 GB by search and nothing measurable by proof. Formalization price: 876 Lean lines in two files (223 + 653), ten `lake env lean` invocations of which four ended in errors, 12 min 46 s of module-check wall plus about four minutes of axiom runs, peak RSS never above 7.04 GB against an `import Mathlib` baseline of 3.3–6.6 GB on this box, ≈ 0.3 CPU-hours for the whole dispatch. The strategist's `ZMod.addOrderOf_coe`, `Nat.card_zmultiples` and `Int.gcd_eq_gcd_ab` were never needed: keeping the dichotomy inside `ℕ` (`k² = 1 ⟺ N ∣ a(a+2)` with `a = (k−1).val`, both factors natural) removed the whole `ℤ`/`natAbs` layer and cut that lemma from a priced 40–80 lines to 20

The second branch of the family's dichotomy, closed: when `k^2 = 1` and `gcd(N/g, g) = 2` (equivalently `g` and `N/g` both even), ` | Good L_{N,k} | = A000898(g/2)^2`. The last searches a space of `30^30 ~ 2e44` maps at a modulus four times the largest order the source's GAP program reached

The source's **Theorem 5.11** re-proved from scratch and uniformly in `n`: ` | Good L_{4n,2n+1} | = A000898(n)^2` for every `n >= 1`, which is OEIS A202828(n). The source proves it by an explicit count of involutions with `i` transpositions (its Lemma 5.10); here it is the instance `g = 2n`, `m = 2` of the classification, and the square is the two parity classes of `ZMod 2n`

OEIS A387317 (the source's Table 2) at the moduli divisible by 4 -- the eight terms `a(32) = 1049760008`, `a(36) = 28558296078`, `a(40) = 848580157352`, `a(44) = 27271456395278`, `a(48) = 943132645308616`, `a(52) = 34877026635366414`, `a(56) = 1373536895464662312`, `a(60) = 57351382705526608630` -- together with a closed form at EVERY `N` (no divisibility hypothesis, unlike GI-9). families.paper_title: Good involutions of linear quandles: a conjecture of Ta,\\ and a complete count when $4\nmid N$
families.paper_abstract: For a positive integer $N$ and a unit $k$ of $\ZZ/N$, the \emph{linear quandle} $\Lambda_{N,k}$ is the Alexander quandle of $\ZZ/N$ with $\varphi_k(x)=kx$; it is the dihedral quandle $R_N$ when $k=-1$ and the trivial quandle when $k=1$.  Ta tabulated the number $|\Good\Lambda_{N,k}|$ of good involutions of every nontrivial linear quandle of order at most $29$, all but two entries by a computer search, and closed his paper with the conjecture that $|\Good\Lambda_{4n,2n-1}|=10$ for every odd $n\ge 3$, having confirmed $n=3,5,7$.  We prove that conjecture, for every odd $n\ge 1$.  The proof runs through a reduction which is uniform in $N$: if $k^{2}=1$ and the ideal of $\ZZ/N$ generated by $k-1$ is generated by a divisor $g$ of $N$, then the good involutions of $\Lambda_{N,k}$ correspond bijectively to the maps $D\colon\ZZ/g\to\ZZ/g$ satisfying $D(u)+D(u+cD(u))=0$, where $c\equiv N/g \pmod g$.  For the conjectured family $g=\gcd(4n,2n-2)=4$ for \emph{every} odd $n$, so two searches over $4^{4}$ maps settle every $n$ at once, whereas the search reported in the source is run one order at a time over a space that grows with $n$.  We then determine $|\Good\Lambda_{N,k}|$ for \emph{every} modulus $N$ not divisible by $4$ and every $k$: it is $0$ unless $k^{2}=1$, and otherwise it is the number of involutions of a set with $\gcd(N,k-1)$ elements, the corresponding term of OEIS A000085.  The mechanism is a dichotomy: if $k^{2}=1$ and $g=\gcd(N,k-1)$, then $\gcd(N/g,g)$ divides $2$, and the value $2$ forces $4\mid N$.  Consequences are a closed form for Ta's per-order sums, OEIS A387317, at every such modulus, twenty-three terms of that sequence beyond its published range, and eight individual counts beyond every published table, the largest being $|\Good\Lambda_{48,17}|=46\,206\,736$.  A two-case classification valid for every modulus, whose second case is the square of a term of OEIS A000898, is proved here in the ordinary way; that second case is the one part of the paper that is not machine-checked.  Every other statement below has been verified with a proof assistant, apart from those attributed to the literature and the few marked in the text as computed but unproved.

families.paper_title: The 2-modular adjacency algebra of $\GQ(2,2)$:\\ Wedderburn decomposition, Cartan matrix and Gabriel quiver
families.paper_abstract: Let $\sX$ be the coherent configuration of type $[3,2;3]$ attached to the generalized quadrangle $\GQ(2,2)$ and let $\FF_2\sX$ be its $2$-modular adjacency algebra, an algebra of dimension $10$ over $\FF_2$.  Shimabukuro determined $\dim_{\FF_2}\Rad(\FF_2\sX)=4$ and $\dim_{\FF_2}\Rad(\FF_2\sX)^2=2$ by computer and asked for the Wedderburn decomposition of the semisimple quotient, the dimensions and Loewy series of the projective indecomposables, and the Gabriel quiver.  We settle the first and the third.  The semisimple quotient is $\Mat_2(\FF_2)\times\FF_2\times\FF_2$; the two surviving types allowed by Shimabukuro's own constraints are separated by an idempotent count, $32$ against $16$.  The Gabriel quiver has three vertices, with simple modules of dimensions $1,2,1$, and exactly two arrows, running in both directions between the point-fibre and the block-fibre vertex; the vertex carrying the two-dimensional simple module is isolated.  The Cartan matrix is $\left(\begin{smallmatrix}2&0&1\\0&1&0\\1&0&2\end{smallmatrix}\right)$, so the three projective indecomposables have dimensions $3,2,3$.  We also show $\Rad(\FF_2\sX)^3=0$, which pins the Loewy length at exactly $3$.  All statements are machine-checked in Lean~4.

families.title: How many M-inner-equivalence classes of simple graphs on at most M vertices are there? (Eilers-Restorff-Ruiz-Sorensen arXiv:1604.05439v2, Table 'numberofiioo', the '?' at M = 5)
families.description: The `?` in the atlas table of Eilers–Restorff–Ruiz–Sørensen, *Geometric classification of graph C\*-algebras over finite graphs* (arXiv:1604.05439v2 = Canad. J. Math. **70** (2018) 294–353, doi:10.4153/CJM-2017-016-7), section "Atlas of graph C\*-algebras of small graphs".
families.paper_title: The number of $5$-inner equivalence classes\\ of simple graphs on at most five vertices
families.paper_abstract: Eilers, Restorff, Ruiz and S\o rensen close their geometric classification of graph $C^*$-algebras with an atlas of small graphs.  A \emph{simple graph} there is a finite directed graph with loops allowed and no multiple edges, and two such graphs with at most $M$ vertices are \emph{$M$-inner equivalent} when a chain of five elementary steps --- isomorphism, a legal row addition, a legal column addition, deletion of a regular source, a legal collapse --- joins them without ever leaving the simple graphs on at most $M$ vertices.  Their table records $2,8,35,218$ classes for $M=1,2,3,4$ and a question mark at $M=5$, the accompanying sentence being that at $M=5$ they ``have not attempted a complete analysis''.  We prove that the entry is $2172$.  The proof is a component certificate for the move graph on the $295\,128$ isomorphism classes of simple graphs with at most five vertices: a spanning forest bounds the number of classes above by $2172$, a move-invariant colouring bounds it below by the same number, and the colouring is a complete invariant, so no transversal is shorter and no family of pairwise inequivalent graphs is longer.  The same machinery, run at $M\le 4$, returns the published $2,8,35,218$ exactly, which is the evidence that the five clauses and their legality conditions have been transcribed correctly; and the two legality conditions that an implementation is most likely to drop --- the path condition on the two additions, and the requirement that a collapsed vertex support no loop --- are each shown to be load-bearing by an explicit pair of graphs that dropping it would wrongly merge.  The theorems below are machine-checked in Lean~4, with no \texttt{sorry} and with the compiled evaluator as the only trusted computational step; the few statements that lie outside the formal development are labelled where they occur.  Two structural by-products, computed outside the formal development and labelled as such, are that each of the two vertex-deleting moves is individually redundant at every $M\le 5$ while the two together are not, and that every class contains a graph on exactly $M$ vertices.

statements.label: t(6) = 26: exactly 26 classes of graphs on six vertices under local complementation and vertex permutation, with an explicit 26-element representative list, a certified descent to the representative and back, and pairwise inequivalence

W(6) = t(6) = 26: for graphs G, H on six vertices, any F_2-linear g with w_H(g x) = w_G(x) for all x forces G and H to be local-complementation-plus-permutation equivalent -- the weight function up to GL(6,2) is a complete invariant of 6-qubit graph states

arXiv:1807.09107 Example 5.10 is wrong: its two length-4 self-dual stabilizer codes ARE monomially equivalent -- exactly 32 of the 6^4*4! = 31104 monomial maps carry one onto the other -- although the displayed weight-preserving isometry f is realised by none of them

Controls: the model really computes |supp x union supp Gamma x|; the code/adjacency encoding is a bijection on all 2^15 codes so the generators act on labelled graphs; equivalence is not the total relation; distinct labelled graphs ARE weight-isometric, so the headline's hypothesis is satisfiable; and the search returns true when an isometry exists, so the negative answer is not an artefact of a broken search

E(6) = 23 < 26 = t(6): only 23 distinct weight enumerators occur among the 26 classes at length 6, and the codes 7 and 36 are an explicit inequivalent pair sharing one -- so the weight ENUMERATOR is not a complete invariant where the weight FUNCTION up to GL(6,2) is
No two of the 59 local-complementation-plus-permutation class representatives at length 7 admit an F_2-linear weight isometry; with Danielsen-Parker's t(7) = 59 this is W(7) = 59

Cost of the two certificate shapes: the length-6 classification plus isometry plus 650-ordered-pair search is 92 CPU-s and 1.56 GB of interpreted native_decide over 554 kB of data; the length-7 pair search alone is 168 M depth-first nodes and needs chunking; the length-7 classification certificate is 13 MB and ~2e10 interpreted operations and is parked for a compiled core; n = 12 on the C side is tens of CPU-hours and 5.4 GB and is parked

families.paper_title: Weight isometries of graph states: the weight function up to $\GL(n,2)$ is a complete invariant for $n\le 7$, and a correction to an example of Pllaha
families.paper_abstract: A self-dual additive code over $\FF_4$ of length $n$ is an $n$-qubit stabilizer state, and every such code is equivalent to the graph code $C_G=\{(x,\Gamma_G x):x\in\FF_2^n\}$ of a graph $G$ on $n$ vertices; two graph codes are monomially equivalent --- equivalently, the two states are related by local Clifford operations and a permutation of the qubits --- exactly when the graphs are related by local complementation and vertex permutation.  Pllaha's Problem~6.3 asks how far the symplectic isometries between two self-dual stabilizer codes can exceed the monomial ones, and Gluesing-Luerssen and Pllaha call their single-code form of the question ``wide open''.  We settle the emptiness half of Problem~6.3 at lengths six and seven.  If $G$ and $H$ are graphs on six vertices and some $\FF_2$-linear $g\colon\FF_2^6\to\FF_2^6$ satisfies $\wtf_H(gx)=\wtf_G(x)$ for all $x$ --- no invertibility assumed --- then $G$ and $H$ are related by local complementations and vertex permutations; so the number of classes surviving the coarser weight equivalence is $W(6)=t(6)=26$.  At length seven the same holds for the $59$ class representatives, which is $W(7)=59$ once Danielsen and Parker's $t(7)=59$ is granted.  The weight \emph{enumerator} is strictly weaker at both lengths: only $E(6)=23$ enumerators occur among the $26$ classes, and we exhibit an inequivalent pair sharing one.  We also correct Example~5.10 of Pllaha's e-print arXiv:1807.09107v1: the two length-four codes it displays \emph{are} monomially equivalent --- exactly $32$ of the $6^4\cdot 4!=31\,104$ monomial maps carry one onto the other --- although the displayed isometry between them is realised by none.  Outside the formal development, the same search run in C against Danielsen's orbit database extends the conclusion to $n\le 11$, where $4\,501\,923$ inequivalent pairs share a weight enumerator and none is weight-isometric. Everything not explicitly labelled as computed outside the formal development is machine-checked in Lean~4.

families.paper_title: Complete uniform hypergraphs that support an unsatisfiable CNF:\\ two open cells, one correction, and the threshold sequence
families.paper_abstract: Karve and Hirani attach to a hypergraph $g$ the set of CNFs that \emph{live} on it --- one clause per edge, on exactly that edge's variables, with an arbitrary choice of signs --- and call $g$ \emph{totally satisfiable} when every such CNF is satisfiable. For the complete $a$-uniform hypergraph $\Ka{a}{b}$ on $b$ vertices they publish a table of statuses for $a,b\le 7$, in which two cells are printed \texttt{unknown}.  We settle both: $\Ka{4}{7}$ is not totally satisfiable, by an explicit $35$-clause CNF that all $128$ assignments falsify, and $\Ka{5}{7}$ is totally satisfiable, because $\binom{7}{5}2^{2}=84<128$.  We also correct a third cell: the table prints $\Ka{3}{5}$ as \texttt{unsat} in boldface, and $\Ka{3}{5}$ is in fact totally satisfiable --- an exhaustive search over all $8^{10}$ sign choices for the ten triples of a five-element set finds no unsatisfiable one.  Beyond the published range we compute the threshold $t(a)=\min\{b:\Ka{a}{b}\text{ is not totally satisfiable}\}$ for $a=2,\dots,8$, obtaining $t=4,6,7,8,9,11,12$, and we compare it with the elementary counting bound $m(a)=\min\{b:\binom{b}{a}\ge 2^{a}\}$: the two agree at every computed $a$ except $a=3$, and $a=3$ is exactly the cell the published table gets wrong.  Every result stated in this abstract is machine-checked in Lean~4, in a development that declares no axiom of its own and contains no \texttt{sorry}; the reproduction of the published table and both formerly unknown cells are checked by the kernel outright, the corrected cell and the thresholds for $a\ge 6$ by the compiled evaluator.

families.paper_title: The ranks of primitives in the greedy regular convolutions
families.paper_abstract: For each positive integer $d$, Snellman's \emph{greedy convolution of block-length $d$} is the bounded homogeneous regular convolution obtained by partitioning $\Np$ greedily into arithmetic progressions $c,2c,\dots,rc$ with $r\le d$.  The head $c$ of such a progression is a \emph{primitive} element and $r$ is its \emph{rank}.  Snellman tabulates the least primitive of each rank for $2\le d\le 16$, records that $36$ of those $135$ cells were not filled by his search, and asks whether a primitive of rank $d-1$ exists at all.  We prove that none does, for any block-length: a primitive whose rank falls short of $d$ has rank at most $d-2$, so the rank spectrum is contained in $\{1,\dots,d-2\}\cup\{d\}$.  The proof is four lines and uses only the greedy rule; it settles the fifteen cells of the table that lie in the rank $d-1$ column, and it proves one clause of Snellman's conjecture for block-length $4$.  The same step yields three arithmetic corollaries the source does not state: a primitive of rank $r<d$ is divisible by some $t$ with $1<t\le d$; consequently every integer whose least prime factor exceeds $d$ is a primitive of full rank $d$; and a primitive of rank $d-2$ is divisible by~$d$.  Finally, we fill the remaining twenty-one unfilled cells with explicit least witnesses, the largest being $5\,000\,000$ at block-length $10$ and rank $8$, so that all $135$ cells of the table are settled and the rank spectrum for $d\le16$ is exactly $\{1,\dots,d-2\}\cup\{d\}$.  Every numbered result is machine-checked in Lean~4.

families.paper_title: The offline optimum of the lower-bound instances for Greedy packet forwarding on a line:\\ a correction to Equation~(16) of Boyar, Favrholdt, Larsen, Schewior and van~Stee
families.paper_abstract: Boyar, Favrholdt, Larsen, Schewior and van~Stee (arXiv:2603.06039) study the algorithm \textsc{Greedy} for forwarding packets on a line of $k$ active routers so as to minimise the maximum flow time, and prove that for packets of length $1$ or $2$ its competitive ratio is exactly $2-2^{1-k}$.  Their lower bound rests on a family of instances $\I{k}{h}$, for which they compute $\Greedy(\I{k}{h})=(2^k-1)h-1$ (their Equation~(10)) and $\Opt(\I{k}{h})=2^{k-1}h+3$ (their Equation~(16)).  We show that Equation~(16) is false: explicit feasible schedules cost $2h+1$ for $k=2$ ($h=4,6$), $4h+2$ for $k=3$ ($h=2,3,4$) and $8h+2$ for $k=4$ ($h=2$).  A counting bound at a single router, proved for an arbitrary instance and an arbitrary feasible schedule, shows that these schedules are optimal: $\Opt(\I{2}{h})=2h+1$ and $\Opt(\I{3}{h})=4h+2$ at those sizes, and $\Opt(\I{2}{h})\ge 2h+1$, $\Opt(\I{3}{h})\ge 4h+2$ for every $h\ge1$; at $k=4$ it gives $17\le\Opt(\I{4}{2})\le18<19$.  Equation~(10) and the two numbers of the source's Proposition~1 are confirmed; the simulated runs of \textsc{Greedy} are free of priority ties, so that its values hold for every tie-breaking rule.  The source's Theorem~2 survives: a smaller optimum strengthens a lower bound, and the limit $2-2^{1-k}$ is unchanged; what changes is the additive constant of the identity it prints, whose sharp form at the tested sizes is $\Greedy=\tfrac32\Opt-\tfrac52$ ($k=2$) and $\Greedy=\tfrac74\Opt-\tfrac92$ ($k=3$).  The source's open question whether packets of length three can raise its lower bound is examined as a measurement: with two active routers no such packet exists, and with three a bounded search found nothing above the source's own $7/4$.  Every theorem and lemma below is machine-checked in Lean~4.

families.paper_title: The greedy superstring ratio at small string lengths: $\rho_{8}, \rho_{9}, \rho_{11} > 2$ and $\rho_{4}, \rho_{5} > 15/8$
families.paper_abstract: Given a finite set $S$ of strings, \GREEDY{} repeatedly replaces a pair of distinct elements of maximum overlap by their overlap merge; ties are broken arbitrarily, and $\rho_{k}$ denotes the supremum of $|g| / \OPT(S)$ over all instances $S \subseteq \Sigma^{k}$ and all outputs $g$ of a legal execution.  The greedy superstring conjecture, that \GREEDY{} never outputs more than twice the optimum, stood for nearly four decades and was refuted on 1~September 2026 by Shibata, who proved $\rho_{k} \ge (9k+2)/(4k+4)$ for every \emph{even} $k \ge 10$, hence $23/11$ at $k = 10$ and $9/4$ in the limit.  We reproduce his refutation as an explicit instance of $198$ strings of length $10$ with a proved optimum, and then extend it in two directions his construction does not reach.  First, it refutes the conjecture already at string length~$8$: an instance of $252$ strings of length $8$ has optimum exactly $259$ and admits a legal greedy execution of output length $519 > 2 \cdot 259$.  Since $\rho_{k} \le 2$ is a theorem for $k \le 4$, string length $8$ is now the smallest at which the conjecture is known to fail.  Second, it fails at \emph{odd} string lengths, which the source's construction --- written for $k = 2s$ throughout --- cannot address at all: at $k = 9$ an instance of $336$ strings has optimum $344$ and a legal greedy output of length $689$, and at $k = 11$ an instance of $250$ strings has optimum $260$ and a legal greedy output of length $521$.  In each case we also exhibit the sharp boundary instance one block smaller, which lands exactly on twice the optimum, or one letter below it.  The paper also retains, from its first version, the refutation of the Cazaux--Rivals conjecture $\rho_{k} = 2 - 1/k$ at the two string lengths $k = 4$ and $k = 5$ left open by Chukhin, Kulikov, Mihajlin and Smal: $\rho_{4} \ge 437/233 > 15/8$ and $\rho_{5} \ge 325/173 > 15/8$, in particular $\rho_{4} > 9/5 = \rho_{3}$.  In every instance the optimum is proved by a counting bound together with an exhibited witness, so no search over superstrings is involved; the executions are certified merge by merge. Every statement about an individual instance made in a theorem or proposition below has been checked by the Lean~4 kernel; the remarks that report simulations instead are marked as such, and the final section says exactly what the kernel does and does not cover. Section~\ref{sec:correction} corrects two sentences of the first version of this paper.

families.paper_title: First values of the equivariant invariants $\tau_0$ and $\tau_1$ of strongly invertible knots
families.paper_abstract: Framba has recently defined an equivariant grid homology for strongly invertible knots and, from it, two integer invariants $\tau_0$ and $\tau_1$ satisfying $\tau_0(K)\le\tau(K)\le\tau_1(K)$.  That paper computes the two invariants for no knot, and asks for a strongly invertible knot at which an inequality is strict, and for two strong inversions on one knot that $\tau_0$ or $\tau_1$ tells apart.  We compute the invariants. For the figure-eight knot with the strong inversion carried by an explicit $6\times 6$ symmetric grid, $\tau_0=-1<0=\tau=\tau_1$, so the first inequality is strict; the same three values come out of a $7\times 7$ grid for the same knot, which exhibits the invariance rather than assuming it.  We also exhibit two $7\times7$ symmetric grid diagrams that agree on the fully blocked grid homology in every bigrading, on the simply blocked homology --- which is $\HFK(5_2)$ --- on $\GH$, and on the dimensions of the equivariant homology, and whose $\tau_0$ are $1$ and $0$.  They therefore carry inequivalent strongly invertible knots, and if their underlying knots agree, as the computed $\HFK$ and their common grid number indicate, then $\tau_0$ separates two strong inversions on $5_2$.  Every homology computed here is the $\FF_2$-homology of a finite bigraded block, obtained by exhaustive enumeration of the $n!$ grid states, and every numerical statement below is machine-checked in Lean~4.

Negative controls: 'every projection keeps a logical qubit', 'TABLE I's eight rows are all the surviving projections', 'only the gross code has k = 12' and 'no projection with k > 0 has d < 4' are all refuted; the k > 0 criterion is non-vacuous (24 subgroups on each side); the CSS check has content (replacing H_Z by H_X makes it fail); and the distance sweep's weight cap is not an artifact -- the same cell returns 6 uncertified at information weight 3 and 6 certified at weight 5

The |K| = 1 cell, the gross code itself: n = 144, rank H_X = rank H_Z = 66, k = 12 and CSS all kernel-bound from a and b; an explicit weight-12 X-type logical operator supported on qubits {4,7,10,16,19,34,40,43,46,52,55,70}; and the bracket 8 <= d_X, d_Z <= 12 from an exhaustive sweep of all 2921370387 combinations of at most 7 rows of the systematic generator of ker H_Z. The exact value d = 12 is Bravyi et al. and is NOT reproved here

The 24 projections of the gross code with k > 0 are only 12 codes up to qubit permutation, and TABLE I of arXiv:2607.28621v1 is redundant as well as non-exhaustive: its two Z12 x Z3 rows are one code and its three Z6 x Z3 rows are one code, so its eight printed rows are five codes. Every equivalence is an explicit qubit permutation carrying X-stabilisers to X-stabilisers and Z to Z (no X/Z relabelling); the one non-equivalence the parameters do not force -- the five [[24,4,4]] cells splitting 4 + 1 -- is separated by the number of weight-6 X-stabilisers, 24 against 16

The k > 0 criterion of the projection census, PROVED for every subgroup at once rather than enumerated: for every subgroup K <= Z12 x Z6 the projection of the gross code by K has k > 0 if and only if (4,0) is not in K and (0,2) is not in K -- that is, exactly when the images of x and y in G/K both still have order divisible by 3 -- and then k >= 2 [kBB_pos_iff is the iff only; k >= 2 is derived in the paper as a corollary of the formal proof, not a separate declaration -- noted 2026-09-08]; kernel-clean (axioms propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound; no native_decide anywhere in the proof), with K an arbitrary AddSubgroup and no case split over the 48

The general-group half of the criterion, for an arbitrary finite abelian group: for every finite abelian Gamma and every x, y in Gamma with x^12 = 1 and y^6 = 1, the bivariate bicycle code of a = x^3 + y + y^2, b = y^3 + x + x^2 over F2[Gamma] has k = 0 as soon as x^4 = 1 or y^2 = 1, because b (resp. a) is then a UNIT of F2[Gamma] -- (1 + x + x^2)^2 = x^2 when x^4 = 1, and 1 + y + y^2 = y when y^2 = 1, each plus a nilpotent -- and k >= 2 as soon as some monoid homomorphism to a characteristic-2 domain sends x and y to primitive cube roots of unity; instantiated in Lean at Gamma = Z12 x Z12 with x = (1,0), y = (0,6) -- a group that is not a quotient of Z12 x Z6 -- giving k = 0 for that n = 288 code, outside the projection census

Negative controls for the proved criterion: both conditions are needed (K = Z12 x 0 contains (4,0) but not (0,2) and has k = 0; K = 0 x Z6 is the mirror image), the criterion is NOT 'the Sylow-3 part of K is trivial' (the kernel of (u,v) |-> u + v mod 3 contains the order-3 element (4,2) and still has k > 0; 16 of the 24 live subgroups have a nontrivial Sylow-3 part), it is not constant (24 subgroups on each side, and the three failure modes occur 8 + 8 + 8 times), and each of the two conditions alone is a false criterion

families.paper_title: Every projection of the gross code:\\ the complete census of the quotients of $\code{144}{12}{12}$\\ by the subgroups of $\Z_{12}\times\Z_6$
families.paper_abstract: The gross code of Bravyi, Cross, Gambetta, Maslov, Rall and Yoder is the bivariate bicycle code over $\F_2[\Z_{12}\times\Z_6]$ with $a=x^3+y+y^2$, $b=y^3+x+x^2$. Hirasaki and Lee (arXiv:2607.28621) project it along quotient maps $\Z_{12}\times\Z_6\to G$, print eight of the resulting codes in their Table~I, and note that the table is not exhaustive.  We make it exhaustive.  Projections are indexed by the subgroups $K\le\Z_{12}\times\Z_6$, of which there are exactly $48$; every projection is a CSS code on $144/|K|$ qubits, and exactly $24$ of them encode at least one logical qubit.  Which ones do is decided by an arithmetic criterion: the projection by $K$ has $k>0$ if and only if the Sylow-$3$ part of $K$ is trivial or one of the two diagonal subgroups $\langle(4,2)\rangle$, $\langle(4,4)\rangle$ of order $3$.  We determine the exact minimum distance of every proper projection with $k>0$, on the $X$ and on the $Z$ side --- $\code{72}{12}{6}$, $\code{72}{8}{6}$, $\code{48}{8}{4}$, $\code{48}{4}{6}$, $\code{36}{8}{4}$, $\code{24}{8}{2}$, $\code{24}{4}{4}$, $\code{18}{8}{2}$, $\code{12}{4}{2}$, $\code{6}{4}{2}$ with multiplicities $1,2,1,1,3,1,5,1,6,2$ --- and find that the $24$ live projections are only $12$ codes up to qubit permutation, with explicit permutations; in particular the two $\Z_{12}\times\Z_3$ rows of Table~I are one code and its three $\Z_6\times\Z_3$ rows are one code, so its eight rows are five codes. The projection by the order-$8$ subgroup $\langle x^3,y^3\rangle$ is, term for term, the $\code{18}{8}{2}$ base code $a=1+y+y^2$, $b=1+x+x^2$ that Section~V of the same paper lifts, so that paper's projection table and its lift family are two ends of one chain. That chain is already in print --- Symons, Rajput and Browne exhibit the gross code as a double cover of the $\code{72}{12}{6}$ code and that code as a $4$-cover of the same $\code{18}{8}{2}$ base code --- and we certify it rather than claim it.  Every finite statement is certified by compiled evaluation inside Lean~4; the distance $12$ of the gross code itself is not re-certified (we certify $8\le d\le12$ and price the rest).  \emph{Added in this version.}  The criterion is now proved rather than enumerated, and proved for every subgroup at once: for an arbitrary subgroup $K\le\Z_{12}\times\Z_6$ the projection by $K$ has $k>0$ if and only if $K$ contains neither $(4,0)=x^4$ nor $(0,2)=y^2$ --- that is, exactly when the images of $x$ and of $y$ in $G/K$ both keep an order divisible by $3$ --- and then $k\ge2$.  The proof works in the group algebra $\F_2[G/K]$: if $y^2=1$ the projected $a$ is a unit ($1+y+y^2=y$, and $x^3+1$ is nilpotent), if $x^4=1$ the projected $b$ is a unit ($(1+x+x^2)^2=x^2$), and if $K$ contains neither element a character $G/K\to\F_4$ sending $x$ and $y$ to primitive cube roots of unity annihilates both polynomials.  The two halves hold for every finite abelian group $\Gamma$ and all $x,y\in\Gamma$ with $x^{12}=y^6=1$, with no semisimplicity; an instance over $\Z_{12}\times\Z_{12}$ on $288$ qubits lies outside the census.  This part of the development is checked by the Lean~4 kernel against Mathlib with no compiled evaluation.  Two published routes reach parts of the census --- Eq.~(8) of Chen et al.\ for the $24$ rectangular kernels $K=A\times B$, in the family they call $\mathrm{BB}(1,1,3,3)$, and the generalized-bicycle dimension formula for the $30$ kernels whose quotient is cyclic --- and between them they decide $18$ of the $24$ live projections; for the other $6$, four of which are printed rows of Table~I, no criterion was found.

families.title: Grünbaum's four-hyperplane counterexample: the five chart polynomials have no common zero on [-1,1]^6
families.description: Grünbaum conjectured in 1960 that every mass in `R^d` can be split into `2^d` parts of equal size by `d` hyperplanes. Hadwiger proved it for `d ≤ 3` (1966); Avis built counterexamples for `d ≥ 5` (1984) by concentrating the mass on the moment curve. **The case `d = 4` resisted both approaches for 66 years.** In the notation `Δ(j,k)` = the least dimension in which any `j` masses can be equipartitioned into `2^k` parts by `k` hyperplanes, the open question was whether `Δ(1,4)` is `4` or `5`.

statements.label: the five chart polynomials of arXiv:2608.23312v1 have no common zero on [-1,1]^6 (exact integer replay of its 38857-leaf Bernstein subdivision certificate)

the nonvanishing that settles Grunbaum's conjecture is tight to a relative 1/3064: at the origin of the chart every |f_s| is at most S_s/3064 with S = (3064,3064,3064,3064,1440) the sup bounds of GE7, so inf over the box of max_s |f_s|/S_s <= 1/3064 ~ 3.3e-4

the sup bounds of GE7 are attained: 3064 is the exact sup norm of f_0, f_1, f_2, f_3 on [-1,1]^6, reached at explicit corners (f_0 = f_1 = -3064, f_2 = f_3 = +3064); for f_4 the Bernstein bound 1440 is not attained (corner maximum 800, numerical sup about 1272)

families.paper_title: How tight is the four-hyperplane counterexample?\\ Exact bounds for its polynomial system
families.paper_abstract: Sober\'on has settled the last open case of Gr\"unbaum's 1960 equipartition problem by producing a mass in $\RR^{4}$ that no four hyperplanes equipartition.  The computational core of that proof is a system of five polynomials $f_{0},\dots,f_{4}$ in six variables, of degree at most $4$ in each variable, attached to a quaternionic chart of $SO(4)$: what the theorem needs is exactly that the five have no common zero on the box $Q=[-1,1]^{6}$, and the source proves this with a subdivision certificate of $38\,857$ dyadic boxes checked in fixed-point interval arithmetic.  We study that polynomial system as an object in its own right.  First, the nonvanishing is re-verified in exact integer arithmetic inside a formal proof: the passage from the certificate to the conclusion --- the power-to-Bernstein change of basis, de~Casteljau subdivision, and the convexity bound on a box --- is machine-checked, and the only thing computed rather than proved is the sign of $38\,857\cdot 5^{6}=607\,140\,625$ integers.  Second, we determine the size of the system: $\sup_{Q}\abs{f_{s}}=3064$ exactly for $s=0,1,2,3$, attained at explicit corners of $Q$, and $\sup_{Q}\abs{f_{4}}\le 1440$.  The two constants are the exact maxima of the Bernstein coefficient arrays of the $f_{s}$ on $Q$; for $f_{4}$, and only for $f_{4}$, that bound is not attained, and its sup norm is left open.  Third, with $S=(3064,3064,3064,3064,1440)$ we show that the nonvanishing is tight: \[ \inf_{z\in Q}\ \max_{0\le s\le 4}\ \abs{f_{s}(z)}/S_{s}\ \le\ 1/3064\approx 3.26\cdot10^{-4}, \] the value at the origin of the chart, where the five values are $(-1,0,0,0,0)$.  No point of $\{-1,0,1\}^{6}$ does better, and unformalised searches get no further than $1/3187$, so the constant is within about $4\ zero by about three parts in ten thousand of its own scale --- which is why a subdivision proof of it cannot be small.  Every theorem and proposition here is machine-checked in Lean~4; the searches that calibrate the constant are not, and are labelled where they occur.

statements.label: The complete Grimmer-Shu-Wang low-rank PEP certificate at horizon N = 3 in closed form: with rho the root in (0.6703, 0.6704) of 6 rho^5 - 5 rho^4 + 4 rho^3 - 3 rho^2 + 2 rho - 1 = 0 and s = sqrt(24 - 2/rho + 1/rho^2), the point d_0 = 5 - s, d_1 = 2 s - 6 - rho^{-3} annihilates all four residuals eps_0 = eps_1 = eps_2 = eps_3 = 0 of System D, has d_0, d_1 > 0, and makes every multiplier c_0..c_3, a_0, a_1, a_2, b_0, b_1 of Systems A, B, C strictly positive

The N = 3 GSW root: existence of a root of 6 rho^5 - 5 rho^4 + 4 rho^3 - 3 rho^2 + 2 rho - 1 in (0.66, 0.68) by the intermediate value theorem, and the enclosure 0.6703 < rho_3 < 0.6704 for every positive root -- against the source's Lemma 2, which proves only 1/2 < rho_N < 1

Every alpha = 1 + rho introduced by the backward recursions of Systems A and B cancels at N = 3: a_1, b_1, a_0, b_0 are POLYNOMIALS in rho, d_0, d_1, explicitly b_1 = (1 + d_0 + d_1) rho^4 + rho^2 - rho and a_1 = d_0 d_1 rho^6 + d_0 rho^3 + d_1^2 rho^6 + d_1 rho^6 + d_1 rho^4 + d_1 rho^3 + rho^3 + rho - 1, with a_0 of degree 7 and b_0 of degree 8 in rho

The exact minimal polynomial of the N = 3 GSW certificate coordinate: d_0 = 5 - s is a root of the monic degree-10 integer polynomial t^10 - 50 t^9 + 1011 t^8 - 10440 t^7 + 56661 t^6 - 145830 t^5 + 128521 t^4 - 65420 t^3 + 22551 t^2 - 4510 t + 353, so (with the enclosure 0.1789 < d_0 < 0.1792 of GW1) the certificate coordinate is one named algebraic number of degree exactly 10 = 2 * [Q(rho_3):Q]

families.paper_title: The Grimmer--Shu--Wang certificate at horizon three: closed form, uniqueness, and the degree of the certificate
families.paper_abstract: Grimmer, Shu and Wang (arXiv:2407.11739) conjectured that the Drori--Teboulle minimax constant-stepsize bound for $N$ steps of gradient descent on $1$-smooth convex functions is certified by a dual multiplier matrix of a specific low-rank shape, determined by one vector $d\in\R^{N-1}$; Lixing Zhang (arXiv:2605.11421) proved that a positive such $d$ exists for every $N\ge3$ by a boundary-sign and Brouwer fixed-point argument that exhibits no certificate, gives no closed form, and makes no uniqueness claim.  We settle all three questions at $N=3$.  Let $\rho$ be the root in $(0,1)$ of $6\rho^5-5\rho^4+4\rho^3-3\rho^2+2\rho-1$, the irreducible quintic factor of the root equation $\rho^6(6\rho+7)=1$, and $s=\sqrt{24-2/\rho+1/\rho^2}$.  The point $d_0=5-s$, $d_1=2s-6-\rho^{-3}$ annihilates all four residuals of the certificate system, is strictly positive, and makes all nine multipliers strictly positive; it is the only zero of the first three residual equations with $d_1\ge0$, the second branch $d_0=5+s$ being an equally exact zero with $d_1<0$; every division by $\alpha=1+\rho$ in the backward recursions cancels, so that $a_0,a_1,b_0,b_1$ are polynomials in $\rho,d_0,d_1$; and $d_0$ is a root of an explicit monic integer polynomial of degree $10$, irreducible over $\Q$ by computation, so the certificate coordinate has degree $10=2\,[\Q(\rho):\Q]$ over $\Q$.  The engine is the pair of conservation identities of Zhang's terminal-completion argument, one of which also shows that the $\delta$-certificate relaxation of Grimmer--Shu--Wang is no relaxation at $\delta=0$.  Every statement is verified in Lean~4 with Mathlib.

families.description: `σ` is the cyclic shift of `F_q^n`, `(σ^k u)_i = u_{i-k}`. A subspace `U ≤ F_q^n` is **cyclically covering** if `⋃_{r<n} σ^r(U) = F_q^n`, and

statements.label: h_2(28) >= 3 with an explicit working triple of F_2^28, checked over all 2^28 words
The lifted triple spans a MAXIMAL working-together subspace of F_2^28: no fourth independent vector extends it
AGJ Table 1 recomputed from the definition: h_2(n) = 2, 2, 2, 0, 3, 2 for n = 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10 (witness and exhaustive non-existence one step up)
A vector of F_2^n works iff x^{2^a}+1 divides v(x), 2^a the 2-part of n -- verified over every vector for 3 <= n <= 12
Controls: the fast UInt32 layer agrees with the transparent coordinate definition, and the search returns false when asked for too much

families.paper_title: The last open cell of the Aaronson--Groenland--Johnston table:\\ an explicit working triple in $\F_2^{28}$\\ that spans a maximal working-together subspace
families.paper_abstract: A subspace $U\le\F_q^n$ is cyclically covering if the cyclic shifts of $U$ cover $\F_q^n$, and $h_q(n)$ is the largest codimension of such a subspace (Cameron, Ellis and Raynaud).  Table~1 of Aaronson, Groenland and Johnston (arXiv:1903.10613) bounds $h_2(n)$ for $n\le29$ and leaves four cells open: $n=21$, $22$, $26$, $28$.  Sun, Ma and Zeng (2025) closed $n=21$ and Wang and Shi (arXiv:2607.24351, $h_2(2p)=2$ for primes $p\ge5$ with $2$ a primitive root) closed $n=22$ and $26$, so $h_2(28)\in\{3,4\}$ is the only value of the table still undetermined.  We do not determine it.  We exhibit three explicit vectors $t_1,t_2,t_3\in\F_2^{28}$ that work together (for every $u\in\F_2^{28}$ a single cyclic shift $\sigma^ku$ is orthogonal to all three), certified over all $2^{28}$ words, so that $U=\{t_1,t_2,t_3\}^\perp$ is a cyclically covering subspace of dimension $25$ --- the table's lower bound $h_2(28)\ge3$ with a witness.  The new fact is that this triple is maximal: none of the $2^{24}$ vectors of $\F_2^{28}$ that work on their own (the multiples of $x^4+1$) extends it to four linearly independent vectors that work together; for each such vector outside the span a witness $u\in\{1,3,\dots,1287\}$ is recorded on which the quadruple fails.  Equivalently, no hyperplane of $U$ is cyclically covering: $U$ is a minimal cyclically covering subspace, and no covering subspace of codimension $4$ lies inside it.  The table's cells $n=5,\dots,10$ are recomputed from the definition, and the characterisation of the vectors that work ($x^{2^b}+1$ divides $v(x)$, $2^b\,\|\,n$) is verified over every vector for $3\le n\le12$.  Every finite statement is certified by compiled evaluation inside Lean~4; the gluing of the two halves of the $2^{28}$-word sweep is a kernel-checked lemma.  The exhaustive negative ($h_2(28)=3$) is priced at about $10^7$ processor-hours by a measured run and was not attempted.

families.title: Skew-regular quaternary Hadamard matrices: which orders can exist, and why order 20 cannot
families.description: A **quaternary Hadamard matrix** of order `n` has entries in `{1, -1, i, -i}` and satisfies `H Hᴴ = n I`. It is **regular** if every row sums to the same complex number `r`, and of **skew type** if `H = I + Q` with `Qᴴ = -Q`, equivalently `H + Hᴴ = 2 I`. **Skew-regular** means both. Source: Kharaghani and Zaitsev, arXiv:2510.06489, which constructs skew-regular quaternary Hadamard matrices of order `1 + p²` with constant row sum `1 - p i`, for every odd prime power `p`.

statements.label: The order of a skew-regular quaternary Hadamard matrix with n >= 2 is 1 + s^2 with s odd; equivalently n = 2 (mod 8)
Headline: no skew-regular quaternary Hadamard matrix of order 20 exists

The source's construction, proved for **every** odd prime power at once: a skew-regular quaternary Hadamard matrix of order `1 + p²` with row sum `1 - p i`
**An iff at every order below 200**: a skew-regular quaternary Hadamard matrix of order `2 ≤ n ≤ 200` exists iff `n ∈ {2, 10, 26, 50, 82, 122, 170}`
The composition route to `n = 226` is closed: the product of two permitted orders is never a permitted order
Negative controls for the construction: it needs `|K| ≡ 1 (mod 4)`, and the diagonal conjugation is what produces regularity

statements.label: Problem 12 of arXiv:2406.19945 has an affirmative answer at k = 1 (n = 4, q = 3): for every u_1,u_2,u_3,u_4 in {0,1,2}^4 there is a vertex w of H(4,3) with g(u_i,w) < i for i = 1,2,3,4 -- stated both in the source's rational form (prob_one_rational) and in the denominator-cleared integer form (prob_one)

Problem 12 of arXiv:2406.19945 has an affirmative answer at k = 2 (n = 7, q = 3), proved by counting rather than by search: the four live constraint sets at the zero vertex have sizes |A_1| = 630 and |A_2^c| = 507, |A_3^c| = 45, |A_4^c| = 3, and 630 > 507+45+3 = 555, so at least 75 vertices w work for every u_1,...,u_7

b(H(4,3)) = 4 and b(H(7,3)) = 6, kernel-bound, as corollaries of HB1/HB2 and the source's derivation; with the matching refutations that H(4,3) has no burning sequence of length 3 and H(7,3) none of length 5

b(H(3k+1,3)) <= 2k+2 for EVERY k, formalized: the three constant words 0-bar, 1-bar, 2-bar are the first three terms of a burning sequence of length 2k+2, by a pigeonhole on the letter counts (k-1)+k+(k+1) < 3k+1

The source's derivation, formalized for EVERY k: an affirmative answer to Problem 12 at k rules out every burning sequence of length 2k+1 and hence gives b(H(3k+1,3)) = 2k+2 exactly; the step it rests on, sum over the three diagonal shifts t of d(u, w + t*1) = 2n, is proved for every n

Negative controls: (i) no vertex w has 3g(a,w) < 2 at n = 4 or n = 7, so the i = 1 threshold cannot be tightened; (ii) 45 of 81 vertices at n = 4 and 1557 of 2187 at n = 7 fail the i = 1 constraint, so the existential is not vacuous; (iii) the bands must widen with i -- for u_1 = 0000, u_2 = 0011, u_3 = 0022 no w satisfies the i = 1 band three times

MEASUREMENT: the counting proof of HB2 has an exact reach. The plain union bound |D_1| > sum_i |D_i^c| holds only for k <= 2 (36 > 3; 630 > 555; fails at k = 3 by 12600 < 28047). Sharpening it by taking, for each i, the worst shift rather than the whole complement -- legitimate because the count depends only on the sorted colour-profile of the shift -- settles k = 1,2,3,4,5 with slacks 33, 429, 5793, 68697, 374163 and FAILS at k = 6 (139675536 < 156258609) and at every k = 6..11 computed. So k = 6 (n = 19) is where this argument stops, and the obstruction is mathematical, not computational.

b(H(n,3)) <= floor(2n/3) + 2 for EVERY n (not only n = 3k+1), kernel-clean: the three constant words are the first three terms of a burning sequence of that length, by a pigeonhole on the letter counts

b(H(6,3)) = 6, kernel-bound by a two-ball bound: however Gamma_4(v_1) and Gamma_3(v_2) are placed they leave at least 118 of the 729 vertices uncovered (minimum at v_2-v_1 = 111111), while the remaining three balls of a length-5 burning sequence hold only 73+13+1 = 87; with HB8 this pins the value

PROSE: the same two-ball bound settles b(H(14,3)) = 11 and b(H(22,3)) = 16, the two further cells the ball-volume bound misses within n <= 22; n = 22 is 3k+1 at k = 7, i.e. the first case for which Tokushige's Problem 12 was actually needed. Slacks 95609 and 530378004; the bound still fails at n = 9,12,15,17,18,20,21

PROSE: b(H(9,3)) = 8 by a three-ball bound. With v_1 = 0 by vertex-transitivity, the 2816 of 19683 vertices v_2 whose two-ball residue is at most 1018 + |Gamma_4| = 3869 were swept against all v_3: min |V minus (Gamma_6(0) u Gamma_5(v_2) u Gamma_4(v_3))| = 1260 > 1018 = |Gamma_3|+|Gamma_2|+|Gamma_1|+|Gamma_0|, so no length-7 burning sequence exists

The ball-volume bound as one reusable kernel-clean lemma (not_isBurning_of_ballSum: for every n and b, if sum_{j<b} |Gamma_{b-1-j}| < 3^n there is no burning sequence of length b), and the values it pins kernel-bound: b(H(5,3)) = 5, b(H(8,3)) = 7, b(H(10,3)) = 8, b(H(11,3)) = 9; plus the control that the same sum fails at n = 6 (793 >= 729)

PROSE: the three-ball bound in closed form. Fixing u = 0, the stabiliser of 0 in Aut(H(n,3)) reduces a pair (v,w) to how many coordinates fall in each of five agreement classes, and a DP over the C(n+4,4) type vectors gives the exact minimum residue. It reproves b(H(9,3)) = 8 and settles, beyond the two-ball bound, b(H(17,3)) = 13 (residue 14702688 > tail 14597433). Every n <= 22 now has a value except n = 12, 15, 18, 20, 21, and the source's conjectured floor(2n/3)+2 is confirmed at every settled n. The extremal configuration is always the three constant words.

The colour-band reformulation of Problem 12, kernel-clean for every n and every i: G(u,w) < 3i (i.e. the source's g(u,w) < i) holds exactly when every letter count of w - u lies in the band [k+1-i, k+i], where n = 3k+1. Consequences proved with it: the condition is vacuous for i >= 2k+1, so a list of 3k+1 vertices constrains only its first 2k members; and the i = 1 band is the set of words whose letter counts are k+1,k,k in some order. The identity behind it, d(u, w+t*1) + #{j : (w-u)_j = -t} = n, is proved for every n.

families.paper_title: Alon's transmitting problem for the Hamming graph $\Ham{n}{3}$: Tokushige's Problem 12 at $k=1,2$, and the burning number of $\Ham{6}{3}$
families.paper_abstract: Tokushige, in his work on Alon's transmitting problem and a multicolour Beck--Spencer lemma, proves $\lfloor(1-1/q)n\rfloor+1\le \bn(\Ham{n}{q})\le\lfloor(1-1/q)n+(q+1)/2\rfloor$ for the burning number of the Hamming graph with $q\ge3$, conjectures that the upper bound is the truth, and closes with an open problem --- Problem 12 of the journal version --- whose affirmative answer would settle the conjecture for $q=3$ and $n=3k+1$.  It asks whether, for arbitrary $u_1,\dots,u_{3k+1}\in\{0,1,2\}^{3k+1}$, some vertex $w$ satisfies $g(u_i,w)<i$ for every $i$, where $g$ maximises $|\tfrac23 n-d(u,\cdot)|$ over the three diagonal shifts of $w$.  The problem is answered there for no $k$.  We answer it affirmatively at $k=1$ and at $k=2$: at $k=1$ by an exhaustive check made small by a vacuity cap, and at $k=2$ --- where the exhaustive form has $2187^5$ instances --- by a union bound over translates, $630>507+45+3$, which in fact produces at least $75$ witnesses $w$ for every input.  We also determine $\bn(\Ham{6}{3})=6$ --- beyond the single value in print, the smallest cell of Tokushige's conjecture at $q=3$ settled neither by ball counting nor by Problem 12 --- using a two-ball refinement of the volume bound. Along the way we record a reformulation of the problem as a band condition on letter counts, valid for every $n$ and $i$, and the burning numbers $\bn(\Ham{n}{3})$ for $n=4,5,6,7,8,10,11$.  Every theorem, proposition, lemma and corollary below has been machine-checked; the closing remarks report frontier measurements made outside the formal development and are labelled as such.
