families.paper_title: Certified dominance at the origin\\ for polynomial-rate shrinkage estimators\\ of a normal mean
families.paper_abstract: Let $X\sim N_p(\theta,I_p)$ be estimated under quadratic loss.  Maruyama and Takemura build, from a positive non-decreasing function $\Phi$, shrinkage estimators $\ith_\varphi$ that dominate the James--Stein estimator $\ith_\JS$ provided they dominate it at the origin, i.e.\ provided $\Rd(\ith_\JS,\ith_\varphi;p)=R(0,\ith_\JS)-R(0,\ith_\varphi)\ge0$.  For their second example $\Phi_2(w;b,\gamma)=(w/b)^\gamma$ with $b=1$, $\gamma=5$ their Proposition~3.2 gives this for all $p\ge8$, and of the remaining dimensions they write only that ``we numerically check that $\Rd(\ith_\JS,\ith_\varphi;p_*)\ge0$ for $3\le p\le7$ individually''; no quadrature rule, error bound or range appears in the paper.  We prove those five cells. We prove the same for $b=1$, $C=1$ at $p=4,\dots,7$, cell by cell, where the source instead propagates upward from $p=3$ by its Proposition~3.1.  At $p=3$ we prove a two-sided rational bracket for the underlying integral, $1/300\le I\le1/50$, so that the dominance there is strict and the risk gain at the origin lies between $1/(6\sqrt{2\pi})=0.0664\ldots$ and $1/\sqrt{2\pi}=0.3989\ldots$, where the source prints only a table symbol.  We also certify one entry the source marks as failing --- at $b=3$, $p=3$ the risk difference is at most $-1/20000$ times an explicit positive constant --- and the return to nonnegativity at $p=4$ in that same column.  The method replaces floating-point quadrature by exact rational coverings: after the substitution $w=u^2$ the whole question is the sign of a one-variable integral of a rational function against the Gaussian weight, and fourteen finite rational computations bound it.  The reduction, the soundness of the coverings, the alternating Taylor sandwich for $\exp$ and the Gaussian tail estimate are proved rather than computed.  All statements are machine-checked in Lean~4; Section~\ref{sec:verif} records exactly what the kernel checks and what it does not.

families.paper_title: Convex polyominoes by area and degree of convexity
families.paper_abstract: The \emph{degree of convexity} $\dc(P)$ of a convex polyomino $P$ is the least $k$ such that any two cells of $P$ are joined by a monotone path inside $P$ with at most $k$ changes of direction; the $k$-convex polyominoes are those with $\dc(P)\le k$.  Two 2026 papers grade this class along adjacent axes and neither crosses them: Castelli and Massazza count by area but only at $k=2$, and Conway and Guttmann count by semi-perimeter --- explicit series for $k=3,\dots,7$ and a conjectured generating function for every $k$. We compute the underlying object both papers summarise --- the joint distribution $T(n,d)$ of convex polyominoes of area $n$ by exact degree of convexity $d$ --- for all $n\le 19$ and all $d$, and read off the cumulative columns for every $k\le 17$; by area only $k=1$ and $k=2$ were previously available.  Three structural facts come out of the triangle: the largest degree of convexity available at area $n$ is exactly $n-2$; degree $d$ first occurs at area $d+2$, and is then attained by exactly four polyominoes; and each near-extremal diagonal $n\mapsto T(n,n-2-j)$ agrees with a polynomial of degree $j$ in $n$ with leading coefficient $4/j!$, for $j\le 5$ over the computed range.  We record the same three phenomena for the semi-perimeter grading, with $n-2$ replaced by $s-3$ and $4/j!$ by $4\cdot 2^{j}/j!$.  We also correct one entry of the published $k=2$ column: the true value of $|\mathrm{ZConv}(29)|$ is $194304762$, not the printed $94304762$.  The enumerations are calibrated against eleven independently published sequences --- three by area, eight by semi-perimeter --- and every theorem below is machine-checked in Lean~4; values quoted from a separate implementation in C are marked as such.

families.paper_title: Exact critical-temperature bounds for the two-dimensional Ising model on periodic tessellations: the Kac--Ward polynomials $P_q$, their decimal cells, and the lower bound on $\Tc$ from the largest face
families.paper_abstract: Joseph and Boettcher (arXiv:2601.02502v2, Phys.\ Rev.\ E 113, 064113 (2026)) prove that the nearest-neighbour ferromagnetic Ising model on any two-dimensional periodic tessellation of the plane has critical value $\tc = \tanh(J/\Tc) \ge \tan(\pi/(2\qmax))$, where $\qmax$ is the largest coordination number, through a factorisation of the characteristic polynomial of the zero-momentum Kac--Ward matrix into universal polynomials $P_q(u)$.  We first make the source's own data exact: $P_q = A_q^2$ or $uB_q^2$ where $A_q, B_q$ are the two binomial halves of $(1+i\sqrt u)^q$, which satisfy $A_q^2 + uB_q^2 = (1+u)^q$ in every commutative ring; all eleven polynomials printed in the source's Table~I are correct; the largest root of $P_q$ is $\cot^2(\pi/(2q))$ for every $q \ge 2$; and every decimal of the source's $t_{\mathrm{c,min}}$ and $T_{\mathrm{c,max}}$ columns is certified by rational arithmetic alone, through the sign of the integer polynomial $A_q$ at rational points and one-sided Taylor bounds on $\exp$ --- no value of $\pi$, $\tan$, $\log$ or $\exp$ is evaluated numerically.  For the three cells $q = 7, 9, 11$ that the source prints only as decimals we give the minimal polynomial of the square of each (degrees $3$, $3$, $5$) and explain, via the casus irreducibilis, why no real-radical closed form exists.  The main new observation is that the source's bound, applied to the dual tessellation and transported back through its own duality relation $\tc^{(\mathrm d)} = (1-\tc)/(1+\tc)$, yields a \emph{lower} bound on $\Tc$ controlled by the largest face size $\pmax$: $\tc \le \tan(\pi/4 - \pi/(2\pmax))$, for every tessellation to which the source's two inputs apply --- in particular, by the source's own admissibility condition, one with no $2$-coordinated site.  Every such periodic triangulation therefore has $\Tc/J \ge 3.6409569\ldots$ (the Triangular lattice), every quadrangulation $\Tc/J \ge 2.2691853\ldots$ (Square), every tessellation with faces of at most six sides $\Tc/J \ge 1.5186514\ldots$ (Honeycomb), and when $1/\pmax + 1/\qmax = 1/2$ the critical value is pinned exactly by these two combinatorial parameters.  The source draws no such conclusion and states that $\Tc$ ``is not bounded from below''; the two statements are compatible, since the new bound degenerates as $\pmax \to \infty$.  Finally, the source's main text prints $\Tc/J = 5.00795$ for the Laves-Star lattice; its own printed data force $\Tc/J \in [5.00699, 5.00719]$, which excludes that value and contains the $5.00705$ of its Table~III.  All stated results are checked in Lean~4 with Mathlib.

statements.label: The four-digit routine reduces to d1(b^3-1) + d2(b^2-b) at EVERY base, and the difference coordinates carry the dynamics

families.paper_title: Base scaling in four-digit Kaprekar dynamics, and an infinite family of bases with no unique terminating cycle
families.paper_abstract: The four-digit Kaprekar routine in base $b$ --- sort the digits downward, subtract the upward arrangement, repeat --- depends only on the two differences $d_1=a_1-a_4$ and $d_2=a_2-a_3$, and so acts on a set $X_b$ of size about $b^2/2$.  Chen, Ono, Schwartz and Thakur classified its terminal cycles for every odd base $B>3$ and closed with a remark, supported only by numerical evidence, predicting that the even bases with a unique terminating cycle are exactly $2^{2n+1}\cdot 3$, $2^{2n+1}\cdot 5$ and $2^{3n\pm1}\cdot 7$, with cycle lengths $6(n+1)$, $1$ and $3$.  We work with the scaling law $K_{mb}(md_1,md_2)=m\,K_b(d_1,d_2)$, valid at every base on the region where one step is $\{\lvert 2d_1-b\rvert,\lvert 2d_2-b\rvert\}$ --- the case $m=2$ is due to Devlin and Zeng --- and with the transport of terminal cycles that it yields.  Our main result is that every base with an odd divisor in $[9,51]$ carries two disjoint terminal cycles and hence has no unique terminating cycle; the covered set contains more than half of the even bases below $10^{6}$, and no previously published result applies to most of those.  We also decide the predicted classification, in both directions, for every even $b\le 200$ and for $b=224$ and $b=384$.  Every statement is machine-checked in Lean~4.

families.paper_title: The NSUCRYPTO~2019 conjecture on the Kasami APN function: exhaustive verification for $n\le 18$, an equidistribution of cubes at even $n$, and the weight distributions computed along the way
families.paper_abstract: Let $\gcd(k,n)=1$, let $F(x)=x^{4^{k}-2^{k}+1}$ be the Kasami function on $\FF_{2^{n}}$, and let $\Delta=\{F(b)+F(b+1)+1 : b\in\FF_{2^{n}}\}$.  A conjecture posed as an unsolved problem at NSUCRYPTO~2019, originating with Carlet, asserts that $\#\{(x,y,z)\in\Delta^{3} : v_{1}x+v_{2}y+(v_{1}+v_{2})z=0\}=2^{2n-3}$ for every pair of distinct nonzero $v_{1},v_{2}$.  The conjecture is open; the largest published verified range is $n\le 13$.  We verify it exhaustively at $n=14,15,16,17,18$: for all $44$ admissible pairs $(n,k)$ in that range and for every one of the $2^{n}-2$ values of $\rho=v_{2}/v_{1}$ --- at $n=18$, all $262{,}142$ of them for each of the six admissible $k$ --- covering $7.3\cdot 10^{11}$ ordered pairs $(v_{1},v_{2})$ in total; together with the smaller cells this settles every admissible $(n,k)$ with $n\le 18$ inside one machine-checked development.  Part of the new range is confirmed a second time by counting the triples of $\Delta^{3}$ directly, with no character sum anywhere.  Three further findings come out of the same computation. First, in every even cell computed here the triples split evenly over the three cosets of the cubes: writing $s=v_{1}x+v_{2}y+(v_{1}+v_{2})z$, each coset receives exactly $(2^{3n-3}-2^{2n-3})/3$ of the triples with $s\ne 0$, so the cubic multiplicative character sum over them vanishes.  This is verified exhaustively at $n=4,6,8$ and at sampled $\rho$ for $n=10,12$; it is the datum Carlet identifies as what the even case needs, and it is pinned at its mean in the same way the conjecture itself is.  Second, the associated character spectrum is the weight distribution of a binary code of Ding, and it confirms Ding's own conjecture on that code at every odd cell computed, $m=15$ and $m=17$ included; at $m=18$, outside the conjecture's scope, the code is a fifteen-weight $[131072,18,64384]$ code.  Third, writing $\max_{a\ne 0}|2S(a)|=2^{(n+v)/2}$ for the character sum $S$ of $\Delta$, the value $v\in\{1,3\}$ holds at $46$ of the $48$ nondegenerate cells with $n$ odd and $5\le n\le 17$ but fails at $(15,4)$ and $(15,11)$, where $v=7$; $S$ is invariant under $a\mapsto a^{2}$, and that locates the exceptional value at $a=1$ in both places where this data is anomalous.  What makes those cells exceptional is open.  Every theorem is machine-checked in Lean~4; the computations that are not are labelled as such.

The complete exceptional-pair list by the criterion for p <= 20000: for 3 <= l <= 23 exactly (79, 13) and (277, 23), each at exactly the two conjugates b, b^{-1}; for 29 <= l <= 47 exactly (14447, 31), (12547, 41) and (659, 47), likewise

Theorem (prose, journal section 3.2): for q = p, rank_{F_p} D < (l-1)/2 if and only if Delta(b) = 0, where S = {k^{-1} mod l : 1 <= k <= (l-1)/2} is a half-system mod l, F_j(T) = prod_{u in S} (T - b^{ju}) in F_p[T], and Delta(b) = det[[T^i] F_j(T)]_{1 <= j, i <= (l-1)/2}. Delta involves no Jacobi sum: it is a function of (p, l, b) alone, computable in O(l^3) against O(p log p) for one Jacobi sum

The wide C censuses, beyond what fits in the kernel: exhaustive minor enumeration finds (79, 13) as the ONLY MDS failure for l = 7, 11, 13 over every prime p < 10^6 (27,460 pairs, 235,426 conjugates) and no failure at all for l = 17, 19 over every p < 10^5 (1,128 pairs, 19,098 conjugates) or for l = 3, 5 over every p < 10^5; and the criterion sweep is complete for 3 <= l <= 47 with p < 10^7 (950,317 pairs, 12 rank drops = 6 exceptional pairs including (593141, 47)), for 53 <= l <= 101 with p < 3*10^5 (3,981 pairs, 16 rank drops = 8 pairs), and -- unified -- for 3 <= l <= 101 with p < 10^6 (124,131 pairs, 1,954,784 conjugates, 28 rank drops = exactly the same 14 pairs and no fifteenth). Fourteen exceptional pairs in all, thirteen of them not in the source. In every single failure the rank drops by exactly one and exactly the inverse pair {b, b^{-1}} fails; no failure at full rank has ever been observed

Heuristic with measured agreement: since Delta(b) is a single determinant in F_p, a conjugate should fail with probability about 1/p, so the expected number of failing conjugates with p <= N is sum_{p = 1 mod l, p <= N} (l-1)/p, which is about log log N + C_l and DIVERGES. Measured on three sweeps: 21.2 predicted against 12 observed for l <= 47 and p < 10^7 (-1.4 sigma), 10.7 against 16 for 53 <= l <= 101 and p < 3*10^5 (+1.2 sigma), and 30.70 against 28 for the unified window 3 <= l <= 101, p < 10^6 (-0.4 sigma, the largest and the only uniform window). If the heuristic is right, Katre's 'except possibly for finitely many primes p' is false for every l >= 7, though only just: one expects about one new exceptional prime per l per factor e^e in N

families.paper_title: Exceptional primes for Katre's MDS conjecture on the Jacobi-sum matrix $D$,\\ and a rank-drop criterion free of Jacobi sums
families.paper_abstract: Let $l$ be an odd prime, $p\equiv1\pmod l$ a prime, $\gamma$ a generator of $\FF_{p}^{\times}$, and let $J(1,1)_{l}=\sum_{i}a_{i}\zeta_{l}^{i}$ be the Jacobi sum of order $l$ attached to $\gamma$.  Katre and Rajwade's condition~(vi), the condition that pins down which conjugate of $J(1,1)_{l}$ belongs to $\gamma$, becomes after expansion a system of $l-1$ congruences modulo $p$ that is \emph{linear} in the $(l-1)/2$ unknowns $b,b^{2},\dots,b^{(l-1)/2}$, where $b=\gamma^{(p-1)/l}$; write $D$ for its $(l-1)\times(l-1)/2$ coefficient matrix.  Katre has conjectured that any $(l-1)/2$ rows of $D$ are linearly independent apart from finitely many $p$, so that $D^{\mathsf T}$ generates an MDS $[\,l-1,(l-1)/2\,]$ code.  Katre and Jadhav proved this for $l=3$ and $l=5$ and reported, in one sentence and without data, a failure at $(p,l)=(79,13)$.  We certify that failure and supply the data: exactly two of the twelve conjugates fail, $b=62$ and $b=65=62^{-1}$, and they fail by a \emph{rank collapse}, $\rank D=5<6$, so that all $\binom{12}{6}=924$ maximal minors vanish at once; explicit kernel vectors are given.  We then exhibit thirteen further exceptional pairs $(p,l)$, which we did not find in the literature, reaching $l=101$ and $p=593141$; each is again a certified rank collapse, at a pair of conjugates $\{b,b^{-1}\}$ inverse to one another.  We verify the conjecture for $l=7,11,13$ on windows by exhaustive enumeration of all maximal minors. We also prove, for $q=p$, that $\rank_{\FF_{p}}D<(l-1)/2$ if and only if an explicit determinant $\Delta(b)$ vanishes, where $\Delta$ is a function of $(p,l,b)$ alone and involves no Jacobi sum; it costs $O(l^{3})$ against $O(p\log p)$, and we machine-check its agreement with the Jacobi-sum rank cell by cell on a census window.  Outside the formal development, wider sweeps and a divergence heuristic suggest that the exceptional set is infinite for every $l\ge7$, with counting function $\asymp\log\log N$, so that the conjecture's clause ``except possibly for finitely many primes $p$'' is heuristically false.  Every theorem below is machine-checked in Lean~4 except the criterion itself, whose proof is by hand.

families.title: Fibers of the four new Keller counterexamples F_4-F_7 of arXiv:2608.00222, whose complete stratifications the paper defers to a subsequent version
families.description: The Jacobian conjecture (Keller 1939) fell in dimension three on 19 July 2026 (Alpöge), with a uniform family the next day (Gallagher) and a geometric explanation — the *tangent sweep* — on 23 July (Speyer). On 31 July 2026 Gao posted **arXiv:2608.00222**, which generalises the sweep from plane curves to direction fields on hypersurfaces and produces five new explicit Keller counterexamples. Four of them are the subject of this family:

statements.label: F_4: an explicit rational target with five distinct rational preimages -- the geometric degree 5 realised over Q
F_5: an explicit rational point off the image -- the degree-ten fiber polynomial degenerates to 20480(w_1-1/4)^10 and the unique root carries gamma = 0
F_5: if the fiber polynomial splits over R then all ten roots equal 1/4 -- the target-independent coefficients pin the whole real locus
F_6: the fiber sextic never splits over R -- at most four of the six generic preimages are ever real
F_6: an explicit rational target with four distinct rational preimages -- the rational maximum of KF4 is attained
F_7: the closed-form transverse solution of the curve-type fiber system in dimension five, and R_0 = w^5(w-1)(w^6+w^5+w^4-w^3-w^2-w+1), as polynomial identities
F_4: the divisibility statements C | S_1, C^2 | S_2, C | S_3 and det J(F_4) = -44/9, as polynomial identities from the construction

F_6: at the explicit target (1,-33/8,-1,-1,57/8) the fiber sextic factors as 2w(w+1)(w-1/2)(w-3/2)(w^2+5/4) and gamma is nonzero at every one of its six roots -- the fiber has exactly six points

F_6: the two non-rational preimages of the fiber over (1, -33/8, -1, -1, 57/8), explicitly in Q(sqrt(-5)) -- with KF5 and KF9 the complete six-point fiber of F_6, and the first non-rational preimage exhibited for any of F_4-F_7

MEASUREMENT: the price of a Q(sqrt(-5)) fiber point in Lean -- 691 lines and 29 s CPU for two modules, no native_decide, a parametric (K, s) carrier instead of a quadratic-field construction, and staging the substitution at every w = gamma^k u boundary is 135x less certificate

F_6: the stage inverted in closed form on gamma != 0, so every root of the fiber sextic lifts to an explicit preimage -- six distinct points derived rather than exhibited, and the four rational KF5 points re-proved by norm_num without native_decide

F_4: the fiber correspondence in both directions -- w2 = N/w1 and gamma = G/w1 from the 2x2 minor -w1, the elimination w1*(third residual) = -R with no side condition, and the triangular stage inverted AND shown unique, so preimages correspond to the roots of the tangency quintic carrying gamma != 0 at every target with Y2 != 0

F_4: the fiber over (1,-13/6,-5/18,97/18) is EXACTLY the five rational points of KF1 -- the tangency quintic splits as (2/9)(w+5/2)(w+1)(w+1/2)(w-1)(w-2), gamma takes the nonzero values 21/4, -1/2, 5/12, 15/4, -7/6 at the five roots, and there is no sixth preimage over any field of characteristic zero, C included

F_4: a target-explicit invariant of every fiber -- prod_j (1 + w_1j^2) = 49 + (81/4)(Y_1 + Y_3 - 2/3)^2 whenever the tangency quintic splits, hence never below 49 and equal to 49 exactly on the plane Y_1 + Y_3 = 2/3; consequently no fiber over a rational target has a sweep parameter with w^2 = -1, and every totally real fiber has one with |w_1| > 1

F_5: the first exhibited preimage of any of its fibers -- F_5(1, 0, 0, -1/2) = (1, 90/29, 129/58, 55/58) with gamma = 1, w_1 = 1, w_2 = 1/2, so that target IS in the image (the complement of the empty-fiber row KF2), together with the F_5 stage inverted in closed form on gamma != 0

families.paper_title: Exact fibers of the Keller counterexamples $F_4$, $F_5$ and $F_6$
families.paper_abstract: The Jacobian conjecture was refuted in dimension three in July 2026, and a general construction of Gao --- sweeping tangent direction fields on parametrised hypersurfaces --- has since produced Keller counterexamples in every dimension greater than two.  Four of those maps, $F_4,\dots,F_7$ in dimensions four and five, have generic fibers of $5$, $10$, $6$ and $12$ points, and their complete fiber stratifications are deferred there to a later version, the relevant Gr\"obner bases being out of reach.  We determine several fibers of these maps exactly and constrain every fiber of two of them.  The degree-ten fiber polynomial of $F_5$ has three leading coefficients that do not depend on the target; they force $\sum_i(r_i-\tfrac14)^2=0$ on any fiber whose roots are all real, so at most one real target can admit such a fiber, and that target is rational and explicit.  Over it the fiber of $F_5$ turns out to be \emph{empty}: every solution of the eliminated fiber system carries $\gamma=0$ and is deleted by the monomial twist.  The target is therefore an explicit rational point off the image of $F_5$, certified by a resultant B\'ezout identity $\mathcal{U}\mathcal{A}+\mathcal{V}\mathcal{B} =-750\,(4w_1-1)^{10}$ valid over every field of characteristic zero.  For $F_6$ the same mechanism gives $\sum_ir_i^2=1$ and $\sum_ir_i^3=\tfrac52$ for every target, which are incompatible over $\RR$: the fiber sextic never splits over the reals, so at most four of the six generic preimages are ever real.  Four is attained --- we exhibit a rational target of $F_6$ with four distinct rational preimages and prove that its fiber has exactly six points, the condition $\gamma\neq0$ at every root being verified exactly rather than numerically.  Finally we exhibit a rational target of $F_4$ with five distinct rational preimages, so that the geometric degree five is attained over $\QQ$. The certificates behind these statements --- the fiber evaluations, the B\'ezout identity and the two reality arguments --- are machine-checked in Lean~4.

families.title: Kite matrices over F_2 and the exact reach of the doubly-perfect construction of Gross-Goedicke (arXiv:2504.15401v2, line 2316) and of the Conjecture of Goedicke's dissertation
families.description: A *doubly perfect function* on the discrete phase space `V = Z_d^{2n}` is a unimodular `λ : V → ℂ` with no standard and no twisted auto-correlations. Rather's ansatz, as sharpened by Gross–Goedicke (`arXiv:2504.15401v2`), makes these the source of **two-unitaries** and hence of perfect tensors / AME states: `U_λ = Σ_a λ(a) |Φ_a⟩⟨Φ_a|` is two-unitary exactly when `λ` is doubly perfect, and a doubly perfect `λ` yields a two-unitary complex Hadamard matrix of order `d^n`.

statements.label: The kite matrix is symmetric, over any commutative ring
`det A = 1` over `F₂` for every `n`
`A + I` is singular over `F₂` exactly when `n ≡ 1 (mod 3)`
`A·A - I` is non-singular over `F₂` exactly when `n ≢ 1 (mod 3)` — the source's own `AB - I` form
The source's own criterion, decided for every `n`: `N = diag(A,A)` is symmetric with `N` and `N+J` both non-singular over `F₂` iff `n ≢ 1 (mod 3)`
Small-`n` certificates: for `n = 1…7` the kernel of `A+I` over `F₂`, by exhaustive `decide`, matches the general theorem
Negative controls: the datum does not work for every `n`; the exclusion is not `{1}` and is not a congruence mod 2
Non-vacuity: `n = 2` is a genuine positive instance, and the source's "`A`, `B` non-singular" hypothesis holds for every `n`
The anti-diagonal support is essential: for the triangular all-ones matrix `T`, `T + I` is singular over `F₂` for every `n ≥ 1`
Over `ℤ`, `A + I` is singular exactly when `n ≡ 4 (mod 6)`
Base-ring controls: at `n = 7` the matrix `A+I` is singular over `F₂` and non-singular over `ℤ`; the two rings differ exactly at `n ≡ 1 (mod 6)`
The Conjecture of Goedicke's dissertation, proved: for the single `2n × 2n` kite `N` and the standard symplectic `J`, `N` symmetric with `N` and `N+J` non-singular over `F₂` iff `n ≢ 1 (mod 3)`
Controls for the dissertation form: explicit kernel vector at `n = 4`, non-vacuity at `n = 2`, refutation of "works for every `n`"
Over `ℤ`, `A - I` is singular exactly when `n ≡ 1 (mod 6)`
The source's own condition, over `ℤ`: `A·A - I` is singular exactly when `n ≡ 1 (mod 3)`
Controls for the two integer factors: they never vanish simultaneously, and each vanishes somewhere

families.paper_title: Kite matrices over $\F_{2}$: the exact reach of a doubly perfect construction
families.paper_abstract: The \emph{kite matrix} $\kite_{n}$ is the $n\times n$ zero--one matrix whose $(i,j)$ entry is $1$ exactly when $i+j\le n+1$.  Gross and Goedicke, constructing doubly perfect functions on the discrete phase space $\Z_{2}^{2n}$ --- and through them two-unitary matrices and absolutely maximally entangled states --- record as a remark, supported by computer experiments, that the block-diagonal quadratic form built from two copies of $\kite_{n}$ appears to give such a function for every $n\not\equiv 1\pmod 3$; Goedicke's dissertation restates a sibling of that claim, for a single kite of order $2n$, as the only conjecture it puts forward, supported by a search over $n\in[500]$.  We prove both, in both directions and for every $n$.  The mechanism is that $\kite_{n}$ is the reversed partial-sum operator, so the kernel equation of $\kite_{n}+I$ differences to a two-term recursion whose transfer matrix is the signed Fibonacci matrix $M=\smat{1}{-1}{1}{0}$, and $M^{3}=-I$ over every commutative ring.  The orbit therefore has period six, and matching it against the closing condition leaves exactly the residues $n\equiv 1,4\pmod 6$; over $\F_{2}$ both are carried by the single factor $\kite_{n}+I$, and their union is $n\equiv 1\pmod 3$.  We also settle the same matrices over $\Z$, where the two residues split between the two factors of $\kite_{n}^{2}-I$: $\det(\kite_{n}+I)=0$ exactly when $n\equiv 4\pmod 6$ and $\det(\kite_{n}-I)=0$ exactly when $n\equiv 1\pmod 6$, so that $\det(\kite_{n}^{2}-I)=0$ exactly when $n\equiv 1\pmod 3$ over $\Z$ as well.  The modulus three is thus not a feature of characteristic two; what characteristic two does is merge the two factors. Every theorem below is machine-checked in Lean~4.

families.title: For which p is the Komalovics-Molnar distance d_p = (Tr((X+Y)/2 - X kappa_p Y))^{1/2} not a metric on the positive cone of M_2? (Komalovics-Molnar Problem 2, J. Math. Anal. Appl. 529 (2024) 127226; restated as Problem 1.2 of Teng Zhang, arXiv:2602.11922v1, whose Proposition 4.2 settles only p = 1/2)
families.description: Let `A` be a unital C\*-algebra with a faithful tracial positive linear functional `τ`, and `A_+` its positive cone. For `p > 0` and `A, B ∈ A_+`, Komálovics and Molnár (*On a parametric family of distance measures that includes the Hellinger and the Bures distances*, J. Math. Anal. Appl. **529** (2024), no. 2, Article 127226; "KM24") set
families.paper_title: Exact rational counterexamples to the triangle inequality\\ for the Komálovics--Molnár distances $d_{1/k}$, $2\le k\le 8$
families.paper_abstract: For $p>0$ and positive semidefinite matrices $X,Y$, Komálovics and Molnár set $X\kappa_pY=(X^{p/4}Y^{p/2}X^{p/4})^{1/p}$ and $d_p(X,Y)=\bigl(\Tr((X+Y)/2-X\kappa_pY)\bigr)^{1/2}$, a one-parameter family through the quantum Hellinger ($p=1$) and Bures ($p=2$) distances, and asked (their Problem~2) whether $d_p$ on $\M_n(\C)_+$, $n\ge2$, is a metric for each $1<p<2$ and fails to be one for each $0\le p<1$, reporting numerical evidence for both halves.  Zhang (arXiv:2602.11922) settled the single value $p=1/2$ by an explicit triple in $\M_2(\C)_{++}$.  We settle $p=1/3,1/4,1/5,1/6,1/7,1/8$, and give an independent, entirely rational witness at $p=1/2$.  The mechanism is that at $p=1/k$ the outer exponent is the natural number $k$: if $X=X_1^{4k}$ and $Y=Y_1^{4k}$ with $X_1,Y_1$ rational and positive semidefinite, then $\Tr(X\kappa_{1/k}Y)=\Tr\bigl((X_1Y_1^2X_1)^k\bigr)$ is a rational number produced by ring arithmetic alone, and the triangle inequality becomes a comparison of two rationals.  Each triple is built from one rational reflection $W$ of $\R^2$: $A_1=\diag(1,1/10)$, $B_1=WA_1W$, and $C_1$ a polynomial in $W$ with two rational eigenvalues chosen for each $k$, so that $d_p(A,C)=d_p(C,B)$ and the failure reads $d_p(A,B)^2-4\,d_p(A,C)^2>1/10$.  The same triples satisfy the triangle inequality at $p=1$, the failure is by a factor below $2$, and a rank-one triple satisfies the inequality at each $p=1/k$, as Komálovics and Molnár's Proposition~8 predicts.  All statements are verified in Lean~4 against \emph{Mathlib}. The half $1<p<2$ of Problem~2 is untouched here; we record, as an unproved reduction, a two-variable inequality which would settle the whole range $0<p<1$ at once.

families.title: Non-rotatable spherical knotoids: the 28-knotoid residue of arXiv:2603.06335 and the source's conjectured 'Non-rotatable' column
families.description: A **knotoid diagram** in `S²` is a generic immersion of `[0,1]` with transversal double points carrying over/under data; a **knotoid** is an equivalence class of such diagrams under Reidemeister moves I, II, III performed *away from the endpoints* (the two "forbidden moves" that pull an endpoint across a strand are not allowed). Turaev introduced them (arXiv:1002.4133v5 = Osaka J. Math. 49 (2012) 195–223) and defines exactly three **basic involutions** on knotoids in `S²`:
families.paper_title: Quandle colourings and the rotatability of spherical knotoids up to seven crossings
families.paper_abstract: Gabrov\v{s}ek and Cavicchioli have tabulated the $427$ prime spherical knotoids with at most seven crossings.  Their table divides them into $37$ rotatable and $390$ non-rotatable knotoids, but the non-rotatable column is marked as conjectural: for $28$ of the seven-crossing knotoids the five polynomial invariants they computed take the same value on the knotoid and on its rotation, and an exhaustive Reidemeister search neither identified the two nor separated them.  We show that all $28$ are non-rotatable, using the quandle colouring counts of G\"ug\"umc\"u and Nelson: Fox $3$-colourings separate $22$ of them from their rotations, and colourings by the Alexander quandle on $\Fp_3^{\,2}$ separate the remaining six.  Eight of the $28$ are also beyond the reach of Nikonov's homotopy index polynomial, the only other published invariant known to us that decides any of them.  The same counts show that two entries of the rotatable column are wrong: $5_{24}$ and $7_{288}$ are not rotatable, although $7_{288}$ is fixed by rotation composed with reversion.  The reason the polynomial invariants could not decide the question is that the rotation implemented in the tabulation is the composite of mirror reflection and Turaev's symmetry, under each of which the bracket polynomial is transformed by $A\mapsto A^{-1}$; we verify this on the published diagrams. Seven of the $390$ conjecturally non-rotatable knotoids remain open.  Every colouring count in this paper is checked from the published PD codes with the Lean~4 proof assistant.

families.title: The moment certificate behind c_2 >= 0.4263: the first Korenblum moment family settled in the kernel, and a two-constant replacement for the second
families.description: **Source.** arXiv:2607.17748v1, Frank Wikström (Lund), *Moment duality and an improved lower bound for Korenblum's constant*, primary math.CV, 20 July 2026 (v1 is the only version). Everything quoted here was read off the arXiv PDF of v1 (`pdftotext -layout`); the LaTeX e-print and the Zenodo software archive (doi 10.5281/zenodo.21446369) were read as well and are described in `family.json`. statements.label: The certificate measure of Table 1 read as exact rationals: the printed identity sum_{j=1}^8 w_j = 0.9900000000000000 = R holds exactly over the integers (sum of the 16-digit numerators = 99*10^14), t_1 = c^2 = 0.18173169 and t_8 = R = 0.99 exactly, and the 0-th atomic moment is exactly R -- so the atomic part has mass R, the Lebesgue part 1_[R,1] dt has mass 1-R, and mu is a probability measure on [c^2,1] with no atom at 1

THE FIRST MOMENT FAMILY IN FULL, kernel-bound and unconditional: A_k = sum_j w_j t_j^k - R^{k+1}/(k+1) >= 0 for EVERY k >= 0, equivalently (10^16 R)^{k+1} <= (k+1) sum_j W_j N_j^k over the integers, with the direct range 0 <= k <= 2183 by `decide` and the range k >= 2184 by the source's own atom argument (2185 w_8 = 0.9901373783170365 > R), so condition (3) of the source's Lemma 3.1 holds for this measure with no analytic input whatever

The source's printed figures recomputed as exact integer comparisons: A_23/(R^24/24) > 6.6452117503e-6 (the source's equation (15); the exact value is 6.6452117503638e-6) and the k = 1300 tail comparison 0.0000225 * 0.001 * 0.998^1300 > sum_j w_j t_j^1300, i.e. the source's printed 1.666810362143132e-9 > 1.611068196498003e-9 (exact values 1.6668103621431331e-9 and 1.6110681964980034e-9)

A TWO-CONSTANT CERTIFICATE FOR THE SECOND MOMENT FAMILY, replacing the source's 35 500-piece quadrature and its separate k >= 1300 window argument: if 1/G_c(sqrt t) >= lam(1-t) + kap(1-t)^2 on [R,1] with lam = 0.0225834 and kap = 0.01098, and beta_c(sqrt t_j) <= b_j at the eight nodes (the source's own printed enclosures), then B_k >= 0 for EVERY k >= 1 -- kernel-bound, by the integer comparison negB k <= posB k for 0 <= k <= 1072 and a uniform induction for k >= 1072 whose step is the rational inequality 100(k+1) >= 99(k+3). The certificate is also TIGHTER than the source's: at the source's own worst index k = 522 it gives B_522/(R^523/523) > 6.0214605308e-6, the exact margin being 6.606814769722e-6 against the source's certified 6.0214605308e-6

Both moment conditions of the source's Lemma 3.1 assembled for the measure of Table 1 at c = 0.4263: for every k >= 0, sum_j w_j t_j^k >= R^{k+1}/(k+1) unconditionally, and for every k >= 1, sum_j w_j b_j t_j^k <= int_R^1 t^k/G_c(sqrt t) dt + R^{k+1}/(k+1) under the two analytic hypotheses -- which is the entire computational content of the source's Theorem 1.1, c_2 >= 0.4263

Negative controls. (a) The quadratic term is not decoration: with kap = 0, i.e. from the linear bound 1/G_c(sqrt t) >= lam(1-t) alone, the certificate FAILS at k = 522 (kernel-refuted), so the two-constant shape is minimal. (b) The source's threshold k >= 2184 for its own atom argument is sharp: 2184 w_8 < R < 2185 w_8. (c) The first family is genuinely tight, not slack: A_23/(R^24/24) < 10^-5. (d) The hypotheses of the criterion are simultaneously satisfiable, so the conditional theorem is not vacuous

MEASUREMENT (not formalised): the nine analytic inputs. Re-derivation of the source's product formula (1) at 120 decimal digits with truncation N = 140 reproduces all seven printed beta enclosures exactly (each printed 15-digit bound is the correctly rounded-up value); the ratio (1/G_c(sqrt t))/(1-t) decreases monotonically on [R,1) from 0.02269328947638196 at t = R to the limit 0.0225834855605, and ((1/G_c(sqrt t))/(1-t) - 0.0225834855...)/(1-t) stays above 0.010980, which is where lam = 0.0225834 and kap = 0.01098 come from; the worst observed ratio (1/G_c(sqrt t))/(lam(1-t)+kap(1-t)^2) over 561 geometric samples down to 1-t = 1e-30 and 4001 uniform samples on [R,0.9999] is 1.000000024820942

MEASUREMENT (parked): re-optimising the measure to push c above 0.4263. A max-min-margin linear program over a 160-node grid on [c^2,R] with 2600 moment rows, bisected on c for R in {0.99, 0.995, 0.999, 0.9995, 0.9999}, returns c = 0.4263 in every case with a residual margin of -1.3e-5 to -1.6e-5, i.e. it does not even reproduce the source's own feasible point (whose true margin is +6.6e-6). The cause is measured: in float64 the quantity 1-K_c(sqrt t)^2 that G_c needs behaves like 5.1e-4 (1-t)^2 and is below the resolution of 1-K for 1-t < 1e-5, so the integrals int_R^1 t^k/G_c dt are wrong for large k

families.paper_title: The moment certificate behind $c_2 \ge 0.4263$: the first Korenblum moment family settled in the kernel, and a two-constant replacement for the second
families.paper_abstract: Korenblum's constant $c_2$ is the supremum of the $c\in(0,1)$ such that $|f|\le|g|$ on $c<|z|<1$ forces $\norm{f}_{A^2}\le\norm{g}_{A^2}$ in the Bergman space of the unit disk. Wikstr\"om (arXiv:2607.17748) proved $c_2\ge0.4263$ through a moment-duality criterion: $c$ is admissible as soon as a probability measure $\mu$ on $[c^2,1]$ with $\mu(\{1\})=0$ satisfies $\int t^k\,d\mu\ge 1/(k+1)$ for $k\ge0$ and $\int\beta_c(\sqrt t)\,t^k\,d\mu\le 1/(k+1)$ for $k\ge1$, where $\beta_c=1-1/G_c$ is built from Wang's annular constant.  The certificate is one explicit measure --- eight atoms with sixteen-digit rational data and Lebesgue measure on $[R,1]$, $R=0.99$ --- for which the two conditions become two families of scalar inequalities $A_k\ge0$ ($k\ge0$) and $B_k\ge0$ ($k\ge1$), certified in the source by Arb ball arithmetic.  We examine that certificate.  (1)~$A_k\ge0$ contains no analysis: it is a comparison of two integers, and we prove it for every $k\ge0$ inside the Lean~4 kernel with no hypothesis --- kernel evaluation for $k\le2183$, and the source's own atom argument $2185\,w_8>R$ for $k\ge2184$.  (2)~For $B_k$ we give a two-constant certificate: \emph{if} $1/G_c(\sqrt t)\ge\lambda(1-t)+\kappa(1-t)^2$ on $[R,1]$ with $\lambda=0.0225834$, $\kappa=0.01098$, and $\beta_c(\sqrt{t_j})\le b_j$ at the eight nodes ($b_j$ the source's printed enclosures), then $B_k\ge0$ for every $k\ge1$.  The passage from these nine real inequalities to the whole family is kernel-checked --- $k\le1072$ by one integer comparison per index, $k\ge1072$ by an induction whose step is $100(k+1)\ge99(k+3)$ --- and it replaces the source's roughly $185\,500$ interval enclosures and its separate $k\ge1300$ argument. The nine inequalities themselves are hypotheses: they are explicit arguments of the formal theorem, they are proved nowhere in this paper, and a reader must not take them as established here; we record only a $120$-digit numerical scan supporting them.  The certificate is also tighter than the source's at the source's worst index: our lower bound for $B_{522}$ is $6.6068\e{-6}\cdot R^{523}/523$, against the $6.0214605308\e{-6}\cdot R^{523}/523$ that the source's quadrature certifies --- a comparison of two lower bounds, not of two values of $B_{522}$. (3)~Negative controls: the quadratic term cannot be dropped ($\kappa=0$ fails at $k=522$), the source's threshold $k\ge2184$ is sharp ($2184\,w_8<R<2185\,w_8$), and the first family is genuinely tight ($A_{23}/(R^{24}/24)<10^{-5}$).  Nothing in the formal development mentions the Bergman space: the step from moments to norms is the source's Lemma~3.1, which we take as prose.

families.title: Exact optimal Korobov generating parameters for the quasi-uniformity criterion lambda_1(Lambda_a) * lambda_1(Lambda_a^perp)
families.description: Founded 2026-09-07 from `arXiv:2602.15390v1`, *Space-filling lattice designs for computer experiments* (stat.ME; a QMC design paper by Naoki Sakai and Takashi Goda, SIAM class file, code at `https://github.com/Naokikiki/Quasi-Uniform-Points`). Lean under `LeanProblemSpec/KorobovQuasiunif/`.
families.paper_title: Exact optimal Korobov generating parameters\\ for the quasi-uniformity criterion $\lambda_1(\Lambda_a)\,\lambda_1(\Lambda_a^{\perp})$
families.paper_abstract: For a prime $N$, a dimension $d$ and a parameter $a\in\{1,\dots,N-1\}$, the Korobov lattice point set with generating vector $(1,a,a^2,\dots,a^{d-1})\bmod N$ is the intersection of the lattice $\Lat_a=\tfrac1N(1,a,\dots,a^{d-1})\Z+\Z^d$ with $[0,1)^d$. Sakai and Goda (arXiv:2602.15390) propose to choose $a$ by maximising the product $\lam(\Lat_a)\lam(\Lat_a^\perp)$ of the first successive minima of $\Lat_a$ and of its dual, since $d\sqrt d/(\lam(\Lat_a)\lam(\Lat_a^\perp))$ bounds the mesh ratio of the design, and they print a table of ``optimal generating parameters'' $a^*$ for $18$ primes $N\le 524287$ and $d\in\{2,3,5,7\}$, computed by scoring each $a$ with the shortest vectors of LLL-reduced bases in place of the successive minima.  We compute the criterion exactly, by complete enumeration and without any lattice reduction, for the $40$ cells with $N\le 2039$, and certify the result in Lean~4.  The exact smallest maximiser and the maximal value are given for every cell.  Exactly three printed entries, at $(N,d)=(251,7)$, $(509,3)$ and $(2039,5)$, are strictly suboptimal for the criterion the table is stated to optimise; the other $37$ attain the maximum, $15$ of them as the smallest maximiser that the published algorithm returns as written, and $22$ as another maximiser, which the invariance of the criterion under $a\mapsto N-a$ and $a\mapsto a^{-1}\bmod N$ explains in all but one case.  As a control against the classical two-dimensional construction, the Fibonacci parameter $a=F_{m-1}$ at $N=F_m$ attains the exact maximum at the Fibonacci primes $13$ and $89$ but not at $233$ or $1597$.

families.title: Problem 17.32 of the Kourovka Notebook: the Cayley-Hamilton analogue for free groups, and the ranks and exponents at which it fails
families.description: Problem **17.32** of the *Kourovka Notebook* (No. 21, Novosibirsk 2026 = arXiv:1401.0300v46, source file `21tkt.tex` line 9316), proposed by **O. V. Bogopolski**:

statements.label: Kourovka Problem 17.32 has a negative answer at rank two: there are w in F_2 and phi in Aut F_2 with <w, phi w, phi^2 w> = F_2 and <w, phi w> != F_2; equivalently not CayleyHamiltonAnalogue 2 (FreeGroup (Fin 2))
The generation half at rank two: phi(w) = y x^2, phi^2(w) = xyxyx = w^2 x, x = w^-2 phi^2(w), y = x^-1 w, hence <w, phi(w), phi^2(w)> = F_2
The properness half at rank two: pi : F_2 -> S_3 with pi(x) = (1 2 3), pi(y) = (2 3) has pi(w) = pi(phi(w)) = (1 2), so <w, phi(w)> is a proper subgroup of F_2
phi(x) = y x, phi(y) = x is an automorphism of F_2 with inverse phi^-1(x) = y, phi^-1(y) = x y^-1, and phi is not the identity
The pair skipping phi(w) generates: <w, phi^2(w)> = F_2

Controls for the rank-two counterexample: <x, phi(x)> = F_2 (properness is a property of the word, not of phi); pi(phi^2(w)) is not in the point stabiliser (the S_3 test does not overreach); and for every commutative group A and every homomorphism rho : F_2 -> A, <rho(w), rho(phi(w))> = rho(F_2), so no abelian quotient can detect the properness
The witnessing quotient is not degenerate: pi : F_2 -> S_3 is surjective

Kourovka Problem 17.32 also fails at rank three: for F_3 = <a,b,c>, phi(a) = b a, phi(b) = a, phi(c) = c and w = a b c, one has <w, phi w, phi^2 w> != F_3 -- witnessed by rho : F_3 onto S_3 with a -> (2 3), b -> (1 2), c -> (1 2), whose values (2 3), 1, 1 all fix a letter that rho(b) moves -- while <w, phi w, phi^2 w, phi^3 w> = F_3 by explicit words in e_i = w (phi^i w)^-1; equivalently not CayleyHamiltonAnalogue 3 (FreeGroup (Fin 3))

Kourovka Problem 17.32 also fails at rank four: for F_4 = <a,b,c,d>, phi(a) = b a, phi(b) = a, phi(c) = d, phi(d) = c and w = a b c, one has <w, phi w, phi^2 w, phi^3 w> != F_4 -- witnessed by rho : F_4 -> S_4 with a, d -> (1 2)(3 4) and b, c -> (1 3 2), whose image lies in A_4 (equality of the image with A_4 checked outside Lean) -- while <w, ..., phi^4 w> = F_4; and the failure is about the initial segment, since <w, phi w, phi^2 w, phi^4 w> already generates F_4

For the sources' rank-two data (w = xy, phi(x) = y x, phi(y) = x), <w, phi^k(w)> = F_2 if and only if k = 2, for every k >= 1: phi acts on the abelianisation by the Fibonacci matrix, so w and phi^k(w) have exponent-sum vectors (1,1) and (F(k+2), F(k+1)) and span a subgroup of Z^2 of index F(k); for k >= 3 the Lean witness is the linear form chi_k with chi_k(x) = F(k+1), chi_k(y) = -F(k+2), whose values on w and phi^k(w) are -F(k) and 0 while chi_k(x) = F(k+1) is coprime to F(k) >= 2

families.paper_title: The Cayley--Hamilton analogue for free groups fails in ranks three and four, and only one power works in rank two
families.paper_abstract: Problem~17.32 of the \emph{Kourovka Notebook}, proposed by O.~V.~Bogopolski, asks whether the free group $F_n$ obeys the Cayley--Hamilton pattern: if $w \in F_n$ and $\varphi \in \Aut F_n$ satisfy $\gen{w, \varphi(w), \dots, \varphi^{n}(w)} = F_n$, must already $\gen{w, \varphi(w), \dots, \varphi^{n-1}(w)} = F_n$?  Two independent solutions appeared in August 2026 and are recorded in the Notebook's answer line; both refute the assertion at $n = 2$ and say nothing about any larger rank.  We give explicit counterexamples at $n = 3$ and $n = 4$.  Both are built from the rank-two automorphism $\varphi(x) = yx$, $\varphi(y) = x$ by adjoining generators that $\varphi$ either fixes (rank three) or transposes (rank four), and each is certified on both sides: explicit words exhibiting every free generator, and an explicit homomorphism to a permutation group under which the initial segment of the orbit fixes a point that some free generator moves.  We also settle, for the rank-two data of the two published solutions, every exponent at once: $\gen{w, \varphi^{k}(w)} = F_2$ holds if and only if $k = 2$, the index of the abelianised pair being the Fibonacci number $\Fib(k)$; the two published solutions record only the cases $k = 1$ and $k = 2$.  A complementary observation explains why the rank-two failure needs a non-abelian witness at all: no abelian quotient can detect it.  Every theorem, proposition, corollary and lemma below is machine-checked in Lean~4 against Mathlib, by kernel evaluation only; Section~\ref{sec:verif} says exactly what is and what is not formalised.  Whether Problem~17.32 fails for every $n \ge 2$ remains open.

families.title: Kourovka Problem 21.97 restricted to abelian groups: the image of |Aut(G)|/|G|, its denominators (exactly the cyclic numbers) and its odd part
families.description: Write `α(G) = |Aut(G)|/|G|`. Problem **21.97** of the *Kourovka Notebook* (No. 21, Novosibirsk 2026 = arXiv:1401.0300v46, source file `21tkt.tex` line 14115), proposed by **M. Tărnăuceanu**:

statements.label: Compute-first gate, in the kernel: the closed form p^(Ev L) * Nv p L agrees with the literal Hillar-Rhea product of Proposition 2.1 of arXiv:2603.29299v2 for every partition of every n <= 6 and every p in {2,3,5,7} (120 cases, by decide)

Ev L >= -1 for every well-formed type list, and Ev L <= 0 exactly for the trivial group, the cyclic p-groups, Z/p x Z/p, Z/p x Z/p^f (f >= 2) and (Z/p)^3 -- the exponent form of the source's Proposition 2.3
The reduced denominator of |Aut(A)|/|A| is the product of the primes p with Ev(type p) = -1 whose p divides no other block's prime-to-p part (AbType.rat_den, via Rat.den_div_eq_of_coprime)
McCulloch's Theorem 1.1 in the model: the reduced denominator of |Aut(A)|/|A| is squarefree

NEW: the reduced denominator b of |Aut(A)|/|A| always satisfies gcd(b, phi(b)) = 1 -- b is a cyclic number (OEIS A003277), i.e. an order at which every group is cyclic. Strictly sharpens McCulloch's Theorem 1.1: 6 and 21 are squarefree but are not denominators
Converse of KA5: every b with gcd(b, phi(b)) = 1 really is a reduced denominator, realized by the cyclic group Z/b, whose ratio phi(b)/b is already in lowest terms

Counting automorphisms from generator images: for GenData G k (k generators plus a normal form), Fintype.card (MulAut G) equals the number of k-tuples of images whose induced map is an injective homomorphism -- a |G|^k search in place of Mathlib's |G|! one

NEW: the complete odd slice of the abelian image. If |Aut(A)|/|A| has odd numerator and odd denominator then it is 1, or 21, or (q-1)/(2q) or 3(q-1)/(2q) for a prime q = 3 mod 4; in particular the only odd INTEGERS in the image are 1 and 21, the latter realized by (Z/2)^3 with |Aut| = |GL(3,2)| = 168
Bridge rows: Mathlib's own automorphism counts Fintype.card (MulAut G) = 4, 8, 168, 8 for C_8, C_2 x C_4, (Z/2)^3, Z/15, and the four resulting ratios 1/2, 1, 21, 8/15 agree with the model's pratio
Nonabelian controls: Fintype.card (MulAut (QuaternionGroup 2)) = 24, so |Aut(Q_8)|/|Q_8| = 3 is an odd prime; and Fintype.card (MulAut (DihedralGroup 4)) = 8, ratio 1
McCulloch's Theorem 1.3 ('no odd prime can equal |Aut(G)|/|G| for a finite abelian G') derived as a corollary of KA8

Negative controls: 21 and 6 are squarefree but are provably NOT reduced denominators (so KA5 is not a restatement of squarefreeness); 3 and 15 ARE denominators, realized by Z/6 and Z/15; and the (q-1)/(2q) branch of KA8 is attained, at q = 3 by Z/6 with ratio 1/3

MEASUREMENT: exhaustive GAP scan of alpha(G) = |Aut(G)|/|G| over all 10,177 groups of every order <= 319 except order 256. Every reduced denominator is a cyclic number (0 exceptions), so neither McCulloch's squarefree obstruction nor its sharpening KA5 is detectably abelian-specific at these orders, although Sureaux's positive answer to 21.97 forces both to fail at some larger order. The odd integers realized at order <= 255 are {1,3,5,7,9,11,13,15,21,23,27,29,33,35,39,41,51,53,55,63} against {1,21} for abelian groups; the smallest witness for an odd prime is Q_8 = SmallGroup(8,4) with alpha = 3
Realization of the two infinite odd families: alpha(Z/2q) = (q-1)/(2q) and alpha((Z/2)^2 x Z/q) = 3(q-1)/(2q), and both are quotients of two odd integers, for every prime q = 3 mod 4

NEW: the odd slice of the abelian image, exactly. A rational r is |Aut(A)|/|A| for a finite abelian A AND has odd reduced numerator and odd reduced denominator if and only if r = 1, r = 21, or r = (q-1)/(2q) or 3(q-1)/(2q) for a prime q = 3 mod 4. This completes row KA8's forward implication to a biconditional

Controls and a gap corollary: no odd-over-odd automorphism ratio of a finite abelian group lies strictly between 1/2 and 1; in particular 3/5 and 5/7 are not |Aut(A)|/|A| for any finite abelian A, although 5 and 7 are cyclic numbers realized by Z/5 and Z/7; and alpha(Z/10) = 2/5 is not odd-over-odd, so the congruence q = 3 mod 4 in KA15 is not decoration

MEASUREMENT correcting KA13's census size: the exhaustive GAP scan of alpha(G) over every order <= 319 except 256 covers 8,570 groups -- 7,012 of order <= 255 and 1,558 of orders 257..319 -- not 10,177. On a fresh re-run: 0 non-cyclic-number denominators; odd integers realized {1,3,5,7,9,11,13,15,21,23,27,29,33,35,39,41,51,53,55,63} for orders <= 255 and {1,3,7,9,11,15,33,35,39,65,69,75} for orders 257..319; and 0 groups of any kind with an odd-over-odd alpha strictly between 1/2 and 1

families.paper_title: Denominators and odd values of the automorphism ratio\\ of a finite abelian group
families.paper_abstract: For a finite group $G$ put $\al(G)=|\Aut(G)|/|G|$.  Problem 21.97 of the Kourovka Notebook asks whether every positive rational is of this form; the answer is yes, by a recent theorem of Sureaux, which also settles the nilpotent case.  For \emph{abelian} groups the answer is no, and the exact image is an open project of McCulloch, who proved that the reduced denominator of $\al(A)$ is squarefree and that no odd prime occurs.  We settle two pieces of that project.  First, the set of reduced denominators of $\al(A)$, as $A$ runs over all finite abelian groups, is exactly the set of \emph{cyclic numbers} $\{b:\gcd(b,\ph(b))=1\}$ --- the orders at which every group is cyclic, OEIS A003277. This is strictly sharper than squarefreeness: $6$ and $21$ are squarefree and are not denominators.  Second, we determine the odd part of the image exactly: an element of the abelian image has odd numerator and odd denominator if and only if it is $1$, or $21$, or $(q-1)/(2q)$ or $3(q-1)/(2q)$ for a prime $q\equiv3\pmod4$.  In particular the only odd \emph{integers} in the abelian image are $1$ and $21$, the latter realized by $(\Z/2)^3$ with $|\Aut|=|\GL(3,2)|=168$; this contains McCulloch's theorem that no odd prime occurs, and is strictly stronger.  Both infinite families do occur, realized by $\Z/2q$ and by $(\Z/2)^2\times\Z/q$ for $q\equiv3\pmod4$.  The list has a gap in it --- no odd-over-odd abelian value lies strictly between $1/2$ and $1$ --- and the gap excludes $3/5$ and $5/7$ from the abelian image outright, although $5$ and $7$ are cyclic numbers and both do occur as denominators.  Both theorems are short arguments built on a proposition of McCulloch, and we say so plainly; what we claim is that the statements are new and that they answer a clean part of his question.  Every statement we prove is machine-checked in Lean~4; the classical formula for $|\Aut(A)|$ that they rest on is taken as given, and every step resting on a finite exhaustive search is named together with the size of that search.

families.title: The census of finite Krasner hyperfields, and which of them are quotients of finite fields
families.description: A **hyperfield** (Krasner) is `(F, ⊞, ·, 0, 1)` where `(F \ {0}, ·)` is an abelian group, `(F, ⊞, 0)` is a *canonical hypergroup* — a commutative, associative, reversible hyperoperation `F × F → P*(F)` with `0` as identity and unique additive inverses — multiplication distributes over `⊞`, and `0` is absorbing. This is Definition 1 of arXiv:2608.03625, following Krasner (1957, 1983).

statements.label: The complete census of Krasner hyperfields of orders 3 to 7 as explicit tables: 5, 7, 27 (= 16 over C_4 plus 11 over C_2 x C_2), 16 and 277 isomorphism classes, each list verified to consist of hyperfields, to be in canonical form under the automorphism group of the multiplicative group, and to be pairwise non-isomorphic

There are exactly 178 isomorphism classes of Krasner hyperfields of order 8 (equivalently A343596(8) = 178): 178 explicit pairwise non-isomorphic tables, and an exhaustive search over all 128^4 = 268435456 admissible presentations showing there are no others

The finite-field quotient classes at orders 3 and 4, located inside the census: exactly 4 of the 5 hyperfields of order 3 and exactly 4 of the 7 of order 4 are quotients F_q/G_r, each realised by an explicit finite field whose irreducibility and primitivity certificate is checked in Lean

Baker-Jin open question (1), finite-field half: of the 27 isomorphism classes of hyperfields of order 5, exactly 9 are quotients of finite fields and 18 are not -- the 9 sit among the 16 classes with multiplicative group C_4, and none of the 11 classes with multiplicative group C_2 x C_2 is a quotient, because F_q^x/G is cyclic
The same matching at orders 6, 7 and 8: exactly 7 of the 16 hyperfields of order 6, exactly 15 of the 277 of order 7, and exactly 9 of the 178 of order 8 are quotients of finite fields

Negative controls for the census and the quotient matching: a table failing the axioms outright, a commutative reversible table with unique inverses that fails associativity, a 179th order-8 class refuted, a 177-class census shown incomplete, a reducible modulus rejected by the field certificate, and C_2 x C_2 shown not isomorphic to C_4

Independent reproduction of both printed tables of arXiv:2608.03625: N_r^emp = 6, 17, 42, 102, 278, 492, 762 with 2, 4, 7, 7, 18, 8, 18 exceptional prime powers for r = 2..8, and Q_r^fin = 2, 4, 4, 9, 7, 15 for r = 1..6

Independent confirmation of the values the source's companion repository added after the arXiv v1: N_r^emp = 578, 1182, 1410, 1742 with 15, 27, 11, 41 exceptions for r = 9, 10, 11, 12, and Q_r^fin = 9, 17, 14, 27, 9, 36 for r = 7..12

Cost and collision measurements: the order-8 census is a 2.7 x 10^8-candidate search that a proved single reversibility instance cuts 519-fold to 777000 nodes; the order-9 census (multiplicative group C_8) is 1.3 x 10^11 candidates and is parked

families.paper_title: There are exactly $178$ Krasner hyperfields of order eight, and which hyperfields of order at most eight are quotients of finite fields
families.paper_abstract: A Krasner hyperfield is a field-like structure whose addition is multivalued.  Let $H_n$ denote the number of isomorphism classes of hyperfields of order $n$.  The values $H_2, \dots, H_6 = 2, 5, 7, 27, 16$ are due to Ameri, Eyvazi and Ho\v{s}kov\'a-Mayerov\'a and $H_7 = 277$ to Massouros and Massouros.  We compute the next value: $H_8 = 178$.  The lower bound is a list of $178$ pairwise non-isomorphic tables; the upper bound is an exhaustive search over all $128^4 = 268\,435\,456$ tables admitted by an elementary reduction, which is stated and proved by hand in full below.  In the notation of the On-Line Encyclopedia of Integer Sequences this is $A343596(8) = 178$, the published entry stopping at order $6$.  We then determine, for every order $n$ with $3 \le n \le 8$, exactly which of the $H_n$ isomorphism classes are quotients $\FF_q/G$ of a finite field by a subgroup of its multiplicative group.  The counts are $4$ of $5$, $4$ of $7$, $9$ of $27$, $7$ of $16$, $15$ of $277$ and $9$ of $178$ at orders $3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8$; the first two reproduce a theorem of Baker and Jin.  The order-$5$ case answers the finite-field half of Baker and Jin's open question~(1): the nine quotient classes all have multiplicative group $C_4$, and none of the eleven classes with multiplicative group $C_2 \times C_2$ is a quotient of a finite field.  The infinite-field half of their question is untouched and remains open. The counts $9, 7, 15$ at orders $5, 6, 7$ agree with counts obtained by Linzi by a different route; what is new for those orders is the identification of \emph{which} classes they are.  The numbered results below are machine-checked in Lean~4.  Section~\ref{sec:verif} says which of them rest on exhaustive computation, how large each search is, and which steps of the argument are made by hand rather than by machine.

families.title: The exact worst-case upper tail under a bounded fourth moment: sharp values and exact dual certificates for the fifteen cells arXiv:2607.05226 could not certify
families.description: For a real random variable `X` with `E X = 0`, `E X² = 1` and `E X⁴ ≤ κ`, how large can `P(X ≥ t)` be? Two classes are studied here, both formalised over honest probability measures on `ℝ` (Bochner integrals, with integrability of `x⁴` part of the definition — without it `∫ x⁴ ∂μ` silently returns `0` for a heavy-tailed law and the moment constraint would be vacuous):

statements.label: Weak duality for the four-moment upper-tail problem over probability measures on R, with integrability of x^4 in the definition of the class
Zelen's branch (t^2 - g*t - 1 > 0) is sharp for the class with fourth moment only BOUNDED, with an exact perfect-square dual certificate q = (u/u(t))^2
The ten rational cells among the thirteen skewness-pinned instances arXiv:2607.05226 reports as uncertified: 4/9, 4/45, 3/7, 3/391, 7/15, 19/159, 16/77, 1/74, 7/51, 4/65

The central branch (t^2 - g*t - 1 < 0) is sharp, with the Hermite quartic certificate; nonnegativity of that certificate is automatic whenever r1 < t < r2
The three skewness-pinned cells below Zelen's branch: (10-sqrt 14)/14, (5-sqrt 5)/10, (4761-307*sqrt 69)/7314

The source paper's algebraic system (S) for Regime IIIb collapses to the single relation 2c(c-b) = (b+t)^2, and its assertion that any solution yields V1 exactly is then proved by weak duality plus attainment
An exact rational point of Regime IIIb: at (t,kappa) = (3/10, 2151/400) the maximum is 1025/1176, and all three closed forms of the source paper's map are refuted there

The source paper's single `fail` cell (t,kappa) = (1/2,3/2): the maximum is the value the collapsed system takes at the root of 16b^6+208b^5+768b^4+476b^3-849b^2-508b+316 in (0.8028,0.8029), sandwiched strictly between the Regime IIIa plateau value 2/3 and 0.6674
Negative controls at a solved cell: 1/2 too large, 2/5 too small, and the class non-empty
Zelen's branch hypothesis is not decoration: one cell outside it has zelenValue = 3/7, and 3/7 is provably not the maximum there
The bound(eps) cell (t,kappa) = (1/2,2) upgraded to an exact certificate; the sandwich (0.7262, 0.7263) confirms the sextic value the source paper publishes
The bound(eps) cell (t,kappa) = (1/2,3) upgraded to an exact certificate: the root of 16b^6+208b^5+768b^4+284b^3-2097b^2-1132b+1756 in (1.1900614,1.1900615), sandwiched in (0.7896, 0.7897)

The three-moment cell arXiv:2607.05226 reports as `fail` without ever naming it, identified from its artifact repository and solved exactly: for X >= 0 with E X = 1, E X^2 = 2, E X^3 = 9/2, max P(X >= 5) = 1/95

Machine-checked erratum: Lemma 2.2 of arXiv:2312.04925 (Kwan-Wigderson), attributed to Zelen 1954 eq. (12), is false as printed for a != 0; refuted at E[Y^4] = 2, a = 1/2, together with the sharp value there

The solution variety of the collapsed system (S) of Regime IIIb is a rational surface: the explicit two-parameter polynomial parameterisation t = r(m^2+2m-2), b = r(2-m^2), c = 2r, proved onto, with the exact maximum at every point of an explicit region

An exact rational curve inside Regime IIIb: for 9 <= 425t^2 and 25t^2 <= 3, max P(X >= t) at kurtosis budget (2125t^4+1422t^2)/27 is exactly (375t^2-3)/(392t^2); the rational locus of IIIb is infinite and is not confined to one curve

Controls for the rational surface: Cantelli's bound for the whole class with its square certificate; the 25t^2 <= 3 window is load-bearing; all three closed forms of the source's map refuted at EVERY point of the curve, with the contact structure

The source's unproven global-solvability clause for Regime IIIb, proved on an explicit two-dimensional region: for t in [1/5,3/10] and every kappa between the two endpoint budgets, (S) has a solution with threshold t and budget kappa, and the supremum is attained

families.paper_title: Kusner's conjecture fails at a second exponent:\\ a certificate for 58 equilateral points in $\ell_6^{56}$
families.paper_abstract: An equilateral set in a normed space is a set of points at pairwise equal distance, and $\eq(\ell_p^n)$ denotes the largest cardinality of one.  Kusner conjectured that $\eq(\ell_p^n)=n+1$ for $2<p<\infty$.  Chalmers has recently refuted this at $p=5$, by exhibiting $58$ points in $\lp{5}$ as the unique zero, inside an explicit box, of a polynomial system with dyadic coefficients; his paper records that it is not known how far that configuration extends in the exponent, and observes that its verification scheme uses the oddness of $5$.  We address both points.  Continued in the exponent inside the square slice that Chalmers uses to make the system square, the solution branch is a closed loop of width $0.0367$ around $p=5$ and reaches no other integer; but the equilateral condition on $58$ points in $\mathbb{R}^{56}$ is $1653$ equations in $3249$ unknowns, so that fold belongs to the slice and not to the problem.  Continuing in the full space and refining in exact arithmetic, we obtain a Newton--Kantorovich certificate at the \emph{even} exponent $6$, on Chalmers' own frozen set and variable order: a centre with dyadic coordinates, a preconditioner, preconditioned residual $\eta=4.4320\times10^{-16}$ and contraction factor $q=2.3563\times10^{-4}$ at box radius $2^{-33}$, so that the Kantorovich test clears by a factor $4176$, and still passes at a box radius $4244$ times the one used at $p=5$.  The five arithmetic claims of the certificate, the radius window, the constants and the negative controls are checked by the Lean~4 kernel.  Because the exponent is even, the sign-constancy hypothesis that the $p=5$ scheme needs disappears entirely.  Subject to the classical reduction of the contraction hypotheses to those arithmetic claims---which is carried out here by hand and is \emph{not} machine-checked, and which we flag at every use---this gives $\eq(\ell_6^{56})\ge 58>57$: Kusner's conjecture fails at a second exponent, and at an even one, where it was open and the best bound available was $\eq(\ell_6^{56})\le169$.

families.paper_title: The degree-246 minimax constant of $(1+t^3)^{1/3}$:\\ its minimal polynomial, and its factorisation over $\Q(\cbrt)$
families.paper_abstract: Let $k$ be the first interior alternation point of the best degree-2 minimax (absolute-error) approximation of $(1+t^3)^{1/3}$ on $[0,1]$.  Filipovi\'c, G\'eraud-Stewart, Naccache and Veli\v{c}kovi\'c (arXiv:2607.22664) prove that $k$ is algebraic of degree $246$ over $\Q$, do not print its minimal polynomial $P$, and conjecture (their Remark~3) that $P$ ``factors as three conjugate degree-82 irreducible polynomials over $\Q(2^{1/3})$, and that $\mathrm{Gal}=S_{82}\rtimes C_3$'', a computation they report as exceeding an hour in SageMath.  We recompute $P$ from the authors' own equiripple system (calibrated by reproducing, coefficient for coefficient, the degree-20 polynomial they print for $(1+t^2)^{1/2}$), and factor it over $\K=\Q(\cbrt)$.  The conjecture is false as stated: $P=f\cdot g$ with $f,g\in\K[x]$ of degrees $82$ and $164$ \textup{(}irreducible over $\K$ by PARI/GP\textup{)}.  What survives is the norm reading, $P=\Nm_{\K/\Q}(f) = f\,f^{\sigma}f^{\sigma^2}$ over the Galois closure: writing $f=f_A+f_B\cbrt+f_C\sqrt[3]{4}$ with $f_A,f_B,f_C\in\Z[x]$, the identity $f_A^3+2f_B^3+4f_C^3-6f_Af_Bf_C=P$ holds exactly in $\Z[x]$, and $g=f^{\sigma}f^{\sigma^2}$.  Both identities, on the explicit integer coefficients, are certified inside Lean~4 (the factorisation for every commutative ring with a cube root of $2$).  We also show that no $\Q$-irreducible polynomial can split into three conjugate factors inside $\Q(\cbrt)[x]$, and that $\Gal(P/\Q)$ is neither $S_{82}\rtimes C_3$ nor $S_{82}\wr C_3$.  Two printed numbers of the source are corrected: its 38-decimal headline constant for the Euclidean case is right to 20 decimals only (certified: it is not a root of the source's own degree-20 polynomial), and its $L_4$ constant $t_1\approx0.3275$ matches neither formulation of its problem.  The computation reported as blocked takes $0.4$\,s in PARI/GP.

families.paper_title: The Laguerre Gram matrix of Gon\c{c}alves' sharpened Strichartz inequality: a closed factorisation, and the spectral conjecture through $S=60$
families.paper_abstract: Let $L_n$ be the Laguerre polynomial normalised by $L_n(0)=1$, so that the $L_n$ are orthonormal for $e^{-x}\,dx$ on $(0,\infty)$, and let \[ Q(a,b,c,d)=\int_0^\infty L_a(x/2)L_b(x/2)L_c(x/2)L_d(x/2)\,e^{-x}\,dx , \] and let $Q_S=\bigl[\,Q(a,S-a,c,S-c)\,\bigr]_{a,c=0}^{S}$. Gon\c{c}alves introduced $Q_S$ to prove a sharpened Strichartz inequality for radial data in $\RR^2$, showed that it is positive semi-definite, doubly stochastic and strictly positive, and closed his paper with two numerical conjectures about it: that the eigenvalues of $Q_S$ are exactly $\lambda(n)=\binom{2n}{n}^2 16^{-n}$ for $n\le\lfloor S/2\rfloor$, each simple, together with $0$ of multiplicity $\lceil S/2\rceil$; and that the least entry of $Q_S$ is $Q(\lfloor S/2\rfloor,\lceil S/2\rceil,S,0)$.  He reports verifying both for $S\le30$.  No formula for $Q(a,b,c,d)$ is given there, and we have found none in the literature.  We give one on the diagonal slice: writing $\Xm_S[a,j]=\binom{S-2j}{a-j}$, $\Hm_S[i,j]=\binom{2(S-i-j)}{S-i-j}$ and $\Dm_S=\mathrm{diag}\bigl((-4)^i\binom{S-i}{i}\bigr)$ for $0\le i,j\le\lfloor S/2\rfloor$, \[ 2^{2S}\,Q_S \;=\; \Xm_S\,\Dm_S\Hm_S\Dm_S\,\Xm_S^{\top} , \] an identity we derive from the two-variable generating function of the Laguerre linearisation coefficients.  It compresses the characteristic polynomial to $\charp_{Q_S}(X)=X^{\lceil S/2\rceil}\cdot\charp_{4^{-S}\Mm_S^2}(X)$ with $\Mm_S=\Dm_S\Hm_S$, so that Gon\c{c}alves' eigenvalue conjecture at $S$ becomes a statement about a matrix of half the size whose eigenvalues are the square roots $(-1)^n\binom{2n}{n}2^{S-2n}$.  Instances of the identity and of the compression are machine-checked, and so is the eigenvalue conjecture in full, with multiplicities, for every $S$ with $31\le S\le60$, thirty values beyond the range reported in the source; likewise the minimum-entry conjecture over the same range, together with the observation --- stated nowhere, and not new mathematics --- that the minimum is attained exactly on the $4$- or $8$-element symmetry orbit of $(\lfloor S/2\rfloor,0)$.  Every statement below is formally verified in Lean~4 except where the text says otherwise.

families.paper_title: Finitely supported witnesses for the sharp discrete Hardy constant on $\Z^N$: $C(9)<12$ and $C(10)<59/4$
families.paper_abstract: For $N\ge3$ let $C(N)$ be the optimal constant in the nearest-neighbour Hardy inequality $\sum_{j}\sum_{n\in\Z^N}|u(n+e_j)-u(n)|^2\ge C(N)\sum_{n\ne0}|u(n)|^2/|n|^2$ over finitely supported $u$ with $u(0)=0$, and let $A_N=(N-2)^2/4$ be the continuum coefficient. Lizama (arXiv:2608.30831) proved $C(N)\le A_N$ for all $N$, $C(3)=A_3$, $C(4)=A_4$, $C(N)<A_N$ for $N=9,10$ and $C(N)\le 3N-\sqrt{N^2+8N-8}$ for $N\ge11$; his dimension-nine argument uses an infinitely supported Gaussian trial function estimated through Jacobi theta functions, and he proves that his finitely supported coordinate Ritz ladder cannot cross $A_9$ at all. We show that a trial function depending on $n$ only through $|n|^2$ turns both quadratic forms into finite sums over the representation numbers $r_N(m)=\#\{n\in\Z^N:|n|^2=m\}$, so that a finitely supported witness is one rational inequality in integers. This yields, with integer profiles supported in $1\le|n|^2\le M$: $C(9)<49/4=A_9$ at $M=36$; $C(9)<121/10$ at $M=144$; $C(9)<12$ at $M=576$; $C(10)<59/4$ at $M=16$ (sixteen integers, against the previously documented $16$); and $C(11)<17$, $C(12)<96/5$, $C(13)<213/10$, $C(14)<117/5$ at $M=64$, each below the best value derivable from the coordinate ladder. Every certificate is checked by the Lean~4 kernel by evaluation on integers. All results are upper bounds; the open equality $C(N)=A_N$ for $5\le N\le8$ is untouched, and we report numerical evidence (not proofs) in its favour: the smallest eigenvalue of $\cE_N-A_N\cD_N$ on balls converges to a negative constant for $N=9,10$ but stays positive and decays like $R^{-2}$ for $N=5,\dots,8$.

families.paper_title: A three-term null vector for $L_{T}+G_{T}$:\\ half of a conjecture on $-1$ as a generalized\\ eigenvalue of LCM matrices to GCD matrices
families.paper_abstract: For a finite set $T$ of positive integers let $L_{T}=(\lcm(t_{i},t_{j}))$ and $G_{T}=(\gcd(t_{i},t_{j}))$ be the LCM and GCD matrices on $T$.  Merikoski, Haukkanen, Sasaki and Tossavainen conjecture that, on $T=\{1,\dots,n\}$ with $n>3$, the number $-1$ is a generalized eigenvalue of $L_{T}$ to $G_{T}$ exactly when the binary expansion of $n$ begins with $10$; their evidence is a floating-point generalized eigensolver run to $n=1000$.  Since $-1$ is a generalized eigenvalue precisely when $\det(L_{T}+G_{T})=0$, this is a singularity statement about the integer matrix with entries $\lcm(i,j)+\gcd(i,j)$.  We prove the ``if'' half for every $n$, with no computation, by exhibiting a null vector: writing $f(a,b)=\lcm(a,b)+\gcd(a,b)$, the three-term identity $2f(2^{s},j)-3f(2^{s+1},j)+f(2^{s+2},j)=0$ holds for all $1\le j<3\cdot 2^{s+1}$, so $2e_{2^{s}}-3e_{2^{s+1}}+e_{2^{s+2}}$ annihilates $L_{T}+G_{T}$ on the whole block $2^{s+2}\le n<3\cdot 2^{s+1}$, which is exactly the set of $n$ whose binary expansion begins $10$.  The bound is sharp, and more is true: $2e_{m}-3e_{2m}+e_{4m}$ annihilates $L_{T}+G_{T}$ (for $4m\le n$) if and only if $m$ is a power of two and $n<6m$, which is why the answer to the conjecture is a condition on binary digits.  The same identity is not about intervals at all, and yields an infinite family of index sets, of every size, on which $-1$ is a generalized eigenvalue: it suffices that $T$ contain $2^{s},2^{s+1},2^{s+2}$ and that $2^{s+1}$ be the only element of $T$ of $2$-adic valuation exactly $s+1$.  This settles, for that family, the general-$T$ case taken up in \S4 of the source.  The ``only if'' half of the conjecture remains open; we record an exact verification of the full biconditional for $4\le n\le 47$ inside the formal development and, outside it, for $2\le n\le 1000$.  Two small errors in the published text are identified and corrected.  Every theorem below is machine-checked in Lean~4; \S\ref{sec:verif} says exactly what the machine checks.

families.paper_abstract: Lee and Saez (arXiv:1512.03793) prove that the harmonic polynomial $p + \bar q$ built from $S(z) = i z^n$ and $T(z) = i (z+1)^{n-1}(z-(n-1))$ by $p = S + T$, $q = S - T$ has exactly $n^2 - 2n + 2 + 4\kmax(n)$ zeros, where $\kmax(n)$ is the largest $k \le n/2$ with $(n-2)\cotan\frac{(2k-1)\pi}{2n-4} - n \cotan\frac{\pi k}{n} > 0$, and they tabulate the count for $4 \le n \le 35$.  We certify $\kmax(n)$ for every $4 \le n \le 200$ by rational interval enclosures of $\sin$ at rational multiples of $\pi$, driven through the paper's own identity $(n-2)\cotan\theta_1 - n\cotan\theta_2 = ((n-1)\sin(\theta_2-\theta_1) - \sin(\theta_1+\theta_2))/(\sin\theta_1\sin\theta_2)$.  Four of the thirty-two printed cells contradict the theorem printed one page earlier: at $n = 7, 15, 22, 30$ the table gives $37, 201, 450, 854$ where the formula gives $41, 205, 454, 858$; the journal version (Comput.\ Methods Funct.\ Theory 17 (2017) 139--149) prints the same thirty-two values.  The formula is right --- at $n = 7$ all $41$ zeros are located numerically --- and the printed row coincides, at every cell, with $n^2 - 2n + 2 + 4\lfloor 0.13237\, n\rfloor$, $0.13237$ being the paper's own rounded asymptotic constant.  We record the exact set of $n \le 200$ at which $\kmax$ increases, $7, 15, 22, 30, 37, 45, 52, 60, \dots, 196$, against the paper's asymptotic $\kmax(n) = (\tfrac14 - \tfrac{X}{2\pi})\, n + O(1)$ with $X = \cos X$, and extend the table to $n = 200$.  Every statement is checked in Lean~4 with Mathlib: the correction, the jump set and the extended table are kernel-checked facts about a certified table of values, and the tie between that table and the real sine and cosine passes through a single \lean{native\_decide} evaluation of $9{,}998$ rational interval enclosures, so the correction is kernel-bound through \lean{native\_decide}.

families.title: Kalmynin's Lev-Sonn primes: the third and fourth ones (p = 25293378613 and 74857799381), the exhaustive classification to alpha <= 300000, and a correction to the printed witness for p = 41
families.description: A. Kalmynin, *On additive irreducibility of multiplicative subgroups*, [arXiv:2504.10202](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.10202) (v1 2025-04-14, **v2 2025-05-28**, the latest, whose arXiv comment reads "misprints corrected"), closes with this Problem, quoted verbatim from the v2 e-print:

statements.label: The two Lev-Sonn primes the source reports, formalised in its own notation: p = 13 at (alpha,n) = (3,3) and p = 41; and n = 3 is the only witness at alpha = 3
CORRECTION: the source's printed witness for p = 41 is (alpha,n) = (5,5) and is wrong -- n = 5 fails, n = 4 holds, and n = 4 is the unique witness in 1 < n <= 5
A third Lev-Sonn prime: p = 25293378613 = 2*112458*112457+1 at (alpha,n) = (112458, 76000), a congruence between binomial coefficients with upper argument 12646801763
The first four Lev-Sonn primes: exhaustively, the only alpha <= 300000 carrying one are 3, 5, 112458, 193466 -- 34603 primes of the form 2alpha(alpha-1)+1 tested, against the 586 of the source

Negative controls: a prime of the shape that is not Lev-Sonn (alpha = 2, p = 5); the too-small claim '13 and 41 are the only ones' refuted; and the primality clause shown non-vacuous at alpha = 4, where the congruence holds but p = 25 is composite
The source's own count reproduced inside Lean: exactly 586 primes of the form 2alpha(alpha-1)+1 with alpha <= 3000, and restricted to that range the sweep returns exactly the source's two primes
MEASUREMENT: Lean's Nat falls off a 2^63 cliff, and splitting the modular multiplication so every intermediate stays below it is 9.4x on the same sweep window

The Lev-Sonn condition with alpha eliminated from the numerator: the congruence at n = j+1 holds if and only if prod_{i=1}^{j}(2i+1) == prod_{i=1}^{j}(2alpha+2i) mod p, i.e. (2j+1)!! == 2^j (alpha+j)!/alpha!

families.paper_title: The third and fourth Lev--Sonn primes
families.paper_abstract: Kalmynin calls a prime $p$ a \emph{Lev--Sonn prime} if $p=2\alpha(\alpha-1)+1$ and $\binom{\alpha^2-1}{n-1+\alpha}\equiv(-1)^{n-1}\binom{\alpha^2-1}{\alpha}\pmod p$ for some $n$ with $1<n\le\alpha$, and asks whether there are infinitely many.  His search over $\alpha\le 3000$ found two, $p=13$ and $p=41$.  We exhibit the next two, \[ p=25\,293\,378\,613\quad(\alpha=112\,458),\qquad p=74\,857\,799\,381\quad(\alpha=193\,466), \] and prove that they are the third and the fourth: for every $\alpha$ with $2\le\alpha\le 300\,000$ the number $2\alpha(\alpha-1)+1$ is a Lev--Sonn prime if and only if $\alpha\in\{3,5,112\,458,193\,466\}$.  The congruence witnessing the first of the two new primes relates binomial coefficients with $616\,862$ and $991\,481$ decimal digits, and the one witnessing the second relates larger ones; the tool that makes them decidable is an exact telescoping identity whose correction factors are units modulo $p$, and which replaces the pair of binomial coefficients by two products of $n-1$ linear factors.  A substitution in it removes $\alpha$ from one side entirely and turns the condition into $(2j+1)!!\equiv 2^{j}(\alpha+j)!/\alpha!\pmod p$ with $j=n-1$.  We also correct the witness printed for $p=41$: the pair $(\alpha,n)=(5,5)$ recorded in the source is not a witness, $(5,4)$ is, and it is the only one.  Every theorem, proposition and lemma below is machine-checked in Lean~4.

families.title: k(L) for simple Lie algebras over finite fields: k(sl_3(F_2)) = 3, the first value of Kishnani-Singh's one-and-a-half generation number

statements.label: The object: sl_3(F_2) pinned to the trace-zero 3x3 matrices over ZMod 2
k(sl_3(F_2)) <= 3: every non-zero element is the first entry of a generating triple
k(sl_3(F_2)) > 2: E_01 lies in no generating pair, certified by ten maximal proper subalgebras that cover the algebra
k(sl_3(F_2)) = 3, both halves in one statement
The exceptional set is exactly 49 elements, proved in both directions
What the 49 are: A^2 = 0 or A^2 = A, equivalently ad(a)^3 = ad(a)^2
Gate: sl_3(F_2) is 2-generated, as Cantor-Jezernik-Zozaya say it is

Over an algebraically closed field of characteristic 2: k(sl_3(F-bar_2)) >= 3, so Bois's characteristic hypothesis cannot be relaxed for type A

families.paper_title: One-and-a-half generation of simple Lie algebras over finite fields: the value $k(\sll_3(\FF_2))=3$
families.paper_abstract: For a simple Lie algebra $L$ over a finite field, Kishnani and Singh define $k(L)$ to be the least $k$ such that \emph{every} non-zero $a\in L$ occurs as the first entry of some generating $k$-tuple, and observe that no clear answer for $k(L)$ seems to be known; the number is the number of variables in their theorem on images of Lie polynomials.  We determine one value: \[ k(\sll_3(\FF_2)) \;=\; 3 . \] The upper bound is a generating triple for each of the $255$ non-zero elements.  The lower bound is structural rather than a report that a search failed: ten proper Lie subalgebras of $\sll_3(\FF_2)$, each containing the root element $E_{01}$, already cover the algebra, so every pair containing $E_{01}$ lies inside a proper subalgebra.  We also determine the exceptional set exactly.  Precisely $49$ of the $255$ non-zero elements lie in no generating pair, namely the $21$ elements with $A^2=0$ and the $28$ with $A^2=A$, equivalently the $a$ with $\ad(a)^3=\ad(a)^2$; the remaining $206$ each have an explicit partner.  The mechanism is characteristic two: if $A^2=\lambda A$ then $\ad(A)^2=\lambda\ad(A)$, because the cross term $2AXA$ vanishes.  In particular $\sll_3(\FF_2)$ is $2$-generated, as Cantor, Jezernik and Zozaya proved, and is nevertheless not one-and-a-half generated: the two properties come apart at the smallest algebra where they can be compared.  All statements are machine-checked in Lean~4.

Since a decomposition of 1 into pairwise orthogonal primitive central idempotents is unique, this pins the block count: F_2[Z3 x Z3], F_2[Z6 x Z3], F_2[Z3 x Z6], F_2[Z12 x Z3] and F_2[Z6 x Z6] have five blocks each, and F_2[Z3 x A_4] has exactly TWO, e_omega = t + t^2 and e_1 = 1 + t + t^2 of the central Z3, of central dimensions 8 and 4
