Z3 x A_4 is not one lift host of [[18,8,2]] but two. A lift needs a surjection pi : Z3 x A_4 -> Z3 x Z3 with kernel V_4, and the two hosts differ in how the five base packets fuse into the two blocks: on the AXIS host (pi(t) = x, the map families/lp-inheritance used) e_omega collects base blocks 0, 1, 3 -- including BOTH live packets -- and e_1 collects the two dead ones 2, 4; on the DIAGONAL host (pi(t) = xy) the two live packets are split, e_omega getting 0, 2, 3 and e_1 getting 1, 4. Both maps are certified homomorphisms with kernel exactly {0,1,2,3} = V_4

The block-resolved census of all 256 gauge-fixed lifts of [[18,8,2]] to Z3 x A_4 along the AXIS quotient: profiles (k', r_tau; (k_e, r_tau_e) per block) = (8,0; (8,0),(0,0)) x 108, (12,2; (12,2),(0,0)) x 72, (16,4; (16,4),(0,0)) x 72, (32,8; (32,8),(0,0)) x 4. The block-resolved census of all 256 gauge-fixed lifts of [[18,8,2]] to Z3 x A_4 along the DIAGONAL quotient, which nobody had enumerated: (12,2; (8,0),(4,2)) x 144, (16,4; (12,2),(4,2)) x 96, (32,8; (20,4),(12,4)) x 16. NO lift inherits nothing -- r_tau >= 2 in all 256, against 108 zero-inheritance lifts on the axis host -- and in the largest class (144 of 256) the WHOLE of the inheritance sits in the e_1 block, a block the axis host cannot reach

Over ALL 48 surjections pi : Z3 x A_4 -> Z3 x Z3 with kernel V_4 (the invertible 2x2 matrices over F_3 acting on (Z3 x A_4)/V_4), the block-resolved census of the 256 gauge-fixed lifts of [[18,8,2]] takes exactly TWO values, 24 maps each; and the invariant that separates them is where the centre goes -- the axis census occurs exactly when pi(t) lies on a coordinate axis of Z3 x Z3 (one of x, x^2, y, y^2) and the diagonal census exactly when pi(t) is one of xy, xy^2, x^2y, x^2y^2

Dead blocks stay dead: if K is a CENTRAL subgroup of H of 2-power order with H/K = G, and e is a block idempotent of F_2[H] whose image Pi(e) in F_2[G] is a sum of base blocks all of which are exact at C_1 (k_e = 0), then the lift is exact at C_1 on the e-block, so k'_e = 0. Proof: the ideals I_K^j F_2[H] are two-sided (K normal) and the filtration is finite (K a 2-group, so I_K is nilpotent); the lifted boundary maps reduce to the base ones modulo I_K, so the graded pieces of the lift complex are copies of the base complex tensored with I_K^j / I_K^{j+1}, which for central K is a trivial F_2[G]-bimodule; e acts on each graded piece as Pi(e); and a filtered complex whose graded pieces are exact at C_1 is exact at C_1, by descending induction on the long exact sequences of 0 -> F^{j+1} -> F^j -> gr_j -> 0

arXiv:2607.28621v1 prints TWO `[[72,8,8]]` codes and they are NOT the same code: the minimum weight of the stabiliser group of the `Z_9` clustered cyclic lift (TABLE III) is EXACTLY 8 on both CSS sides — no `X`- and no `Z`-stabiliser of weight `<= 7`, every check row of weight exactly 8 — whereas every one of the 1024 gauge-fixed index-4 lifts of `[[18,8,2]]` (256 over each of `Z_12 x Z_3`, `Z_6 x Z_6` and the two `Z_3 x A_4` hosts), TABLE VII's `[[72,8,8]]` and all 18 of BS15 included, has ALL of its check rows of weight exactly 6. The minimum weight of the `X`-stabiliser group is a permutation invariant of a CSS code and the global Hadamard only exchanges the two sides, so no permutation of the 72 qubits, even composed with the Hadamard, carries one code onto the other — and the CC `[[72,8,8]]` is not permutation-equivalent to ANY two-block group-algebra code `LP[a,b]` over any group of order 36 with `|supp a| = |supp b| = 3`, a class that also contains the twisted-torus `[[72,8,8]]` of arXiv:2503.03827

Negative controls for the clustered cyclic layer. Not vacuous: `stabMin8` is FALSE for TABLE VII's `Z_12 x Z_3` `[[72,8,8]]` — its weight-6 check rows are stabilisers, so the `noDep7` exhaustion does fire — while the rank identity `rank H_X + dim ker H_X = 72` holds there, so that `false` comes from the dependency search and not from a degenerate null basis. Too small: `rawDExactOk` at `d = 6` is false for the `Z_9` CC code and at `d = 2` for the `[[24,8,3]]` base. Too large: `lowOkR` refuses a claimed distance outside `{2, 3, 4, 6, 8}` rather than defaulting to true, in particular at `d = 9 = |K| d`, and `rawDExactOk` at `d = 9` is false

The eighteen `[[72,8,8]]` gauge-fixed `Z_12 x Z_3` lifts of `[[18,8,2]]` (row BS15) are ONE code. `eighteenIdx = [19, 21, 28, 33, 36, 47, 81, 84, 95, 115, 117, 124, 163, 165, 172, 177, 180, 191]` is exactly the set of positions where `z12z3Dist` certifies `d = 8`; those 18 gauge-fixed lifts are pairwise distinct as pairs `(supp a, supp b)`; and for each of them an explicit permutation of the 72 qubits carries TABLE VII's lift (position 36, `a = {0,3,24}`, `b = {0,10,2}`) onto it, mapping the multiset of the 36 `H_X` rows onto the multiset of `H_X` rows and likewise for `H_Z` — an isomorphism of Tanner graphs, not merely an equality of row spaces. Each permutation is `left h |-> left phi(h+u)`, `right h |-> right phi(h+v)` for `phi` in `Aut(Z_12 x Z_3) = Aut(Z_4) x GL(2,F_3)` (order 96) and `u` in `supp a`, `v` in `supp b`. So up to relabelling the qubits there is exactly ONE `[[72,8,8]]` gauge-fixed `Z_12 x Z_3` lift of `[[18,8,2]]`, and BS15's count 18 is a count of gauge-fixed labellings, not of codes

Negative controls for the permutation certificate. Not vacuous: the identity array passes `permArrOk`, and `codeIsoOk` identifies TABLE VII's lift with itself, so the test can succeed. Too small: exchanging the images of qubits 0 and 1 in the first certificate makes `codeIsoOk` false, and the identity array with position 1 overwritten by 0 is rejected by `permArrOk` — so the certificate really checks that the map is a bijection and that it matches the rows. Too large: none of the 18 permutations carries TABLE VII's lift onto gauge-fixed lift 0, whose certified distance is 2

The exact minimum distance of EVERY gauge-fixed index-3 lift of the `[[18,8,2]]` base code of arXiv:2607.28621v1 Eq. (68) / TABLE VII to an ABELIAN host. Four of the five groups of order 27 surject onto `Z_3 x Z_3` (all but `Z_27`), and the abelian two are `Z_9 x Z_3` (quotient `basePi 9 3`, kernel `{0,9,18}`) and `Z_3^3` (the projection `pi333` forgetting the third coordinate, kernel `{0,1,2}`), both certified homomorphisms onto `Z_3 x Z_3` with every gauge-fixed lift a chain map over the base; the two NON-abelian hosts `(Z_3 x Z_3) : Z_3` and `Z_9 : Z_3`, which arXiv:2607.28621v1 TABLE VI also lists for this base as `[[54,8,6]]`, are NOT covered. Each abelian host carries 81 gauge-fixed lifts. On `Z_9 x Z_3`: `d = 2` for 27 and `d = 6` for 54. On `Z_3^3`: `d = 2` for 45 and `d = 6` for 36. NO such lift has distance 4 — the distance is 2 or 6 and nothing between, against all four values `2, 4, 6, 8` at index 4 — and BOTH abelian hosts reach the top `d' = |K| d = 6`, 90 of the 162 lifts doing so, against 18 of 1024 at index 4 and on the cyclic-kernel host only. Every certificate is exact both ways: the logical parity checks number `k` on both CSS sides, no logical operator of either type has weight `< d`, and an explicit `X`-logical of weight `d` is exhibited

The `(k', d)` census of the two ABELIAN index-3 hosts of `[[18,8,2]]` (the two non-abelian hosts of order 27 are not covered), and the placement of TABLE VII's two printed lifts inside it: `Z_9 x Z_3` gives `(k', d, count) = (8,2,27) (8,6,54)` — the host gains NO logical qubits at all, `k' = k = 8` for all 81 lifts — while `Z_3^3` gives `(8,2,36) (8,6,36) (24,2,9)`, so 9 of its 81 lifts reach the largest value in the census, `k' = 24 = |K| k` and every one of those 9 has distance 2. TABLE VII's `Z_9 x Z_3` row `1 + x + x^2`, `1 + x^3 y + y^2` is lift 3 of the enumeration and its `Z_3 x Z_3 x Z_3` row `1 + x^2 + xz`, `1 + y^2 + yz` is lift 30; both are `[[54,8,6]]`, the printed value. So at index 3, as at index 4, the classes with `k' > k` never get past the bottom of the distance range, and the number of logical qubits determines the distance on `Z_9 x Z_3` only in the trivial sense that there is one class [corrected 2026-09-09, hygiene 11d: was so 9 of its 81 lifts reach the maximum `k' = 24 = |K| k`]

Negative controls for the index-3 census. Not vacuous: `dExactOk` at `d = 6` is false on the first `Z_9 x Z_3` gauge-fixed lift, whose certified distance is 2, and at `d = 8` on the second, whose certified distance is 6 — so a lift is not silently promoted one rung. Too large: "every abelian-host index-3 lift reaches `d' = |K| d = 6`" is false, 27 of the 81 `Z_9 x Z_3` lifts and 45 of the 81 `Z_3^3` lifts carrying a weight-2 logical. Too small: `pi333` with a single image changed fails `homOk`, so the host is pinned by the homomorphism test and not by the shape of the array

families.paper_title: Block spectroscopy of non-abelian lifts:\\ the two $\Z_3\times A_4$ hosts of $\code{18}{8}{2}$
families.paper_abstract: A two-block group-algebra code over a finite group $H$ has check matrices $H_X=[L_a\mid R_b]$ and $H_Z=[R_b^{T}\mid L_a^{T}]$.  For abelian $H$, Lee's logical spectroscopy resolves its logical space into packets, the primitive central idempotents of $\F_2[H]$.  For non-abelian $H$ neither regular action of $H$ commutes with both check matrices, so there is no packet decomposition; the centre of $\F_2[H]$ still acts, and its primitive idempotents---the blocks of $\F_2[H]$---resolve the logical space of the code, and the inheritance map of a lift, block by block.  We carry this out for every index-2 and index-4 lift of the $\code{18}{8}{2}$ code of Hirasaki and Lee.  Group theory leaves four host groups, the index-2 one reached by a coordinate reduction in either coordinate; one of the four, $\Z_3\times A_4$, is non-abelian, and $\F_2[\Z_3\times A_4]$ has exactly two blocks against the five packets of the base.  A lift to $\Z_3\times A_4$ needs a surjection onto $\Z_3\times\Z_3$ with kernel $V_4$, and there are $48$ of them.  Over all $48$ the block-resolved census of the $256$ gauge-fixed lifts takes exactly two values, $24:24$, according to whether the image of the central generator lies on a coordinate axis or on a diagonal of $\Z_3\times\Z_3$: along an axis map $108$ lifts inherit nothing from the base and the second block is dead in all $256$; along a diagonal map no lift inherits nothing, and in $144$ of the $256$ the whole of the inheritance sits in the block that the axis map never reaches.  On the distance side, all $768$ gauge-fixed index-4 lifts with elementary abelian kernel along the three quotient maps we use carry a logical operator of weight at most $6$, so none reaches $|K|\,d=8$, the distance Table~VII of Hirasaki--Lee prints for the cyclic-kernel lift; and two non-abelian $\code{72}{12}{6}$ codes and a non-abelian $\code{72}{8}{4}$ are certified exactly.  Every enumerated statement is checked by the Lean~4 kernel.  This version adds the exact minimum distance of every one of the $1024$ gauge-fixed index-4 lifts along the four quotient maps used here.  The lower bounds of the first version were column tests, which bound the minimum weight of the whole kernel of a check matrix; that kernel contains the rows of the other check matrix, of weight $6$, so no such test can reach $d\ge7$.  Quotienting the stabilisers out through $k$ logical parity checks and meeting in the middle does reach it, exactly.  On the cyclic-kernel host $\Z_{12}\times\Z_3$ the $256$ lifts have $d=2,4,6,8$ for $31,117,90,18$ of them: exactly $18$ attain $|K|\,d=8$, none has $d=7$, and the $\code{72}{8}{8}$ of Table~VII of Hirasaki--Lee, printed there without a certificate, is one of the $18$; a code with the same parameters over the same group is printed, likewise without a witness, by Liang, Liu, Song and Chen as a generalised toric code on a twisted torus.  On the three elementary-abelian-kernel hosts the $768$ lifts split $31/189/36$, $76/108/72$ and $112/0/144$ over $d=2/4/6$.  Crossed with the number $k'$ of logical qubits, the distance is determined by $k'$ on both $\Z_3\times A_4$ hosts and on $\Z_6\times\Z_6$ outside one class, and not at all on $\Z_{12}\times\Z_3$, whose single class $k'=8$ carries all four distances; the $18$ $\code{72}{8}{8}$ codes maximise $kd^2/n=512/72$ over all $1024$ lifts.  The statements of the first version are reproduced unchanged.  This version adds three things.  (1)~The second $\code{72}{8}{8}$ of Hirasaki and Lee, the $\Z_9$ lift in their Table~III of the $\code{24}{8}{3}$ clustered cyclic code of Gu et al., is certified exactly, base and lift ($d'=8<9=|K|\,d$), and shown to be a different code from the $\Z_{12}\times\Z_3$ one: its minimum stabiliser weight is $8$ on both sides against at most $6$ for every index-4 lift, an invariant under permutations of the qubits composed with the global Hadamard.  (2)~The $18$ lifts of distance $8$ are one code up to relabelling, by explicit permutations; the $18$ counted gauge-fixed labellings.  (3)~The index-3 census over the two abelian groups of order $27$, one quotient map each: all $162$ gauge-fixed lifts are certified exactly, $27/54$ and $45/36$ at $d=2/6$, none at $d=4$, both hosts reaching $|K|\,d=6$.  On $\Z_9\times\Z_3$ that census is one of two, over the $48$ maps, $24$ each; on $\Z_3^{\,3}$ it is the only one over all $624$.  The two non-abelian groups of order $27$ are not covered.

families.title: E(n,m), the maximum number of linear extensions of an n-element poset with at most m antichains (Question 8 of Johnson-Leader-Russell): the exact table for n <= 9, the poset case of their tower-of-cubes Conjectures 5 and 6 verified for n <= 9, and a 23-element poset refuting Conjecture 6 eleven elements below the published counterexample
families.description: For a finite poset `P`:

statements.label: The exact table E(n,m) = max{e(P) : |P| = n, a(P) <= m} for every n <= 7 and every m, as the profile arrays prof3..prof7, kernel-checked over all naturally labelled posets (96,428 at n = 7), with the enumeration proved complete (mem_dseqs)

The poset case of JLR Conjectures 5 and 6 holds for n <= 7: at every tower size (n/t)(2^t-1)+1 and every generalised-tower size 1+a(2^t-1)+b(2^(t+1)-1), E(n,|T|) = prod b_i! exactly, attained by the tower

An explicit 23-element poset with a(P) = 6111 <= 6143 and e(P) = 21271190434790400 > 11!*12!: JLR Conjecture 6 fails for posets already at n = 23, eleven elements below the published counterexample, so the smallest such n satisfies 9 < n* <= 23
The 34-element counterexample poset of arXiv:2604.05661v2 verified from the poset itself: a(P) = 260553 < 2^18 - 1 and e(P) = 131576429145341435860520294400 > (17!)^2

An explicit 33-element poset -- the 9-regular circulant bipartite poset on 16+16 elements with one maximal element on top -- with a(P) = 172127 <= 196607 and e(P) = 8486591273961280582975488000 > 16!*17!

Negative controls: the O(a(P)*n) ideal counter agrees with the 2^n scan on every poset with n <= 6; the tower compared against is a realised 23-element poset with exactly (6143, 11!*12!); a(P) <= 6110 is false; the bucket order at that size has strictly fewer linear extensions

The exact table E(n,m) and the tower cells for n = 8 and n = 9 (2,800,472 and 116,473,461 naturally labelled posets): the tower is extremal at every tower and generalised-tower size, and the first m at which no bucket order attains E(n,m) is 14 (n = 8) and 15 (n = 9), continuing the pattern floor(3n/2)+2 from n = 3

The first m at which no bucket order with at most m antichains attains E(n,m) is floor(3n/2)+2 for every 3 <= n <= 7 (m = 6, 8, 9, 11, 12), with the n = 3 witness: the poset 0 < 2 with 1 isolated has 6 antichains and 3 linear extensions while every bucket order with at most 6 antichains has at most 2

The exact table E(10,m) over all 6,855,780,268 naturally labelled posets on 10 elements: the tower is extremal at every tower and generalised-tower size (m = 11,...,16, 21, 30, 63, 1024), and the first m with no bucket-order maximiser is 17 = floor(3*10/2)+2; with LA3 this brackets the smallest n at which a poset beats a (generalised) tower at its own size as 10 < n* <= 23, against the published n* <= 34

families.paper_title: The maximum number of linear extensions of an $n$-element poset with at most $m$ antichains: the exact table for $n\le 7$, the poset case of the Johnson--Leader--Russell tower conjectures for small $n$, and a $23$-element poset that beats a generalised tower of cubes
families.paper_abstract: For a finite poset $P$ let $a(P)$ be its number of antichains (equivalently, of order ideals; the empty one included) and $e(P)$ its number of linear extensions, and let $E(n,m)=\max\{e(P): |P|=n,\ a(P)\le m\}$.  Johnson, Leader and Russell asked (Question~8 of \emph{Set systems containing many maximal chains}) for this maximum; it is the quantity the recent space--time tradeoffs for permutation problems optimise over, and no table of its values has appeared in the literature.  We determine $E(n,m)$ exactly for every $n\le 7$ and every $m$ by an exhaustive census of all naturally labelled posets, and record the same table for $n=8,9,10$ (up to $6\,855\,780\,268$ posets) as computer data.  At every size a tower or generalised tower of cubes can have, the tower is extremal among posets for $n\le 7$ (and, as data, for $n\le 10$): the poset case of Johnson--Leader--Russell's Conjectures~5 and~6 holds there, although both conjectures are false for general set systems and Jabal Ameli, Nederlof and Wang have refuted Conjecture~5 with a $34$-element poset.  Below the tower sizes the picture changes early: the first $m$ at which no bucket order attains $E(n,m)$ is $\lfloor 3n/2\rfloor+2$ for $3\le n\le 7$ (and, as data, up to $n=10$).  Finally we exhibit a $23$-element poset with $6111\le 6143$ antichains and $21\,271\,190\,434\,790\,400>11!\,12!$ linear extensions, and a $33$-element one with $172\,127\le 196\,607$ antichains and more than $16!\,17!$ linear extensions, so the poset case of Conjecture~6 fails at $n=23$, eleven elements below the published counterexample; the least such $n$ satisfies $7<n^\ast\le 23$ (and $10<n^\ast\le 23$ on the computer data).  Every theorem is checked in Lean~4 from the definitions.

families.title: The Shifted Lonely Runner Conjecture: exact loneliness gaps, and the counterexamples that refute it

families.paper_title: Explicit shift vectors and certified loneliness gaps\\ for the Shifted Lonely Runner Conjecture
families.paper_abstract: For integer speeds $v=(v_1,\dots,v_n)$ and shifts $s=(s_1,\dots,s_n)$, the loneliness gap $\gamma(v;s)=\sup_{t\in\mathbb{R}}\min_{i}\dist{s_i+v_it}$ measures how far from every integer the whole pack of runners can simultaneously be pushed; the Shifted Lonely Runner Conjecture asserts $\gamma(v;s)\ge 1/(n+1)$ whenever the $|v_i|$ are distinct and nonzero. Blanco, Criado and Santos recently refuted it for every $n$ with $5\le n\le 17$, but their paper prints an attaining shift vector for only three instances, and their companion code stops at $n=13$.  We give explicit rational shift vectors $s^{(n)}\in[0,1)^n$ for every $n$ with $7\le n\le 17$, together with the exact value of $\gamma((1,2,\dots,n);s^{(n)})$ and an exact rational maximising time. At $n=7$ and $n=8$ the vectors reach the published optimal values $25/214$ and $1/10$; for $9\le n\le 14$ they certify $\gmin(1,\dots,n)\le 1/(n+2)$; and for $n=15,16,17$ --- the range where no exact value of $\gmin$ is published --- they certify $\gmin(1,\dots,n)\le 2/(2n+3)$, that is, $2/33$, $2/35$ and $2/37$. Every gap is proved on both sides by a purely integral certificate: a finite interval cover for the upper bound and one rational time for the lower bound. We also reproduce, as upper bounds with explicit witnesses, the published values of $\gmin(1,\dots,n)$ for $5\le n\le 13$, and give the corresponding maximising times, which neither source prints. Every one of these certificates has been checked by the Lean~4 kernel, together with the soundness of the certificate scheme itself and the controls that make it falsifiable.

families.title: Eq. (D2) of arXiv:2607.28621 evaluated exactly: the coherent information of the [[18,8,2]] / [[24,8,2]] / [[36,8,4]] bivariate bicycle codes under independent X noise, and the exact location of the finite-size crossings the paper's MCMC places 'near p_c ~= 0.11'
families.description: Researcher track `jong-yeon-lee`. Source: **arXiv:2607.28621v1**, Yuta Hirasaki and Jong Yeon Lee, *Lifting Lifted Product Codes* (submitted 2026-07-30; still v1 on 2026-09-07). Appendix D and FIG. 5(a) are this family's whole target. Companion family in this repository: `gross-projections` (same source, its Example 4 and TABLE I), which supplies the parity-check matrices and, in its row `GP8`, the permutation-equivalence classes of the projected codes.

statements.label: Eq. (D2) of arXiv:2607.28621v1, stated in Lean over all 2^18 error patterns of the [[18,8,2]] code with Im(H_X^T) and ker(H_Z) as the source defines them, equals a sum of 2^13 = (n+k)/2-many terms in exact integers: I_C = k + sum_{b < 2^13} (N b / q^n) log_2 (N b / T b). Proved for every rational error rate p = a/q at once, with the coset parametrisation (that one list spans Im(H_X^T) on its low 5 bits and ker(H_Z) on all 13, and that a complement basis plus two dual maps split F_2^18) discharged by native_decide.

The exact values of the normalised coherent information I_C/k of Eq. (D2) under independent X noise, to 32 decimal digits, for three gross-code projections: [[18,8,2]] (the source's own Sec. V base code, m = 13), [[24,8,2]] (m = 16) and [[36,8,4]] (m = 22, float64), at p = 0.05, 0.10, 0.105, 0.11, 0.115, 0.12 and on the whole 1/1000 grid in [0.100, 0.115]. At p = 11/100 they are 0.49657641398253889683 ([[18,8,2]]), 0.49596670405839297505 ([[24,8,2]]) and 0.4960165692 ([[36,8,4]]).

The exact location of the finite-size crossings of FIG. 5(a): the [[18,8,2]] and [[36,8,4]] curves of the source's own lift tower cross strictly inside (109/1000, 110/1000) -- at p = 0.109 the [[36,8,4]] curve is above by 1.698e-3 and at p = 0.110 below by 5.598e-4 -- so the crossing is strictly BELOW the p_c ~= 0.11 the paper reads off its MCMC. The [[18,8,2]] and [[24,8,2]] curves cross inside (108/1000, 109/1000) (+4.633e-4 then -7.369e-5).

The coherent-information curve is an invariant of permutation equivalence, and it separates exactly the classes gross-projections GP8 found combinatorially: the three [[36,8,4]] projections of the gross code have the same I_C/k to 15 significant digits at every p tested, while the five [[24,4,4]] projections split 4 + 1 (K = [0,16,26,36,52,62] gives 0.5651578571021063 at p = 0.10 against 0.5649856971413770 for the other four).
The two exact endpoints of Eq. (D2) for the [[18,8,2]] code, kernel-checked: at p = 0 the coherent information is exactly k = 8, and at p = 1/2 it is exactly 0.

The exact coset masses of the [[18,8,2]] code: the 2^13 integers N b sum to 100^18 at p = 11/100 and to 1000^18 at p = 109/1000 (so the cosets partition the 2^18 error patterns and Eq. (D1)'s weights add to one), and every one of them is strictly positive at p = 11/100 (so no term of the reduced sum is a log-of-zero junk value).

Negative controls: at p = 11/100 the 2^13 coset masses of the [[18,8,2]] code are NOT all equal, and the 2^8 logical sectors are NOT equiprobable (T b != 2^8 N b for some b) -- so the exact collapse at p = 1/2 (row LC5) is a fact about p = 1/2 and not an artefact of the coset parametrisation, and I_C at p = 11/100 is strictly between 0 and 8.

The 2^13 coset masses of the [[18,8,2]] code at p = 11/100 and at p = 89/100 are equal coset by coset, so its coherent-information curve is exactly symmetric about p = 1/2: I_C(p) = I_C(1-p). FIG. 5(a) of the source plots only [0, 0.2] and neither states nor uses this.

What the source actually prints, as the comparison baseline: FIG. 5(a), 'As the code size increases, the curves cross near p_c ~= 0.11'; FIG. 5(b), 'A subset of the curves intersects near p ~ 0.105'; and the estimator, Metropolis plus parallel tempering, 60 replicas, 10,000 thermalisation and 100,000 measurement updates, averaged over 1,000 disorder realisations, with the paper's own warning that its estimator 'contains the logarithm of an empirical frequency'.

families.title: The inheritance profile of a lift of a two-block group-algebra code: how many logical qubits of the lifted code descend from the base, for the gross-code Bockstein tower and for every gauge-fixed lift of the [[18,8,2]] base code of arXiv:2607.28621 Sec. V
families.description: Researcher track `jong-yeon-lee`. Sources: **arXiv:2607.28621v1**, Yuta Hirasaki and Jong Yeon Lee, *Lifting Lifted Product Codes* (submitted 2026-07-30; Sec. II A–C, Sec. V, TABLE VI, TABLE VII, and the first question of the Conclusion and outlook) and **arXiv:2607.05386v2**, Jong Yeon Lee, *Logical Spectroscopy* (Theorem 6 "Even Abelian lifts", Proposition 11 "Halving exact sequence", TABLE VI). Nearest external work: **arXiv:2511.13560v3** (Symons, Rajput, Browne, *Sequences of Bivariate Bicycle Codes from Covering Graphs*), which the two Lee papers cite for the odd-index parameter bounds,

statements.label: The composite inheritance ranks of the gross-code Bockstein tower [[18,8,2]] < [[36,8,4]] < [[72,12,6]] < [[144,12,12]] (seeds a = x^3+y+y^2, b = y^3+x+x^2 of arXiv:2607.28621v1 Eq. (32) reduced to each level): r_tau = r_p = 2, 4, 2 for the three composite quotients, with the chain-map identities H_X P_1 = P_0 H_X' and H_Z P_1 = P_0 H_Z' of Proposition 2 checked on every pair. Exactly 2 of the gross code's 12 logical qubits descend from its [[18,8,2]] odd skeleton, and the composite is not a function of the single-step ranks: steps passing 4 and 6 classes compose to 2, which could a priori have been anything in 0..4

The inheritance profile of the source's own Sec. V lift family (arXiv:2607.28621v1 TABLE VI groups with TABLE VII boundary maps), with every printed k recomputed from the printed polynomials: 2 of 12 for the [[72,12,6]] lift to Z6 x Z6 and 4 of 8 for the [[72,8,8]] lift to Z12 x Z3 -- the two index-4 cells, which no source computes -- alongside 4 of 8 at index 2 and 8 of 8 at both index-3 lifts. The [[72,12,6]] lift also factors through either intermediate Z_2 quotient, each of which passes 6 of the 12 while the composite from the base passes 2

The index-2 law: for any group extension 1 -> K -> H -> G -> 1 with |K| = 2 -- no abelian, cyclic or centrality hypothesis -- the projection and transfer of the 2BGA complexes form a short exact sequence 0 -> Q^pi -> Q -> Q^pi -> 0, so r_tau + r_p = k'; and when H is abelian the CSS self-duality of the 2BGA complex (the swap-and-invert involution T = [[0,J],[J,0]], which satisfies H_X T = J H_Z and commutes with pi) gives r_tau = r_p, hence r_tau = r_p = k'/2 and rank delta_1 = rank delta_2 in arXiv:2607.05386v2 Proposition 11

The index-2 law verified on 35 instances: the 16 gauge-fixed lifts of [[18,8,2]] to Z6 x Z3, the 16 to Z3 x Z6, and the three Z_2 steps of the gross-code tower, every one with r_tau = r_p and 2 r_tau = k'

Zero-inheritance lifts exist at index 4: an explicit abelian one (H = Z6 x Z6, K = Z2 x Z2; the identity-section lift, i.e. the plain bivariate-bicycle code 1+x+x^2, 1+y+y^2 on the 6 x 6 torus) and an explicit non-abelian one (H = Z3 x A_4, K = V_4, the group arXiv:2607.28621v1 TABLE VI itself uses for its non-abelian [[72,12,6]] instance), each with k' = 8 = k and r_tau = r_p = 0 -- the lift has exactly as many logical qubits as the base code and shares none of them, all eight being created by the lift. In the censuses this is 162 of 256 gauge-fixed Z6 x Z6 lifts and 108 of 256 Z3 x A_4 lifts

The inheritance profile of every gauge-fixed lift of the [[18,8,2]] base code over six hosts -- Z6 x Z3, Z3 x Z6 (index 2), Z9 x Z3 (index 3), Z12 x Z3, Z6 x Z6 and the non-abelian Z3 x A_4 (index 4); 16 + 16 + 81 + 256 + 256 + 256 lifts -- with the profile distribution of each and the chain-map identities on every single lift. r_p = r_tau in every cell including the non-abelian host; every index-3 lift has r_tau = k' = k = 8; the [[72,12,6]] cells (36 abelian, 72 non-abelian) all have r_tau = 2; and no cyclic-kernel (Z12 x Z3) lift reaches r_tau = 0 while both elementary-abelian-kernel hosts do, 162 and 108 times

The sources' own printed numbers reproduced from their own seeds: n = 144, rank H_X = rank H_Z = 66 and k = 12 for the gross code; k = 8, 8, 12, 12 at the four tower levels; (h_2, h_1, h_0) = (4,8,4), (4,8,4), (6,12,6) and rank delta_1 = rank delta_2 = 4, 2, 6 of arXiv:2607.05386v2 TABLE VI, hence the single-step transfer ranks 4, 6, 6; and k = 8, 8, 8, 12, 8 for the five arXiv:2607.28621v1 TABLE VII lifts, all CSS

The transfer multiplies Hamming weight by the lift index exactly, wt(tau_1 v) = |K| wt(v), checked on all 2^13 X-cycles of [[18,8,2]] for the lifts of index 2, 4 and 8 out of it; and the lightest X-logical of [[18,8,2]] whose transfer is still a nontrivial logical operator upstairs has weight 2 at all three levels, so the gross code's inherited classes carry transferred representatives of weight 16 against d = 12

Negative controls: 'the gross code inherits all eight logical qubits of [[18,8,2]]' and 'it inherits none' are both refuted (r_tau = 2, strictly between); even lifts do both, an index-2 step keeping 6 of 12 while an index-4 lift keeps 0 of 8; the chain-map check is not vacuous (a rotated, non-homomorphic pi fails it) and neither is the restriction to cycles (an explicit non-cycle whose transfer is a non-cycle); rank plus nullity is checked at both ends of the tower; the census counts add up to |K|^4 on every host; and the inheritance profile is not a function of (|K|, k, k') -- Z12 x Z3 and Z6 x Z6 give r_tau = 4 and 0 on the same base code with the same |K| = 4 and the same k' = 8 -- which is also why the k'/2 law is index-2 only, a Z12 x Z3 lift with k' = 16 having r_tau = 4 rather than 8

The swap duality of two-block group-algebra codes over an ARBITRARY finite group H, formalized: with J the antipode permutation matrix (J e_h = e_{h^{-1}}) and W = J (+) J on the n = 2|H| qubits, H_X(a,b) W = J H_Z(b,a) and H_Z(a,b) W = J H_X(b,a) -- the 2BGA codes Q(a,b) and Q(b,a) are CSS-dual to each other over any group, abelian or not. Consequences, also general and also kernel-bound: rank H_X(a,b) = rank H_Z(b,a), rank H_Z(a,b) = rank H_X(b,a), k(a,b) = k(b,a), and the CSS condition H_X H_Z^T = 0 (from L_a R_b = R_b L_a). For commutative H the block swap S alone gives H_X(a,b) S = H_X(b,a), whence T = W S = [[0,J],[J,0]] satisfies H_X(a,b) T = J H_Z(a,b) -- the founding journal's involution, derived rather than postulated -- together with the exact converse: if H_X(a,b) S = H_X(b,a) for EVERY pair of seeds then H is abelian

r_tau != r_p over a non-abelian host -- the family's second open question, answered in the negative by two kernel-bound witnesses. (i) LIFT INDEX 2: H = D_8 (dihedral of order 16), K = Z(D_8) = <r^4> of order 2, G = H/K = D_4, so base and host are both non-abelian; seeds a~ = (1+r)(1+s) and b~ = (1+r^2)(1+s) taken along the identity section; base [[16,9]], lift [[32,13]], r_tau = 7, r_p = 6. Because r_tau + r_p = k' holds for EVERY extension of index 2 (the |K| = 2 half of row LI3, which needs no hypothesis on H) and k' = 13 is ODD, r_tau = r_p = k'/2 is arithmetically impossible: the abelian half of the index-2 law is not merely unproved over general groups, it is false, and the parity of k' is the obstruction. (ii) LIFT INDEX 4: H = D_4 x Z_2, K = <r^2> x <z> = Z_2 x Z_2, G = Z_2 x Z_2 (abelian base), a~ = rsz + r^3 z, b~ = 1 + rz + rs + r^2 s z; base [[8,4]], lift [[32,10]], r_tau = 2, r_p = 3 with k' = 10 EVEN, so the failure is neither a parity accident nor an artefact of a non-abelian base

What survives the swap duality on homology, kernel-checked on 776 instances: r_tau(a,b) = r_p(b,a) and r_p(a,b) = r_tau(b,a), with k and k' swap-invariant, on all 256 gauge-fixed lifts of the [[18,8,2]] base code over the non-abelian host Z_3 x A_4 plus both counterexamples of row LI11 (258), on the 256 gauge-fixed Z_12 x Z_3 lifts and the 256 Z_6 x Z_6 lifts, and on all six steps of the gross-code tower [[18,8,2]] < [[36,8,4]] < [[72,12,6]] < [[144,12,12]] (518)

The general theorem behind LI12: for EVERY finite group H, every extension 1 -> K -> H -> G -> 1 and every lift (a~, b~) of (a, b), r_tau(a,b) = r_p(b,a) and r_p(a,b) = r_tau(b,a), where (b~, a~) is the lift of (b, a) along the same pi. Two steps, neither using commutativity: (i) tau_1 = p_1^T and the perfect pairing H_1 x H^1 -> F_2 give rank tau-hat_1 = rank p-hat^1 -- equivalently, in rank-only form, r_tau = rank(N_H P_1^T M_G^T) and rank p-hat^1 = rank(M_G P_1 N_H^T) for N_H a basis of ker H_X^lift and M_G a basis of ker H_Z^base, and these two matrices are transposes; (ii) the swap duality W = J (+) J of row LI10 carries H^1(Q(a,b)) to H_1(Q(b,a)) at the base and at the lift and commutes with P_1, since pi(h^{-1}) = pi(h)^{-1}. This is the correct general replacement for r_tau = r_p, which row LI11 refutes

families.paper_title: Which logical qubits of a lifted product code descend from its base?\\ Inheritance profiles along the gross-code tower\\ and across every gauge-fixed lift of $\code{18}{8}{2}$
families.paper_abstract: A lift of a two-block group-algebra code along a group extension $1\to K\to H\to G\to1$ comes with two chain maps: a projection $p$ from the lifted code down to the base code and its transpose, the transfer $\tau$.  Hirasaki and Lee (arXiv:2607.28621) show that when $|K|$ is odd the transfer is injective on homology, so every logical operator of the base code is inherited by the lift, and they ask what happens when $|K|$ is even, where ``no analogous relation follows directly''.  We answer the question numerically and exactly for the codes those authors study, by computing the \emph{inheritance profile} of a lift: the rank $\rt$ of the induced transfer on the first homology (the number of base logical qubits that survive) and the rank $\rp$ of the induced projection.  Along the tower $\code{18}{8}{2}\subset\code{36}{8}{4}\subset\code{72}{12}{6} \subset\code{144}{12}{12}$ of the gross code, each $\Z_2$ step passes exactly half of the logical qubits of the larger code (ranks $4,6,6$, which are one subtraction away from Lee's Bockstein table in arXiv:2607.05386), but the composites are $2,4,2$: only two of the twelve logical qubits of the gross code descend from its $\code{18}{8}{2}$ skeleton, and the composite rank is not determined by the single-step ranks.  For the five lifts of $\code{18}{8}{2}$ printed in Section~V of arXiv:2607.28621 the profiles are $4,8,8,2,4$ out of $8,8,8,12,8$; in particular the $\code{72}{12}{6}$ lift over $\Z_6\times\Z_6$ keeps only $2$ of its $12$ logical qubits from the base.  Across all $881$ gauge-fixed lifts of $\code{18}{8}{2}$ over six host groups (five abelian and one non-abelian) we find that an even-index lift can inherit \emph{nothing}: $162$ of the $256$ lifts to $\Z_6\times\Z_6$ --- the plain bivariate bicycle code $1+x+x^2$, $1+y+y^2$ on the $6\times6$ torus among them --- and $108$ of the $256$ lifts to $\Z_3\times A_4$ have $k'=8=k$ and $\rt=\rp=0$: as many logical qubits as the base and none in common.  This is the extreme case of the warning of Symons, Rajput and Browne (arXiv:2511.13560) that a logical basis known for the base code ``may only lift to a set of logical operators \dots\ that do not span'' the logical space of the lift: here it lifts to nothing at all.  The per-step rigidity is the index-$2$ law $\rt=\rp=k'/2$, whose rank count is already in Lee's Proposition~11 and which we record with a short proof; the census, the composites and the zero-inheritance lifts are new.  Every finite statement is certified by compiled evaluation inside Lean~4 and independently recomputed in NumPy.  \emph{Added in the second version.}  The first version left open whether $\rt=\rp$ holds when the host group is not abelian, and named the likely route: that the codes of $(a,b)$ and of $(b,a)$ are $X$/$Z$-dual over any group.  That duality is a published theorem of Lin and Pryadko (Theorem~6 of arXiv:2306.16400), and we machine-check it for every finite group in the matrix form the profile needs: with $J$ the permutation $e_h\mapsto e_{h^{-1}}$ and $W=J\oplus J$, $H_X(a,b)\,W=J\,H_Z(b,a)$ and $H_Z(a,b)\,W=J\,H_X(b,a)$; hence $k(a,b)=k(b,a)$, and the block swap alone carries the checks of $Q(a,b)$ to those of $Q(b,a)$ for every pair of seeds only if $H$ is abelian. What the duality gives on homology is $\rt(a,b)=\rp(b,a)$, not $\rt=\rp$, and the latter fails: an index-$2$ lift of a $\codek{16}{9}$ code over the dihedral group $D_4$ to $D_8$ has $k'=13$ and $(\rt,\rp)=(7,6)$ --- since $\rt+\rp=k'$ at index $2$ for every host, an odd $k'$ makes equality impossible --- and an index-$4$ lift of an $\codek{8}{4}$ code over $\Z_2\times\Z_2$ to $D_4\times\Z_2$ has $k'=10$ and $(\rt,\rp)=(2,3)$.  The swapped identity is certified on $776$ instances, the two counterexamples among them.  The census of the first version could not see the failure: its seeds have weight $3$, and a search outside the formal development finds that over $\Z_3\times A_4$ the equality holds for every weight-$3$ seed pair and fails for about one sampled weight-$4$ pair in six.

families.title: The exact superintegrability locus of the 13-parameter 5-component Lotka-Volterra system of arXiv:2411.18264v4: the four printed Darboux polynomials certified, and functional independence of the four integrals shown to hold if and only if the eight parameter differences that make up their coefficients are all nonzero
families.description: P. H. van der Kamp, *Hypergraphs and Lotka-Volterra systems with linear Darboux polynomials*, arXiv:2411.18264. **Live version v4** (9 Jun 2025), primary `nlin.SI`, cross-list `math.DS`, no journal reference on the arXiv record, but the paper *is* published: J. Dynam. Differential Equations, `doi:10.1007/s10884-025-10446-2`, online 2025-07-10, no volume/issue/pages assigned as of September 2026. Everything quoted here was read from the **v4 e-print** (`TTR2.tex`, `curl https://arxiv.org/e-print/2411.18264v4`) and every *number* — equation (34), Lemma 2, equation (3), Table 7, page 18 — from th
families.paper_title: The superintegrability locus of a 13-parameter five-component\\ Lotka--Volterra system with linear Darboux polynomials
families.paper_abstract:
Van der Kamp (arXiv:2411.18264) presents a five-component homogeneous Lotka--Volterra system with thirteen parameters, his matrix~(34), as a new superintegrable system that is not equivalent to a tree-system.  The paper prints four linear Darboux polynomials for it with the words ``it is easy to see'', asserts that the four integrals obtained from them by its equation~(3) are functionally independent, and hedges every statement of the paper to ``generic values'' of the parameters, noting that for special values ``it may happen that integrals are no longer functionally independent''.  We prove the two printed assertions and identify the exceptional set exactly.  The four Darboux polynomial identities hold as polynomial identities over an arbitrary commutative ring.  The logarithmic Jacobian of the four integrals is reduced, by a two-sided identity valid for any homogeneous Lotka--Volterra system with linear Darboux polynomials, to a polynomial matrix $V=NA-\diag(P)B$ from which the inverse of $A$ has disappeared and which vanishes in every column outside the hyperedge of the corresponding Darboux polynomial.  For the matrix~(34) we compute $V$ in closed form and prove: when $\det A
eq0$, at every point with $x_k
eq0$ and $P_i
eq0$, the four logarithmic gradients are linearly independent if and only if $K=pquvwzrs
eq0$, where $p,\dots,s$ are the eight parameter differences that make up the coefficients of the four Darboux polynomials.  The condition $K
e0$ is exactly the non-degeneracy hypothesis $\alpha_j
eq0$ of the paper's own Lemma~2 for the nine printed coefficients, so the system is superintegrable precisely where its printed Darboux polynomials are non-degenerate and nowhere else: there is no further degeneration in the region $\det A
eq0$.  On the exceptional set the dependence is witnessed by an explicit relation whose coefficients do not involve $x$.  Two explicit rational points, one on each side of the locus, show that both directions are non-vacuous.  Every statement is checked in Lean~4 -- the general ones over an arbitrary commutative ring or field, the two control points over $\Q$ -- without \lean{native\_decide}.

families.title: Fortuna's conjecture: is the solution of X A + A^T X = -Q entrywise nonnegative for every Hurwitz companion A? -- the n = 5 complex-pair cell that arXiv:2606.16492 leaves open
families.description: Founded 2026-09-07 from arXiv:2606.16492v1 (A. Ferrante, *On the Lyapunov equation with the state matrix in companion form*, eess.SY / math.RA). Record: `journal/2026-09-07-lyapcomp-fortuna-founding.md`.
families.paper_title: Fortuna's conjecture on the companion Lyapunov equation\\ at the first open cell: an exact verification at a degree-five\\ companion matrix with a complex-conjugate pair
families.paper_abstract: Let $a(s)=s^n+a_{n-1}s^{n-1}+\dots+a_0$ be a Hurwitz polynomial, $A$ its companion matrix and $X$ the solution of the Lyapunov equation $XA+A\tp X=-Q$ with $Q=Q\tp\psd$.  Fortuna's conjecture, as stated by Ferrante (arXiv:2606.16492), asserts that $X$ is entrywise nonnegative.  Ferrante proves it when $A$ has only real eigenvalues, records that the cases $n\le4$ can be settled by brute force and that the diagonal and the two corner entries are always nonnegative, and names the removal of the real-root assumption as the main open question.  We give an exact verification in a cell outside those bounds: at the companion matrix of $(s+1)^3(s^2+s+1)=s^5+4s^4+7s^3+7s^2+4s+1$, whose spectrum contains $\exp(\pm2\pi i/3)$ and which is not diagonalizable, the solution for every rank-one $Q=qq\tp$ is entrywise nonnegative, each of its fifteen distinct entries being written as an explicit sum of squares in $q$ with rational coefficients; the solution is also shown to be unique among symmetric matrices by an explicit inversion of the Lyapunov operator over $\Q$.  Two identities valid for every degree and every spectrum are recorded: $2a_0X_{1,n}=Q_{11}$, which turns Ferrante's corner remark into a value, and $X_{k,k-1}=a_{k-1}X_{k,n}-Q_{kk}/2$.  Controls show that the companion form and the Hurwitz hypothesis are both needed and that the conclusion is strictly stronger than $X\psd$.  Recomputing Ferrante's counterexample to total nonnegativity exactly over $\Q$, we find that the minor he names, the leading $2\times2$ principal minor, is positive ($+4355916893/28812000$), as it must be when $X\psd$, and that the negative minor is the non-principal one on rows $\{1,2\}$ and columns $\{2,3\}$, equal to $-51562093/72030$.  Outside the formal development we report a floating-point-free search ($57{,}678$ rational instances at $n=5$, no counterexample), a symbolic verification along the one-parameter family $(s+1)^3(s^2+ps+1)$, $p>0$, and the identification, for $n\le5$, of the inverse of the matrix of the quadratic form $X_{nn}$ with the Hermite matrix of $a$, whose $(n,n)$ entry is $2a_{n-1}$; this yields $X_{n,n-1}\ge0$ for every Hurwitz $a$ of degree at most $5$.  Every pinned statement is verified in Lean~4 against \emph{Mathlib} without compiled evaluation.

families.title: The quantity m_0(c,d) of Sawin-Shusterman-Stoll: the stabilisation lemma that makes their algorithm a stopping rule, m_0(1+kx,l) <= 2 for every prime l, and their Remark 5.3 proved for every k >= 1 and 2 <= l <= 4·10^4 (title extended 2026-09-03; v1 covered k, l <= 1000)
families.description: Founded 2026-09-03 from **arXiv:1803.10811v1** = William Sawin, Mark Shusterman, Michael Stoll, *Irreducibility of polynomials with a large gap*, **Acta Arith. 192 (2020), no. 2, 111–139**, DOI `10.4064/aa180526-12-6`. The arXiv listing carries only `[v1]` (submitted 2018-03-28, primary category `math.NT`), so the corpus copy, the arXiv PDF and the published article are the same text; the published numbering is confirmed below.

statements.label: The source's Remark 5.3 over the box k,l <= 1000: for every weakly robust (1+kx,l) there, m_0(1+kx,l) <= 2 except at the two exceptions it names
The stabilisation lemma: for a weakly robust pair, 'every T_m pair has ab = cd' is monotone in m, so m_0(c,d) <= M is one finite condition on T_{M+1}
m_0(1+kx, l) <= 2 for EVERY k >= 1 and EVERY prime l, with no computation: the trivial splitting of the constant term never produces a bad T_3-pair
The source's two exceptions really are exceptions: m_0(1+2x,4) >= 3 and m_0(1+3x,9) >= 3, by explicit T_3 witnesses
Negative control: the bound 2 in MG1 cannot be replaced by 1, since m_0(1+3x,2) >= 2
Non-vacuity: m_0(1+3x, 6) <= 2 for a pair Lemma 5.2 does not cover, so MG1's hypotheses are satisfiable outside the source's proved range
A sufficient arithmetic criterion for weak robustness of (1+kx, l): k dominating every divisor e >= 2 of l whose cofactor is also >= 2
Two narrowing lemmas for the non-trivial splitting: a bad T_3-pair with 2 <= a_0 <= b_0 forces k^2 <= a_0^2 + b_0^2, and weak robustness forces b_0 <= k
PROSE: a counterexample to Remark 5.3 beyond the two known ones would have b_0 <= a_0^2, so the remaining region is a two-parameter band and not a search
MEASUREMENT: the compute-first gate and the price of the box, in C and in Lean

Remark 5.3 of Sawin-Shusterman-Stoll over 2 <= l <= 4*10^4 and EVERY k >= 1 (the k-box is gone, not enlarged): m_0(1+kx,l) <= 2 for every weakly robust pair there, except at the two exceptions it names
MEASUREMENT: the price curve of the chord kernel, the landed frontier l <= 4*10^4 at 405 CPU-s, and the price of the next box
The two exceptions of Remark 5.3, exactly: m_0(1+2x,4) = 4 and m_0(1+3x,9) = 3, by the T_4 and T_5 reductions
Controls for the chord kernel: innerOK is false at exactly the three cells that carry a bad T_3-pair, and the weak-robustness hypothesis of MG11 is load-bearing since m_0(1+4x,16) >= 3

families.paper_title: The invariant $m_0$ of Sawin--Shusterman--Stoll\\ for the pairs $(1+kx,\,l)$: a stopping rule, every prime~$l$,\\ and a proved range
families.paper_abstract: Sawin, Shusterman and Stoll attach to a pair $(c,d)$ of integer polynomials with $c(0),d(0)\neq 0$ an integer $m_0(c,d)$: the least $M$ such that for every $m>M$, every pair $(a,b)$ with $\deg a,\deg b<m$, $ab\equiv cd \bmod x^m$ and $\wt{a}+\wt{b}\le\wt{c}+\wt{d}$ already satisfies $ab=cd$, where $\wt{\,\cdot\,}$ is the squared Euclidean length of the coefficient vector.  It controls the threshold beyond which the non-reciprocal part of $x^{N}c(x^{-1})+d(x)$ is irreducible.  For the two-parameter family $(c,d)=(1+kx,\,l)$ they prove $m_0=1$ on a range, and remark that outside it $m_0(1+kx,l)\le 2$ \emph{appears} to hold, with the two exceptions $m_0(1+2x,4)=4$ and $m_0(1+3x,9)=3$; a proof ``should be possible'', they write, ``but the arguments seem to get rather technical''.  No verification range is stated.  We contribute three things.  First, a stabilisation lemma: for a weakly robust pair with $(cd)(0)\neq 0$, the property ``every element of $T_m$ satisfies $ab=cd$'' is monotone in $m$.  This is what makes the authors' own procedure --- compute $T_1,T_2,\dots$ until $ab=cd$ throughout --- a stopping rule, and it turns the infinite assertion $m_0(c,d)\le M$ into a single condition on the one set $T_{M+1}$; the source does not state it.  Second, an infinite unconditional sub-family: $m_0(1+kx,l)\le 2$ for \emph{every} $k\ge 1$ and \emph{every} prime~$l$, with no computation, by a sum-of-squares certificate; the source's lemma reaches prime $l$ only for $l\ge 5$ and $k\le l^{2}/2$.  Third, two narrowing inequalities which confine a hypothetical further exception to the band $2\le a_0\le b_0\le k\le\sqrt{a_0^{2}+b_0^{2}}$, where $a_0b_0=l$.  They leave $k$ in an interval of length about $a_0^{2}/2b_0$ rather than in a box, and enumerating that interval --- each of the two levels of the enumeration being a line meeting a disk, which is what makes it affordable --- proves the remark's bound $m_0\le2$ for \emph{every} $k\ge1$ and every $l$ with $2\le l\le4\cdot10^{4}$ such that $(1+kx,l)$ is weakly robust and $(k,l)$ is not one of the two exceptions; no upper bound on $k$ is imposed.  We also certify the two exceptional values themselves, $m_0(1+2x,4)=4$ and $m_0(1+3x,9)=3$, and that the constant $2$ cannot be lowered. All of this is machine-checked in Lean~4.

families.title: Minimum complete symmetry breaks for finite magmas: the n!-1 question of arXiv:2502.10155 certified at n = 3, 4, 5, and reduced for general n to the permutations that move 0
families.description: **How many permutations does a complete symmetry break for finite magmas need?**

statements.label: S_n minus the identity is a canonizing set for order-n magmas, for every n (the n!-1 upper bound)
if some magma of order n is lexicographically minimal under every permutation except one, p, then p belongs to EVERY canonizing set for order-n magmas
explicit witnesses for all n!-1 non-identity permutations force every canonizing set for order-n magmas to have at least n!-1 elements
the minimum canonizing set for magmas of order 3 has exactly 5 = 3!-1 elements, and equals S_3 minus the identity (so it is unique)
the minimum canonizing set for magmas of order 4 has exactly 23 = 4!-1 elements, and equals S_4 minus the identity (so it is unique)
the minimum canonizing set for magmas of order 5 has exactly 119 = 5!-1 elements, and equals S_5 minus the identity (so it is unique)

border embedding: if a magma A of order n has covering set exactly {s}, then the order-(n+1) magma with a zero first row, a zero first column and A+1 in the remaining n x n block has covering set exactly {s+}, where s+ fixes 0 and shifts s up by one. Hence essentiality transfers from S_n to the point stabiliser of 0 in S_(n+1), and the source's question reduces to the permutations that MOVE 0

exhaustive witness census: exactly 3,237 of the 19,683 order-3 magmas and 178,932,325 of the 4,294,967,296 order-4 magmas have a singleton covering set, and every non-identity permutation is witnessed under EACH of the source's three vectorizations; the per-permutation counts at n = 4 range 229,956-122,487,593 (row-by-row), 7,592-73,777,649 (diagonal-first) and 516,498-137,996,740 (concentric)
all 719 = 6!-1 non-identity permutations of S_6 are essential for order-6 magmas, with explicit witnesses
at least 719 of the 5,039 non-identity permutations of S_7 -- those fixing 0 -- are essential for order-7 magmas

the 156 subgroups of S_5 as explicit data, verified in the Lean kernel to be subgroups (identity, closure under composition and inverses, pairwise distinct), together with the Moebius bottom row mu(1,K) of the subgroup lattice and its defining identity sum over K contained in H of mu(1,K) = [H = 1] at every one of the 156; likewise the 30 subgroups of S_4 and the 6 of S_3

the equivariant count g(K) = number of K-equivariant tables X x X -> X equals the product over the K-orbits on X x X of the number of X-points fixed by the orbit's stabiliser, verified in the Lean kernel for every one of the 156 subgroups of S_5 (and for the 30 of S_4, the 6 of S_3) against the recorded values

families.title: Completely regular codes in the Manhattan metric: a finite ball that decides the infinite grid
families.description: Completely regular codes in the infinite grid `G_n = ℤⁿ` under the **Manhattan metric**, and the finite 0/1 program that decides their nonexistence.

statements.label: The reduction: infeasibility of the finite 0/1 program on the radius-r ball refutes the code in the infinite grid
Search soundness: a search that returns false witnesses that no colouring of the ball satisfies the constraints
No completely regular code of covering radius 1 in G_3 with a_0 = 0 and c_1 = 4 or c_1 = 5
No completely regular code of covering radius >= 2 in G_3 with any of 40 upper-left 3 x 2 parameter blocks
Non-vacuity: the even-weight code of Z^3 is a completely regular code with matrix [0,6|6,0]
Negative controls: the ball size, the search reach, and the cost of the lumped class
Arc consistency on the class domains: a propagator whose only proved property is that no solution loses a colour
The source's program `LP_{≥2}` excludes exactly 59 of the 91 admissible `3 × 2` blocks in `G_3`
The parameter matrix of a CRC has symmetric support, which kills the 16 blocks with `b₁ = 0` that no ball can see
75 of the 91 blocks refuted, and the remaining 16 are exactly the blocks of codes that exist
Controls for the propagator: soundness, complementarity, the ball, and agreement with the unpropagated search

families.title: generalized Markov equations x^2+y^2+z^2+k1x+k2y+k3z = xyz -- Question 7.1 (6.1 in v1; renumbered in v2) of the source answered in BOTH halves (existence and orbit count) for every cell with k_i <= 8
families.description: **Question 6.1** of *Mutation-preserving generalized cluster algebras and Laurent mutation invariants*, [arXiv:2608.10551](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.10551), Zhichao Chen and Yimin Huang, submitted 11 Aug 2026:

statements.label: Vieta descent for the generalized Markov equation: every positive solution descends to a fundamental one, and every fundamental one lies in an explicit box
The largest admissible k is exactly 3+k1+k2+k3, for every (k1,k2,k3); the source's Proposition 4.5 is the (2,0,0) case and needs no native axiom
The admissible set of every cell is closed under divisors
Validation: the source's Theorem 4.8 and the Markov-Hurwitz classification, re-derived from the general machinery
Question 6.1 (existence half) answered for all 64 cells with k1,k2,k3 <= 3: the complete list of admissible k per cell
Negative controls: the descent bound is load-bearing, and the two obvious guesses about the answer are false
The Γ̂-orbits of a generalized Markov equation are in bijection with the fundamental solutions in the descent box, so the orbit half of Question 6.1 is a finite computation
Solvability depends only on the multiset {k₁,k₂,k₃}
The unit family: for every factorisation t·s = 2+k₃ the value k = t + k₁ + k₂ + s is admissible; hence a positive even coefficient always breaks the divisor pattern
Question 6.1, existence half, answered for every cell with k₁,k₂,k₃ ≤ 8: 165 non-decreasing cells, 145 of them new
Validation: [GM23]'s single orbit at k = 3+k₁+k₂+k₃ reproved kernel-clean for every cell, and the source's own orbit theorem and Table 2 reproduced representative by representative
Question 6.1, orbit half, answered for every NON-DECREASING cell with k₁,k₂,k₃ ≤ 8: 165 orbit profiles, 1,430 orbit counts

Negative controls for the orbit layer: the count is 0 at k = 0 for every cell, is not bounded by a small constant, and the four fundamental solutions of the source's k=1 cell really are in four distinct orbits
The number of `Γ̂`-orbits depends only on the multiset `{k₁,k₂,k₃}`
`gcd` is a `Γ̂`-orbit invariant, so an orbit of positive solutions is entirely primitive or entirely imprimitive
The primitive decomposition of the orbit count: `𝒩(k₁,k₂,k₃;k) = Σ_{d≥1} 𝒩ᵖ(k₁,k₂,k₃;k·d)`, for every cell and every `k`
The fully symmetric solutions of an arbitrary cell: `(t,t,t)` solves iff `k·t = 3+k₁+k₂+k₃`, and every such solution is fundamental
The Generalized Uniqueness Conjecture of arXiv:2511.03428 is false: an infinite family of counterexamples, plus every one with `λᵢ ≤ 8`
Twenty-five instances of [GM23]'s reordered-uniqueness failure, ten of them on the equation `k = 3+k₁+k₂+k₃`, each at a cell with a single `Γ̂`-orbit
Validation: the two published ordered-uniqueness counterexamples reproduced from this development's machinery

families.paper_title: Solvability and mutation orbits of the generalized Markov equations $x^2+y^2+z^2+k_1yz+k_2xz+k_3xy=kxyz$
families.paper_abstract: Chen and Huang, in their study of mutation-preserving generalized cluster algebras, ask (Question 7.1) to classify the $k\in\ZZ_{>0}$ for which $x^{2}+y^{2}+z^{2}+k_1yz+k_2xz+k_3xy=kxyz$ has a positive integer solution and to determine the orbits of the solutions under the generalized cluster mutation group $\Gh$; they record that for general $k$ ``we are even not clear about the existence of the solutions''.  We prove a Vieta descent bound valid for every $(k_1,k_2,k_3,k)$: every positive solution descends to a \emph{fundamental} one, and every fundamental solution lies in an explicit box.  Two consequences hold for all coefficient triples: $k$ admissible implies $k\le 3+k_1+k_2+k_3$, a bound attained at $(1,1,1)$, and the admissible set is closed under divisors.  We then show that each $\Gh$-orbit of positive solutions contains \emph{exactly one} fundamental solution, so the number of orbits is the cardinality of an explicitly enumerable finite set; this makes the second half of Question 7.1 a finite computation for every coefficient triple.  Carrying it out, we answer the existence half for every $(k_1,k_2,k_3)$ with $k_i\le 8$ --- the answer depends only on the multiset $\{k_1,k_2,k_3\}$, of which there are $165$ in that range, all but two outside the cases settled in the literature --- and the orbit half for each of those $165$ multisets in its non-decreasing representative: $1430$ orbit counts, of which the literature covered $169$. We also exhibit a \emph{unit family} of admissible values, one for each factorisation $ts=2+k_3$, and deduce that a triple with a positive even coefficient never has admissible set equal to the divisors of $3+k_1+k_2+k_3$.  The tabulated data show that the orbit count is not monotone in $k$, is not bounded by a small constant, and is not determined by the admissible set.  Every numbered statement is formalized and machine-checked in Lean~4.

families.title: Minimising the chain dimension of the weak Markus-Yamabe counterexample: the degree filtration of the subalgebra generated by the Alpoge map
families.description: On 5 August 2026 Castañeda, Honorato and Valenzuela-Henríquez posted **arXiv:2608.05392**, *The weak Markus–Yamabe conjecture fails in dimension 14*. A `C¹` map `X : ℝⁿ → ℝⁿ` is **Hurwitz** if every eigenvalue of `JX(x)` has negative real part; the weak Markus–Yamabe conjecture says a Hurwitz map is injective. The paper's engine is a **chain realization theorem**: any polynomial Keller map `F = I + H` of `ℝⁿ` with component degrees `d₁,…,dₙ` yields an explicit polynomial vector field on `ℝᴺ`,

statements.label: The Alpoge map: det J F = -2 as a ring identity in the nine partial derivatives, the same determinant from the formal Jacobian of the sparse representation, and three distinct rational points with common image (-1/4,0,0)

The normalized map F~ = (R/2, Q, P): the expanded components, degree vector (4,6,7), sum max(d_i,2) - 3 = 14, and a root of lambda^3 - 58 lambda^2 - (289/2) lambda - 1 in (-1,0) so that -F~ is not Hurwitz on R^3
The resolvent cubic 2 P r^3 - Q r^2 + 2 r - R = 0 at r = x/(1+xy), and the source's collision as its totally split fiber r in {0,2,-2}

The degree filtration of the subalgebra Q[R,Q,P] generated by the Alpoge map: among all polynomials of degree at most 8 in the three generators, the elements of total degree at most 3, 5, 6 form spaces of dimension exactly 1, 2, 3, spanned by 1, then 1 and R, then 1, R and Q

Retargeting cannot beat 17: for every polynomial map A of R^3 of degree at most 8 such that 1, A_1(F~), A_2(F~), A_3(F~) are linearly independent, sum_i max(deg (A o F~)_i, 2) >= 4+6+7 = 17, so the chain realization of arXiv:2608.05392 cannot produce a dimension below 14 from any change of target coordinates

The dimension-fourteen field of arXiv:2608.05392 Theorem 5.1, kernel-checked: J X + I_14 is nilpotent of index exactly 14 (M^14 = 0, M^13 has 33 nonzero entries), the field has degree 7, and the three rational points S_1, S_2, S_3 are distinct singularities

Measured negative on the source side: of the 966 = 21 x 46 elementary triangular right compositions F~ o B with B a single-monomial shear of degree 2 or 3 and 46 rational coefficients, none lowers sum max(deg,2) below 17; the best is 18, attained only by B = (x, y - xz/3, z)

families.paper_title: The degree filtration of the Alp\"oge subalgebra:\\ retargeting cannot lower the Markus--Yamabe dimension below fourteen
families.paper_abstract: A recent chain realization theorem of Casta\~neda, Honorato and Valenzuela-Henr\'iquez turns a polynomial Keller map $F$ of $\RR^n$ with a multi-point fiber into a polynomial vector field on $\RR^N$, $N=\sum_i\max(\deg F_i,2)-n$, whose Jacobian has spectrum $\{-1\}$ everywhere and whose singularities are the fiber; fed with Alp\"oge's three-dimensional counterexample to the Jacobian conjecture it refutes the weak Markus--Yamabe conjecture in dimension~$14$.  The authors close by asking for the minimum of $\sum_i\max(\deg(A\circ F\circ B)_i,2)$ over polynomial automorphisms $A,B$ of $\RR^3$, every unit removed being one dimension off the counterexample.  We settle the target side of that minimisation, which is a question about the degree filtration of the subalgebra generated by the components of $F$.  Among all polynomials of degree at most $8$ in the three generators, those of total degree at most $3$, $5$ and $6$ span spaces of dimensions exactly $1$, $2$ and $3$: spanned by $1$; by $1$ and $R$; and by $1$, $R$ and $Q$.  This does not follow from the numerical semigroup $\langle4,6,7\rangle$: the three leading forms are algebraically dependent, the generators are not a SAGBI basis, and genuine subduction occurs.  The consequence is that $\sum_i\max(\deg(A\circ F)_i,2)\ge4+6+7=17$ for every polynomial map $A$ of degree at most $8$ whose composite with $F$ is dominant --- a class wider than the automorphisms the question asks about --- so no change of target coordinates lowers the realized dimension below $14$.  The certificate behind the filtration is a $162\times162$ integer identity, machine-checked in Lean~4.

families.title: gamma-vectors of matroid Chow polynomials: gamma-positivity, Kruskal-Katona, and real-rootedness certificates
families.description: > **2026-08-23 scoop-audit flag:** arXiv:2604.04550 is now v3 (2026-07-10) with "newly found counter-examples to a real-rootedness question raised in previous versions" and an abstract ending "an infinite family of flag chordal nestohedra whose h-polynomials are not real-rooted" — the sentence below calling `realRooted_*` an instance of an OPEN CFL Conjecture 1.1 needs re-checking against v3's body (not yet read). Question 9.8 is unaffected.

statements.label: Each of 121 computed Chow polynomials is palindromic and has the stated gamma-vector, which is nonnegative (gamma-positivity)
Each of the 121 gamma-vectors satisfies the Kruskal-Katona inequalities, i.e. is the f-vector of a simplicial complex
Each of the 121 Chow polynomials is real-rooted, with simple roots -- instances of CFL Conjecture 1.1, which is open

Negative controls: the Kruskal-Katona check is tight on real data, strictly stronger than gamma-positivity, refuted independently by mathlib's Kruskal-Katona, and the source's own hypotheses are necessary
Search: no flag built matroid found whose gamma-vector violates Kruskal-Katona (CFL Question 8.7)
CFL Question 9.8 refuted: a flag, non-complete built matroid (U(7,8), 19-element building set) whose Chow gamma-vector (1,5,2,1) is not an f-vector; verified at ranks 7 through 11 by coloop padding
Correction: Kruskal-Katona is provably vacuous below rank 5, so the earlier scan (U(3,4), U(3,5), U(4,5)) could not bear on Question 9.8

The Question 9.8 counterexample is a rank-7 family with unbounded ground set: for four lines `U(2,s_i)`, `s_i ≥ 2`, truncated to rank 7, the building set (atoms, lines, two opposite line-joins, all triple joins, `E`) of size `n+11` is flag, non-complete, and has γ = `(1,5,2,1)`, which is not an `f`-vector — twelve members, `n = 8..12`, eleven of them non-uniform

The `k`-block partition family on `U(2k−1,2k)`: flag iff the complement of `Γ` is triangle-free (`k ≥ 4`), γ = `(1, 3+m, m, 1)` at `k = 4` with Kruskal–Katona holding iff `m = | Γ | ≥ 3`, and slack exactly `0` at the minimum for `k = 5, 6` — so `k = 4` is the unique crossing point

Negative controls: blocks of rank ≥ 3 lose flagness and γ-positivity together (17 rows, none γ-positive); a Kruskal–Katona failure off the flag class (`k = 3`, γ = `(1,1,1)`) proves nothing; and the rank-7 truncation is what bites (rank 6 and rank 8 both pass)

What the counterexample does not kill: `(1,5,2,1)` is an `M`-vector, so Question 9.8 fails at the `f`-vector step and nowhere earlier; `MacOk` is defined from the family's own `binRep` and separates from `KKOk` on exactly this vector

The Kruskal–Katona pseudopower of Defs.lean obeys proved thresholds, not just decide on cases: largestBinom is the largest a with C(a,k) ≤ m, m^{(k)} = 0 for m ≤ k, m^{(1)} = C(m,2), 1 ≤ m^{(i)} ↔ m ≥ i+1, and m^{(i)} = 1 ↔ i+1 ≤ m ≤ 2i — for every m below the definition's 2^128 fuel bound

The `k`-block family obeys one law for every `k`: with γ of the family's shape `(1,…,m,1)`, the top Kruskal–Katona inequality holds iff `m ≥ k−1` and is tight iff `m ≤ 2k−4`; flagness forces `m ≥ mantelMin k = ⌊(k−1)²/4⌋` (Mantel), and comparing the quadratic bound with the two linear thresholds gives `mantelMin k ≥ k−1 ↔ k ≥ 5` and `mantelMin k ≤ 2k−4 ↔ k ≤ 8` — so `k = 4` is the **only** `k` whose flag members fail the **top** Kruskal–Katona inequality, and the minimum flag member is exactly tight **precisely for `5 ≤ k ≤ 8`**

The k-block scan extended from k ≤ 6 to k = 12: 168 rows over the whole flag range, each palindromic with expand γ = H, γ-positive, an M-vector, of γ-length k with γ_{k−2} = |Γ| and γ_{k−1} = 1; the k ≤ 6 part reproduces every landed bsPartTable row, and Kruskal–Katona fails exactly once, at (k,m) = (4,2)

γ₂ ≤ C(γ₁,2) is the level-1 Kruskal–Katona inequality (m^{(1)} = C(m,2)); it holds with margin ≥ 2 on all 234 landed γ-positive rows and all 168 new ones; and it does not follow from H being a palindromic γ-positive M-vector — h = (1,6,12,6,1) is all three and has γ = (1,2,2) with γ₂ = 2 > 1 = C(γ₁,2)

Negative controls and one correction: the landed HuntBuildSets.lean docstring's "k = 6 … slack 0 at |Γ| = 6, .., 9" is off by one — at |Γ| = 9, 9^{(4)} = 2 and the slack is 1, so the range is 6, 7, 8; the thresholds are sharp (2^{(2)} = 0, 3^{(2)} = 4^{(2)} = 1, 5^{(2)} = 2); raising the top entry of a tight member breaks Kruskal–Katona; and mantelMin 4 = 2 is exactly the failing \|Γ\|

The dual of the lattice of flats of every Bose–Burton geometry `B_{r,k}(q)` is a TN-poset: the `q`-Pascal matrix with bottom row the Whitney numbers `W_{r-j}` is totally nonnegative, for every `r`, every `0 ≤ k ≤ r-1` and every real `q > 1`. Proof: an explicit nonnegative resolving array in closed form, `λ_j = q^{C(s,2)-C(j,2)-j(r-1-j)} (∏_{i=s}^{j}(q^i-1)) Σ(r,s,j)` with `Σ = ∑_{m+n=r-j-1} q^{jn} [j-s+m, m]_q > 0`. In Lean: the certificate verified for 381 matrices, and total nonnegativity checked from the definition, over every one of the `C(2n,n)` minors, for 14 of them (corrected 2026-08-28) plus 17 perturbed matrices in the controls (`r ≥ 6` priced at 8.1 GB and parked).

The Chow polynomial `uH_{B_{r,k}(q)}` of a Bose–Burton geometry is palindromic, has the stated γ-vector, is γ-positive, satisfies the Kruskal–Katona inequalities and is real-rooted with `rk − 1` simple roots — 41 instances (`q ∈ {2,3,4,5,7,9}`, `r ≤ 8`), **29 of them in the range `2 ≤ k ≤ r-2`**, each with a kernel-checked sign-alternation certificate.

The Chow polynomials of Bose–Burton geometries, **computed inside the kernel** from the Gaussian binomials by the `O(r²)` chain recursion rather than supplied as data: 41 instances reproduced by `bbChow`, 8 literature/ledger anchors, and the exact identity `uH_{B_{r,1}(q)} = uH_{PG(r-1,q)}` (`q ≤ 5`, `r ≤ 8`).

Kurtz's criterion `γ_i² > 4γ_{i-1}γ_{i+1}` holds on all 41 Bose–Burton γ-vectors, so each of those instances has a second, elementary proof of real-rootedness independent of the total-nonnegativity route; and it is strictly sufficient — it fails on CFL Example 9.5's `(1,7,5,1)` (correctly, that `h` is not real-rooted) and on `γ(A₁₅)` (which is real-rooted).

Negative controls for the total-nonnegativity layer: a random nonnegative bottom row usually destroys TN (45/60 at `r = 4`, 59/60 at `r = 5`; four explicit failures in Lean, two with their negative `2×2` minors exhibited), no single-entry `+1` perturbation does, the admissible window for two entries is pinned exactly on both sides, the resolvability identity fails when paired with the wrong deletion, different `k` give different Chow polynomials, and the alternation-certificate checker rejects a truncated, a mis-signed and a reversed certificate.

For every prime power `q ≥ 3` there is an explicit matroid whose Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomial is not unimodal and whose Chow polynomial equals that of a Bose–Burton geometry, hence is real-rooted: `k = 6`, `s = [6,2]_q − [6,1]_q + 1`, `S` a cap of size `base^t` in `AG(2t,q)`, `r = 7 + 2t` — tabulated for 17 prime powers, with both Cheng–Liu hypotheses, both cap inequalities, the strict local valley, and total nonnegativity of `R(L(B_{r,6}(q))*)` at `r = 21` (`q = 3`) and `r = 25` all decided in the kernel

The 21 rank-7 projective deletions `PG(6,2) ∖ (P(W) ⊔ S)` whose lattice of flats is not upper rank-uniform have real-rooted Chow polynomials, each with a sign-alternation certificate on 7 rational points

The rank-7 Cheng–Liu census: 26 projective deletions `PG(6,2) ∖ (P(W) ⊔ S)`, Chow polynomial computed from the actual lattice of up to 29 211 flats, each palindromic with `expand γ = H`, γ-positive, Kruskal–Katona-feasible, Newton- and Kurtz-passing; Cheng–Liu Proposition 2.6 reproduced on every row

Proposition A and A′ as computed instances: the Chow polynomial of a projective deletion sees only the flat spans of rank `≥ 2`, so `uH_M = uH_{B_{r,k}(q)}` on all 10 computed `δ ≡ 0` instances (`q = 2,3,5`, ranks 4, 5, 7) while `P_M` moves by `s·t`, and also on 3 `δ ≢ 0` instances where a partial line deletion mimics a full one; it fails on all 5 computed `δ ≢ 0` instances that do not, matching Lemma B's thresholds exactly

Negative controls: the sign-alternation certificate rejects a short list, a reversed list and a point moved into a region with no sign change; the γ-vectors are pinned by `expand` (a `±1` perturbation of either entry breaks it); Kurtz's criterion is sharp at `γ₃ = 19 851 141` against an actual `2 323 260`; the resolvability identity fails when paired with the wrong Whitney row at ranks 21 and 25; the unimodality predicate is non-vacuous on both sides

Proposition A, formalized over an arbitrary field: if the deleted set contains `P(W)`, is line-separated from `W` and has `delta == 0`, then a subspace of dimension `>= 2` is a flat span iff it is not contained in `W` — the same condition as for the Bose–Burton geometry — hence `uH_M = uH_{B_{r,k}(q)}` identically in `Z[X]`

Lemma B, formalized in both of its forms and both characteristics: over a field with at least 3 elements and `W ⊓ X = 0`, `S ⊆ X`, the Chow polynomial does not move — `uH_M = uH_{B_{r,k}(q)}` identically in `Z[X]` — either when `S` is a cap (no projective line carries three of its points), or, for `S` a cone inside an affine chart `X ∖ H` with `H` a hyperplane of `X`, when `S` contains no full affine line; both converses hold; and over `F_2` the lattices of flat spans differ already in rank 2 as soon as `k >= 1, s >= 1` or `k = 0, s >= 2`, so `delta != 0` always

Proposition A-prime, formalized: the chain sum defining the Chow polynomial is blind to flats of rank 1, so two projective deletions whose flat spans agree in every rank `>= 2` have equal Chow polynomials with no hypothesis on either; and the named instance — deleting all points of a projective line except one gives `uH = uH_{B_{r,2}(q)}` for every rank and every field, while `delta != 0`

The abstract chain sum is the family's Chow polynomial, in two characteristics: over the computed flat-span lattices of `PG(2,2)` and three of its deletions it reproduces the landed `bbChow 2 3 0 = 1+8t+t^2` and `bbChow 2 3 2 = 1+7t+t^2` at `t = 1,2,3`; over `PG(2,3)` and four of its deletions it reproduces `bbChow 3 3 0 = 1+14t+t^2` and `bbChow 3 3 2 = 1+13t+t^2`; and over the Boolean lattice of rank 3 the Eulerian polynomial `A_3`

Negative controls for the formalization layer: the weight hypothesis `w 1 = 0` is load-bearing (with `w m = m` the transfer fails, `95 != 86`); not all projective deletions share a Chow polynomial (`10` vs `9` at `t = 1`); agreement in rank `>= 2` is strictly weaker than equality of lattices; `delta != 0` is realized; and Proposition A's hypotheses are non-vacuous on both sides
Formalization cost of this pull, measured: 3 prose theorems became 8 Lean files, 2132 lines, 91 theorems, in about 3 h 40 min of wall time and 217 s of total kernel checking

families.paper_title: Flag $\gamma$-vectors that are not $f$-vectors, total nonnegativity for Bose--Burton geometries, and Chow polynomials of projective deletions
families.paper_abstract: For a matroid $M$ and a building set $\bG$ of its lattice of flats, the Chow polynomial $\bH(M,\bG)(t)$ is palindromic, and Coron, Ferroni and Li proved that its $\gamma$-vector is nonnegative when $(M,\bG)$ is flag, and is the $f$-vector of a simplicial complex when $(M,\bG)$ is complete.  They ask whether the $\gamma$-vector of a flag built matroid is the $f$-vector of a flag simplicial complex, and name ``satisfies the Kruskal--Katona inequalities'' as an intermediate step.  We answer both negatively: a flag, non-complete building set of $19$ flats on the uniform matroid $\U(7,8)$ has $\bH = 1+11t+37t^2+55t^3+37t^4+11t^5+t^6$ and $\gamma = (1,5,2,1)$, and no simplicial complex has two edges and one triangle.  Coloops give such examples in ranks $7$ through $11$, and lengthening four lines gives twelve of rank $7$ with unbounded ground set, eleven non-uniform. We then locate the failure: in the $k$-block family on $\U(2k-1,2k)$, of which the counterexample is the $k = 4$ member, the top Kruskal--Katona inequality fails at exactly one pair $(k,m)$, and the flag member with fewest edges is tight exactly for $5 \le k \le 8$, because Mantel's quadratic bound crosses the two linear Kruskal--Katona thresholds between $k = 4$ and $k = 9$.  In the second half we take the maximal building set and turn to real-rootedness.  We prove that the $(r+1) \times (r+1)$ matrix of Gaussian binomials whose bottom row is replaced by the Whitney numbers of the Bose--Burton geometry $B_{r,k}(q)$ --- the projective space $PG(r-1,q)$ with the points of a $k$-dimensional subspace deleted --- is totally nonnegative, for every $r$, every $0 \le k \le r-1$ and every real $q > 1$.  The proof exhibits the forced resolving array of Br\"and\'en and Saud-Maia-Leite in closed form, with manifestly positive coefficients.  Equivalently, the dual of the lattice of flats of every Bose--Burton geometry is a TN-poset, confirming for this family their conjecture that the dual of any upper combinatorially uniform geometric lattice is a TN-poset; and for $2 \le k \le r-2$ these lattices are neither perfect matroid designs, nor supersolvable, nor paving, so they lie outside the classes named alongside that conjecture.  With a theorem of Br\"and\'en and Vecchi it follows that the Chow polynomial and the augmented Chow polynomial of $B_{r,k}(q)$ are real-rooted --- instances of a conjecture of Ferroni--Schr\"oter and Huh--Stevens which, for $2 \le k \le r-2$, no published sufficient condition we could find reaches, apart from the Chow polynomials in rank at most six.  The third part perturbs the geometry.  Cheng and Liu have recently refuted unimodality of matroid Kazhdan--Lusztig polynomials by deleting from a Bose--Burton geometry a further point set $S$ that is line-separated from $W$.  We show that the chain sum defining the Chow polynomial never reads a flat of rank~$1$, so that the Chow polynomial of a projective deletion depends on the deleted set only through the flat spans of dimension at least~$2$; that the Cheng--Liu perturbation is therefore invisible to the Chow polynomial as soon as every projective line outside $W$ retains two surviving points; and that over a field with at least three elements a cap has that property, while over $\mathbb{F}_2$ it fails as soon as $W \neq 0$ and one further point is deleted, or two points of a chart are. Consequently, for every prime power $q \ge 3$ there is an explicit matroid whose Kazhdan--Lusztig polynomial is not unimodal and whose Chow polynomial is that of a Bose--Burton geometry, hence real-rooted: the Cheng--Liu refutation does not transfer.  On the other side of that dichotomy we compute a census of $26$ rank-$7$ deletions of $PG(6,2)$ from their lattices of up to $29\,211$ flats; the $21$ whose lattice of flats is not upper rank uniform lie outside every published sufficient condition we could find, and all $21$ Chow polynomials are real-rooted.  The coefficient data is computed from the Feichtner--Yuzvinsky formula, from the second part on inside the proof assistant itself; every arithmetic assertion is machine-checked in Lean~4, and the transfer theorems of the third part are formalised there over an arbitrary field.

families.paper_title: The minimal degree of a polynomial identity of all Matsuo algebras is at least six
families.paper_abstract: Matsuo algebras are the commutative non-associative algebras attached to groups of $3$-transpositions; they are the axial algebras of Jordan type that come from a group, and for $\eta \ne \tfrac12$ every algebra of Jordan type $\eta$ is one of them or a quotient of one.  A recent survey of Gorshkov and Shpectorov records a problem of Rowen: do all Matsuo algebras satisfy identities not implied by commutativity, and if they do, what is the minimal degree of such an identity?  The survey states the published lower bound as $4$, attributing it to a proposition of Chayet and Garibaldi through work of Osborn.  We raise the bound to $6$.  The proof rests on a single small algebra: the six-dimensional Matsuo algebra $\Mat{2}{S_4}$ over $\QQ$, built from the six transpositions of $S_4$ with $\eta = 2$, whose space of multilinear identities is \emph{zero} in degrees $3$, $4$ and $5$.  The degree-$5$ statement is certified by an explicit $105 \times 105$ integer block of the evaluation matrix together with an explicit inverse of that block modulo $101$.  We also verify that $\Mat{2}{S_4}$ is unital with $1 = \tfrac15 \sum_{a \in D} a$, that the Frobenius form printed in the survey is associative on it with Gram determinant $5$, and that it is not a Jordan algebra --- exactly the hypotheses under which the published proposition applies, so that the bound the published literature really gives is $5$ and the theorem below is one degree past it.  A rank computation carried out outside the formal development gives degree $6$ as well, which would raise the bound to $7$; that computation is labelled as such wherever it appears and is not machine-checked.  Everything else is machine-checked in Lean~4.
